description: Tiered GH component knowledge - token-aware density layers

input_providers._description: Components that generate test data for each input type. Used by gh_explore_deep for automatic wiring.

vector.notes: Unit Z vector with factor slider

dabc854d-f50e-408a-b001-d043c7de151d.name: Sphere
dabc854d-f50e-408a-b001-d043c7de151d.quick: Creates a spherical NURBS surface from a base plane and radius | outputs single Surface (not solid brep) | Smoke test gotcha — verify write path works in rel

contexts.basic_sphere: Connect a Plane (or use default World XY) to B and a Number to R; outputs S as a NURBS surface. Use Plane Origin or Construct Plane to position sphere center.
contexts.solid_operations: For boolean ops needing a closed brep, Cap Holes or use Quad Sphere (361790d6) instead — this component outputs a surface, not a solid.
contexts.array_of_spheres: Wire a list of planes to B and matching radii to R; Grasshopper auto-matches or uses longest-list to generate multiple spheres.

dabc854d-f50e-408a-b001-d043c7de151d.errors: Null output if R is zero or negative. If downstream ops expect a Brep/solid, surface may fail — cap or convert. Plane input defaults to World XY if omitted.

working_configs.description: Default sphere with plane and radius

gotchas.text: Smoke test gotcha — verify write path works in release mode overlay

0373008a-80ee-45be-887d-ab5a244afc29.name: Cylinder
0373008a-80ee-45be-887d-ab5a244afc29.quick: Creates cylindrical surface from base plane, radius, and length | outputs open surface, not closed solid

contexts.basic_cylinder: Connect Plane to B (origin+orientation), Number to R (radius) and L (length/height); outputs Surface C — use Cap Holes or similar to close ends into a brep solid
contexts.oriented_cylinder: Feed a constructed Plane (e.g., from XY Plane or Plane Normal) to B to control cylinder axis direction; R and L accept numeric sliders for parametric sizing
contexts.boolean_operations: Output Surface C typically needs to be converted to closed Brep before use in boolean ops — cap or join with flat end surfaces first

0373008a-80ee-45be-887d-ab5a244afc29.errors: <~30 tokens: Negative or zero R/L causes invalid geometry; output is open surface — boolean ops fail without capping ends first>

2a43ef96-8f87-4892-8b94-237a47e8d3cf.name: Box 2Pt
2a43ef96-8f87-4892-8b94-237a47e8d3cf.quick: Creates a box from two corner points and an orientation plane | Plane P controls axis alignment
2a43ef96-8f87-4892-8b94-237a47e8d3cf.description: Create a box defined by two points.

contexts.bounding_box: Wire two diagonal corner Points to A and B; supply a Plane for orientation (e.g., World XY). Outputs a Box primitive usable with Boolean or Brep operations.
contexts.oriented_box: Connect a custom Plane to P to align box axes to a non-world orientation; A and B define extents along that plane's axes.
contexts.geometry_containment: Pair with Bounding Box output points or manually defined Points to wrap geometry in a fitted box volume.

2a43ef96-8f87-4892-8b94-237a47e8d3cf.errors: If A and B are coincident or coplanar relative to P, box has zero volume and fails. Missing Plane defaults to World XY; mismatched plane orientation can produce unexpected box skew.

28061aae-04fb-4cb5-ac45-16f3b66bc0a4.name: Center Box
28061aae-04fb-4cb5-ac45-16f3b66bc0a4.quick: Creates a box centered on a plane with X/Y/Z dimensions | box is symmetric about the base plane origin
28061aae-04fb-4cb5-ac45-16f3b66bc0a4.description: Create a box centered on a plane.

contexts.basic_box_creation: Connect a Plane (e.g., XY Plane) to B; wire Number sliders to X, Y, Z for width/depth/height. Box is centered on plane, so half-dimensions extend each side.
contexts.replacing_domain_box: Use instead of Domain Box when you want simple numeric dimensions rather than domain intervals. Simpler wiring for symmetric boxes around a known plane.
contexts.positioning: Feed a Construction Plane or oriented Plane to B to align box to custom orientation. X/Y/Z remain relative to that plane's axes.

28061aae-04fb-4cb5-ac45-16f3b66bc0a4.errors: <~30 tokens: Null output if Plane input is missing or invalid. Zero/negative X, Y, or Z values produce degenerate or invalid Box geometry.

57da07bd-ecab-415d-9d86-af36d7073abc.name: Number Slider
57da07bd-ecab-415d-9d86-af36d7073abc.quick: Interactive numeric input slider; outputs a single number value | set min, max, and precision via right-click

contexts.numeric_input: Double-click to set range/precision; wire output directly to numeric inputs like Construct Point XYZ coords or any component expecting a number
contexts.parameter_control: Use multiple sliders to drive geometry parameters; right-click to rename for clarity in complex definitions
contexts.integer_mode: Right-click > Type to switch between float/integer/odd/even modes for discrete control

57da07bd-ecab-415d-9d86-af36d7073abc.errors: No direct errors; mismatched type (e.g., float slider into integer-only input) may cause silent rounding; range limits block out-of-bounds values

59e0b89a-e487-49f8-bab8-b5bab16be14c.name: Panel
59e0b89a-e487-49f8-bab8-b5bab16be14c.quick: Text/data display and input panel | Can hold static text, numbers, or multiline strings passed as output

contexts.static_text_input: Type text directly into panel; wire output to string-expecting inputs like annotation, path, or expression components
contexts.data_inspection: Connect any wire to panel to preview values; acts as a live readout of geometry, numbers, or lists
contexts.multiline_string: Enable multiline mode (right-click) to input multiple strings as a list; each line becomes a separate item

59e0b89a-e487-49f8-bab8-b5bab16be14c.errors: Panel output is always a string type; downstream components expecting numbers or geometry may fail without explicit conversion

2e78987b-9dfb-42a2-8b76-3923ac8bd91a.name: Boolean Toggle
2e78987b-9dfb-42a2-8b76-3923ac8bd91a.quick: Outputs a single True/False boolean value; double-click to toggle state

contexts.conditional_control: Wire output to boolean inputs (e.g., Cull, Dispatch, Gate) to switch logic on/off; no inputs required, just double-click component to flip True/False
contexts.parameter_switching: Use alongside Value List or Slider to conditionally activate branches; connect to components expecting boolean flags to enable/disable operations

2e78987b-9dfb-42a2-8b76-3923ac8bd91a.errors: No computation errors possible; downstream failures occur if connected input expects non-boolean type or if toggle state is unintentionally left at wrong value causing silent logic errors

4c4e56eb-2f04-43f9-95a3-cc46a14f495a.name: Line
4c4e56eb-2f04-43f9-95a3-cc46a14f495a.quick: Line | Inputs: Start Point, End Point → Line

962034e9-cc27-4394-afc4-5c16e3447cf9.name: Extrude
962034e9-cc27-4394-afc4-5c16e3447cf9.quick: Extrudes points/curves/surfaces along a vector (B=geometry, D=direction vector) → outputs extruded geometry
962034e9-cc27-4394-afc4-5c16e3447cf9.description: Extrude points, curves and surfaces along a vector.

contexts.curve_to_surface: Connect a curve to B and Unit Z (or custom vector) to D; outputs a ruled surface. Common pattern: closed curve → Extrude → cap ends with Boundary Surfaces for a solid.
contexts.surface_to_brep: Feed a planar surface into B with a Z vector to D to create an open box/wall geometry. Pair with Boundary Surfaces to cap.
contexts.point_to_line: Extruding a point along a vector produces a line segment, useful for quick geometry construction before Loft.

962034e9-cc27-4394-afc4-5c16e3447cf9.errors: Fails silently or outputs null if D vector has zero length. Non-planar surfaces may produce unexpected open Breps. Unlike Extrude Along, D must be a straight vector — curves as direction won't work.

75164624-395a-4d24-b60b-6bf91cab0194.name: Sweep2
75164624-395a-4d24-b60b-6bf91cab0194.quick: Sweeps profile curve(s) along two rail curves to create a Brep surface | Rails and sections must be compatible curves
75164624-395a-4d24-b60b-6bf91cab0194.description: Create a sweep surface with two rail curves.

contexts.basic_two_rail_sweep: Connect two guide curves to R¹ and R² inputs, one or more cross-section curves to S; H (Boolean) controls closed/open sweep; outputs single Brep surface
contexts.multiple_sections: Multiple section curves can be provided to S input as a list; sections should intersect or align with both rails for clean geometry
contexts.closed_sweep: Set H to True to create a closed (looping) sweep when rails form a closed loop; False for open sweep

75164624-395a-4d24-b60b-6bf91cab0194.errors: Fails if rails and section curves don't share endpoints or intersect properly; mismatched curve directions between R¹ and R² cause twisted surfaces; open sections on closed rails may produce unexpected results

e64c5fb1-845c-4ab1-8911-5f338516ba67.name: Series
e64c5fb1-845c-4ab1-8911-5f338516ba67.quick: Series | Inputs: Start, Step, Count → Series

87e1d9ef-088b-4d30-9dda-8a7448a17329.name: Graft Tree
87e1d9ef-088b-4d30-9dda-8a7448a17329.description: Graft a data tree by adding an extra branch for every item.

f80cfe18-9510-4b89-8301-8e58faf423bb.name: Flatten Tree
f80cfe18-9510-4b89-8301-8e58faf423bb.quick: Collapses all branches into single {0} path; P input sets target path (default {0})
f80cfe18-9510-4b89-8301-8e58faf423bb.description: Flatten a data tree by removing all branching information.

contexts.collapse_for_operations: Wire any multi-branch tree into T; output is single branch {0} with all items in original order. Use before operations requiring flat lists.
contexts.custom_target_path: Supply a path to P to flatten into a specific path instead of default {0}. Rarely needed but useful for downstream path matching.
contexts.pre_processing: Commonly placed after Graft Tree or complex tree-generating components to reset structure before feeding into components expecting simple lists.

f80cfe18-9510-4b89-8301-8e58faf423bb.errors: Flattening loses all branch structure permanently — downstream components relying on branch grouping will misalign. P input expects a valid path type; wrong type causes null output.

47886835-e3ff-4516-a3ed-1b419f055464.name: Circle 3Pt
47886835-e3ff-4516-a3ed-1b419f055464.quick: Creates circle through 3 points; outputs circle geometry, plane, and radius | points must be non-collinear
47886835-e3ff-4516-a3ed-1b419f055464.description: Create a circle defined by three points.

contexts.geometry_from_points: Wire three Point params to A, B, C; outputs Circle (C), fit plane (P), and computed radius (R). Common after sampling surface points or extracting vertices.
contexts.reverse_engineering_radius: Use R output to measure circumradius of triangles; pair with Arc 3Pt when only partial arc is needed instead of full circle.
contexts.plane_extraction: P output gives the circle's plane for downstream Orient or Transform ops; useful when plane orientation from 3 picked points is needed.

47886835-e3ff-4516-a3ed-1b419f055464.errors: Fails or returns invalid circle if A, B, C are collinear (no unique circle exists); duplicate points also cause failure. Ensure all three points are distinct and non-collinear.

1a38d325-98de-455c-93f1-bca431bc1243.name: Offset Curve
1a38d325-98de-455c-93f1-bca431bc1243.quick: Offsets a curve by distance D in plane P | Plane input is required to define offset direction for non-planar or ambiguous curves
1a38d325-98de-455c-93f1-bca431bc1243.description: Offset a curve with a specified distance.

contexts.2d_offset: Wire a planar curve to C, a Number slider to D, and an XY/reference Plane to P; outputs offset curve parallel to input at given distance
contexts.variable_offset: Connect expression or parameter-driven Number to D for dynamic offset distances; useful for wall thickness, setbacks, or buffer zones
contexts.3d_curve_offset: P plane guides offset direction for 3D curves; without correct plane, offset may produce unexpected geometry or fail

1a38d325-98de-455c-93f1-bca431bc1243.errors: Fails or returns null if C input receives non-curve geometry (typed as Integer in JSON — likely a mislabel); missing or misaligned Plane P causes offset direction errors or no solution

03e331ed-c4d1-4a23-afa2-f57b87d2043c.name: Cone
03e331ed-c4d1-4a23-afa2-f57b87d2043c.quick: Creates conical surface from base Plane, Radius (R), and Length (L); outputs Surface (C) and tip Point (T)

contexts.basic_cone: Wire a Plane to B for cone base orientation/position, a Number to R for base radius, a Number to L for cone height/length. C outputs the conical surface, T outputs the apex point for further geometry use.
contexts.tip_point_usage: T (apex Point) can be wired to downstream components like Line, Vector, or other geometry ops to reference the cone tip without extra calculation.
contexts.orientation_control: Use Plane component or XY/YZ/XZ Plane to control cone axis direction. Default world XY plane places cone upright along Z-axis.

03e331ed-c4d1-4a23-afa2-f57b87d2043c.errors: Negative or zero R/L values likely produce invalid or null surface. Mismatched units between R and L may produce unexpected proportions. Non-planar input to B will cause type error.

361790d6-9d66-4808-8c5a-8de9c218c227.name: Quad Sphere
361790d6-9d66-4808-8c5a-8de9c218c227.quick: Creates spherical Brep from quad NURBS patches | B=base plane, R=radius; outputs multi-patch Brep not single surface
361790d6-9d66-4808-8c5a-8de9c218c227.description: Create a spherical brep made from quad nurbs patches.

contexts.basic_sphere_creation: Connect a Plane (or use World XY) to B and a Number to R; outputs a Brep composed of quad NURBS patches, unlike the standard Sphere component which outputs a single surface
contexts.subdivision_workflows: Preferred over standard Sphere when downstream operations require quad topology; wire S into Brep components or mesh converters that benefit from structured quad patch layout
contexts.comparison_with_sphere: Use Quad Sphere instead of Sphere when pole singularities cause issues; quad patch structure avoids degenerate edges at poles, useful for paneling or UV-sensitive operations

361790d6-9d66-4808-8c5a-8de9c218c227.errors: Negative or zero R will likely fail or produce degenerate geometry; B must be a valid Plane — null plane input causes no output; output is a Brep not a Surface, so Surface-only inputs downstream will error

0bb3d234-9097-45db-9998-621639c87d3b.name: Bounding Box
0bb3d234-9097-45db-9998-621639c87d3b.quick: Bounding Box | Inputs: Content, Plane → Box

4c619bc9-39fd-4717-82a6-1e07ea237bbe.name: Line SDL
4c619bc9-39fd-4717-82a6-1e07ea237bbe.quick: Line SDL | Inputs: Start, Direction, Length → Line

a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.name: Loft
a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.quick: Creates lofted Brep through section curves (C); curve order and direction matter critically for clean results.
a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.description: Create a lofted surface through a set of section curves.

contexts.basic_loft: Connect list of curves to C; curves must be ordered sequentially. Loft Options (O) controls type (Normal, Loose, Tight, Straight), closed loft, and rebuild settings.
contexts.closed_loft: Set Loft Options to Closed=true to connect last section back to first. All curves should have consistent seam points to avoid twisting.
contexts.variable_sections: Feed profile curves at different elevations or positions; pair with Divide Curve or explicit planes to generate evenly spaced sections before lofting.
contexts.network_vs_loft: Use Loft for ordered rail-free sections; use Network Surface (neighbor) when you have crossing curve grids; use Sweep2 when two rails guide the surface.

a7a41d0a-2188-4f7a-82cc-1a2c4e4ec850.errors: Twisted/self-intersecting surface: mismatched curve directions or seam points. Null output: fewer than 2 curves supplied, or non-compatible curve types in list.

46b5564d-d3eb-4bf1-ae16-15ed132cfd88.name: Ellipse
46b5564d-d3eb-4bf1-ae16-15ed132cfd88.quick: Creates ellipse from plane + two radii | Plane sets center/orientation; R1/R2 are semi-axes
46b5564d-d3eb-4bf1-ae16-15ed132cfd88.description: Create an ellipse defined by base plane and two radii.

contexts.basic_ellipse: Connect XY Plane (or constructed Plane) to P, two Number sliders to R1 and R2; outputs closed Curve E plus focal points F1, F2
contexts.oriented_ellipse: Use Plane component or Plane Normal to orient ellipse in 3D space; R1 and R2 control major/minor axis lengths respectively
contexts.extracting_foci: F1 and F2 outputs give focal points directly — useful for geometric constructions without manual calculation

46b5564d-d3eb-4bf1-ae16-15ed132cfd88.errors: Fails or produces degenerate result if R1 or R2 is zero or negative; equal R1/R2 produces a circle; null/invalid Plane input causes no output

845527a6-5cea-4ae9-a667-96ae1667a4e8.name: Polygon
845527a6-5cea-4ae9-a667-96ae1667a4e8.quick: Creates regular polygon on a plane with given radius and side count; optional fillet radius rounds corners.
845527a6-5cea-4ae9-a667-96ae1667a4e8.description: Create a polygon with optional round edges.

contexts.basic_polygon: Wire a Plane (P), Number for radius (R), and Integer for sides (S, e.g. 6 for hexagon) → outputs closed Curve (P) and side length (L). Rf=0 gives sharp corners.
contexts.rounded_polygon: Set Rf (fillet radius) > 0 to round corners; Rf must be smaller than the inscribed circle radius or geometry fails. Useful for slot/panel shapes.
contexts.array_patterns: Combine with Plane from point/normal inputs and Series/Range for R or S to generate grids of polygons for paneling or tiling workflows.

845527a6-5cea-4ae9-a667-96ae1667a4e8.errors: S must be integer ≥ 3; S<3 causes no output. Rf too large relative to R causes invalid fillet geometry. Non-planar or null Plane input breaks output.

9d2583dd-6cf5-497c-8c40-c9a290598396.name: Arc SED
9d2583dd-6cf5-497c-8c40-c9a290598396.quick: Creates arc from start point, end point, and tangent direction vector at start | tangent vector D must be non-zero and not parallel to SE line
9d2583dd-6cf5-497c-8c40-c9a290598396.description: Create an arc defined by start point, end point and a tangent vector.

contexts.arc_from_endpoints_with_direction: Wire two Points to S and E, a Vector (e.g., from Unit Vector or line tangent) to D; outputs arc geometry A, construction plane P, and radius R. Useful when you know endpoint positions and desired departure angle.
contexts.chaining_curves: Use arc endpoint and tangent from a prior curve segment to feed S and D, ensuring G1 continuity. Combine output A with other curves in Join Curves for smooth polycurves.
contexts.extracting_arc_properties: Output R (radius) feeds downstream scaling or offset operations; output P (plane) can drive oriented geometry placement along the arc.

9d2583dd-6cf5-497c-8c40-c9a290598396.errors: <~30 tokens: Arc fails if S equals E (zero-length), if D is a zero vector, or if D is exactly parallel to the SE direction (collinear — no unique arc exists).

75f4b0fd-9721-47b1-99e7-9c098b342e67.name: BiArc
75f4b0fd-9721-47b1-99e7-9c098b342e67.quick: Creates two joined arcs (bi-arc) matching endpoint positions and tangent directions | R parameter controls junction point ratio
75f4b0fd-9721-47b1-99e7-9c098b342e67.description: Create a bi-arc based on endpoints and tangents.

contexts.smooth_curve_fitting: Wire two Points (S, E) and two Vectors (Ts, Te) for tangent-continuous curve; outputs A1+A2 as individual arcs and B as joined curve; R~0.5 for symmetric split
contexts.tangent_matching: Use alongside Arc SED or Evaluate Curve to extract tangent vectors at endpoints; ensures G1 continuity between adjacent segments
contexts.fabrication_paths: B output provides single Curve for downstream use; A1/A2 allow per-arc radius inspection or further manipulation

75f4b0fd-9721-47b1-99e7-9c098b342e67.errors: <~30 tokens: Fails if S==E (zero-length), or if Ts/Te are zero vectors; degenerate geometry if tangents are anti-parallel at certain R values

4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.name: Scale
4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.quick: Uniformly scales geometry from a center point by factor F | F=1 = no change, F=0 collapses to point
4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.description: Scale an object uniformly in all directions.

contexts.resize_geometry: Connect any geometry to G, a Point for center C, and a Number for scale factor F. Outputs scaled geometry and reusable Transform X.
contexts.reuse_transform: Output X (Transform) can be fed into Transform component to apply same scale to other geometry without recomputing.
contexts.scale_from_origin: Use a Point component set to 0,0,0 as C to scale from world origin; common when geometry is already centered.

4d2a06bd-4b0f-4c65-9ee0-4220e4c01703.errors: <~30 tokens: F=0 collapses geometry to a point; null C defaults may cause unexpected center; use Scale NU for non-uniform axes.

b7798b74-037e-4f0c-8ac7-dc1043d093e0.name: Rotate
b7798b74-037e-4f0c-8ac7-dc1043d093e0.quick: Rotate | Inputs: Geometry, Angle, Plane → Geometry

f12daa2f-4fd5-48c1-8ac3-5dea476912ca.name: Mirror
f12daa2f-4fd5-48c1-8ac3-5dea476912ca.quick: Mirrors geometry across a plane | Plane input defines mirror plane; outputs mirrored geometry and transform matrix

contexts.basic_mirroring: Connect any geometry to G, provide a Plane (e.g., XY, YZ, or custom) to P; outputs mirrored copy. Use XZ/YZ world planes for standard axis mirroring.
contexts.transform_reuse: X output provides the mirror Transform matrix; feed into Transform component to apply same mirror to other geometry without re-specifying the plane.
contexts.symmetry_modeling: Combine original and mirrored geometry via Merge or Brep Join after mirroring to create symmetric forms. Pair with Orient or Rotate Axis for complex symmetry setups.

f12daa2f-4fd5-48c1-8ac3-5dea476912ca.errors: Wrong plane orientation produces unexpected mirror direction. Null or missing Plane input causes component failure. Non-planar or invalid geometry in G may produce null output.

2f407944-81c3-4062-a485-276454ec4b8c.name: Fillet
2f407944-81c3-4062-a485-276454ec4b8c.quick: Rounds sharp corners of a curve using radius R | R must be small enough to fit between corners
2f407944-81c3-4062-a485-276454ec4b8c.description: Fillet the sharp corners of a curve.

contexts.rounding_polyline_corners: Connect a polyline or polygon to C, set R as a number; outputs smoothed curve with arc fillets at each sharp corner
contexts.pre_offset_smoothing: Apply Fillet before Offset Curve to avoid offset failures at sharp corners; R should be less than offset distance
contexts.design_cleanup: Use after Simplify Curve to round remaining sharp vertices; chain output C into further curve operations

2f407944-81c3-4062-a485-276454ec4b8c.errors: <~30 tokens: Fillet fails if R is too large for corner spacing; smooth/tangent curves with no sharp corners produce no change or null output>

8073a420-6bec-49e3-9b18-367f6fd76ac3.name: Join Curves
8073a420-6bec-49e3-9b18-367f6fd76ac3.quick: Join Curves | Inputs: Curves, Preserve → Curves

2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.name: Divide Curve
2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.quick: Divides curve into N equal segments | N is count of segments (produces N+1 points); K keeps end point
2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.description: Divide a curve into equal length segments

contexts.point_array_generation: Wire Curve to C, integer slider to N; outputs P (points along curve), T (tangent vectors), t (parameters). Common pattern: feed P into downstream geometry operations.
contexts.tangent_frames: Use T output alongside P to orient objects along curve; T gives unit tangent vector at each division point. Pair with Orient or Plane components.
contexts.parameter_extraction: t output gives normalized or curve parameters at each division point; useful for evaluating other data at same locations via Evaluate Curve.

2162e72e-72fc-4bf8-9459-d4d82fa8aa14.errors: N=0 or negative causes no output; N must be integer ≥1. Null/invalid curve on C produces no points. K (knot) boolean affects whether curve knots are preserved as extra points, changing output count unexpectedly.

1e531c08-9c80-46d6-8850-1b50d1dae69f.name: Divide Distance
1e531c08-9c80-46d6-8850-1b50d1dae69f.quick: Divides curve into points spaced D units apart | D is absolute distance, not count
1e531c08-9c80-46d6-8850-1b50d1dae69f.description: Divide a curve with a preset distance between points

contexts.point_sampling: Wire Curve to C, Number (distance value) to D; outputs evenly spaced Points P, tangent Vectors T, and parameters t along curve. Last segment may be shorter than D.
contexts.downstream_geometry: P points feed into geometry placement; t parameters feed into Shatter or Curve Frames for further curve subdivision at those locations.
contexts.variable_spacing: Use a single Number or slider for D to control spacing globally; unlike Divide Curve, no segment count needed — spacing is metric/unit-based.

1e531c08-9c80-46d6-8850-1b50d1dae69f.errors: If D is larger than curve length, may return only start/end points or fail to divide. Zero or negative D causes invalid output. Curve must be valid and non-degenerate.

922dc7e5-0f0e-4c21-ae4b-f6a8654e63f6.name: Simplify Curve
922dc7e5-0f0e-4c21-ae4b-f6a8654e63f6.quick: Reduces curve complexity by removing redundant control points | 't' = tolerance, 'a' = angle tolerance; output 'S' indicates if simplification occurred

contexts.reducing_control_points: Wire a complex NURBS or polyline curve into C; set t (distance tolerance) and a (angle tolerance) as Number sliders; output C is simplified curve, S (Boolean) confirms if curve was actually changed
contexts.pre_processing_for_offset_fillet: Use before Offset Curve or Fillet to reduce unnecessary knots/segments, improving downstream operation reliability; connect simplified C output directly to those components
contexts.cleaning_imported_geometry: Apply after Project Curve or Pull Curve to clean up over-tessellated results; tight tolerances (small t) preserve shape while removing redundant points

922dc7e5-0f0e-4c21-ae4b-f6a8654e63f6.errors: S returns False if curve is already minimal — no error but no change occurs. Overly large 't' tolerance may over-simplify, distorting curve shape. Null or non-simplifiable curves (e.g., lines, circles) may pass through unchanged.

2ad2a4d4-3de1-42f6-a4b8-f71835f35710.name: Shatter
2ad2a4d4-3de1-42f6-a4b8-f71835f35710.quick: Splits a curve at parameter values t into segments | t must be curve domain parameters, not normalized 0-1 values

contexts.splitting_at_points: Reparameterize curve or use Curve Closest Point to get t values; feed multiple t numbers as list; outputs list of curve segments between split points
contexts.combining_with_division: Use Divide Curve or Divide Distance to generate t parameters, then feed into Shatter to get actual segment curves rather than just points
contexts.selective_segment_extraction: Use List Item on S output to isolate specific segments after shattering; useful for trimming or rebuilding partial curves

2ad2a4d4-3de1-42f6-a4b8-f71835f35710.errors: No output segments if t values are outside curve domain; single segment returned if t list has one value at endpoint; duplicate or unsorted t values may produce zero-length segments

b25c5762-f90e-4839-9fc5-74b74ab42b1e.name: Offset Surface
b25c5762-f90e-4839-9fc5-74b74ab42b1e.quick: Offsets a surface by distance D; T toggles solid/open result | negative D offsets inward
b25c5762-f90e-4839-9fc5-74b74ab42b1e.description: Offset a surface by a fixed amount.

contexts.thickening_shell: Connect surface to S, numeric slider to D for thickness; set T=True to cap into solid Brep; use Cap Holes if gaps remain
contexts.inward_offset: Negative D value offsets surface toward its normal flip side; pair with Reverse Surface if offset direction is wrong
contexts.parametric_spacing: Chain multiple Offset Surface components with incremental D values to create concentric surface layers; feed results into Isotrim for trimmed subsets

b25c5762-f90e-4839-9fc5-74b74ab42b1e.errors: <~30 tokens: Non-manifold or self-intersecting surfaces fail at large D values; open surfaces with T=True may produce incomplete solids requiring Cap Holes

b648d933-ddea-4e75-834c-8f6f3793e311.name: Cap Holes
b648d933-ddea-4e75-834c-8f6f3793e311.quick: Caps all planar holes in a Brep | only works on planar holes; non-planar openings remain open
b648d933-ddea-4e75-834c-8f6f3793e311.description: Cap all planar holes in a Brep.

contexts.closing_open_breps: Wire an open Brep (e.g., from Brep Join or Loft) into B; outputs a closed solid Brep if all holes are planar. Often used before boolean or volume operations.
contexts.post_offset_cleanup: After Offset Surface creates open edges, Cap Holes closes flat ends. Pair with Offset Surface → Cap Holes to produce closed solids.
contexts.fillet_prep: Use before or after Fillet Edge to ensure the Brep is solid; non-planar holes will not be capped and may cause downstream failures.

b648d933-ddea-4e75-834c-8f6f3793e311.errors: Fails silently (returns uncapped Brep) when holes are non-planar. Null output if input Brep is invalid or null. No effect if Brep is already closed.

bb6666e7-d0f4-41ec-a257-df2371619f13.name: Sweep1
bb6666e7-d0f4-41ec-a257-df2371619f13.quick: Sweeps profile curve(s) along one rail curve → Brep | M (miter) must be 0, 1, or 2; values ≥3 trigger 'Invalid miter type' warning
bb6666e7-d0f4-41ec-a257-df2371619f13.description: Create a sweep surface with one rail curve.

contexts.basic_sweep: Connect a rail curve to R and one or more profile curves to S; leave M=0 (None) for simple sweeps. Output is a Brep surface.
contexts.miter_control: Set M integer to 0=None, 1=Trimmed, or 2=Rotated to control how corners are handled at kinks in the rail. Use a Panel or integer slider clamped 0–2.
contexts.multiple_profiles: S accepts multiple cross-section curves; Sweep1 interpolates between them along the rail, useful for variable-section forms.

bb6666e7-d0f4-41ec-a257-df2371619f13.errors: M ≥ 3 triggers 'Invalid miter type' warning and may produce no output. Rail or profile curves that don't intersect/align can produce degenerate or null Brep.

adeadd58-4e28-46ed-853a-b590507d892e.name: Pipe
adeadd58-4e28-46ed-853a-b590507d892e.quick: Creates pipe (Brep) around a rail curve | E cap type must be 0 (open), 1 (flat), or 2 (round) — values >2 error
adeadd58-4e28-46ed-853a-b590507d892e.description: Create a pipe surface around a rail curve.

contexts.basic_pipe: Wire a Curve to C, a Number to R (radius), Integer 0/1/2 to E (cap type), Boolean to Fr (fit rail). Outputs closed Brep pipe surface.
contexts.open_pipe: Set E=0 for no caps (open tube). Useful when pipe ends will be joined to other geometry. R drives uniform radius along full curve.
contexts.capped_pipe: E=1 gives flat planar caps; E=2 gives round hemispherical caps. Use Fr=True to fit pipe to rail curve more closely.
contexts.variable_radius: For varying radius along curve, use Pipe Variable neighbor instead — Pipe only supports single uniform R value.

adeadd58-4e28-46ed-853a-b590507d892e.errors: <E must be exactly 0, 1, or 2; any other integer triggers 'Invalid cap type' error. Degenerate or zero-length curves will likely fail to produce Brep output.

fab11c30-2d9c-4d15-ab3c-2289f1ae5c21.name: Solid Difference
fab11c30-2d9c-4d15-ab3c-2289f1ae5c21.quick: Subtracts B Breps from A Breps; both must be closed/valid solids or operation fails silently.
fab11c30-2d9c-4d15-ab3c-2289f1ae5c21.description: Perform a solid difference on two Brep sets.

contexts.boolean_subtraction: Wire closed Brep geometry to A (base solid) and B (cutter solid); outputs trimmed Brep. Pair with Solid Union to recombine results. B must fully or partially overlap A.
contexts.cutting_voids: Use instead of Trim Solid when cutter is a full solid volume; Trim Solid is better for open surface cutters. Ensure both A and B are watertight Breps.
contexts.multiple_cutters: B accepts multiple Breps (list); all are subtracted from A simultaneously. Flatten or graft inputs to control per-item vs. combined operations.

fab11c30-2d9c-4d15-ab3c-2289f1ae5c21.errors: Fails or returns null if A or B are open/non-manifold Breps. No overlap between A and B returns A unchanged. Degenerate geometry or self-intersecting Breps cause silent failures.

cdee962f-4202-456b-a1b4-f3ed9aa0dc29.name: Revolution
cdee962f-4202-456b-a1b4-f3ed9aa0dc29.quick: Revolves a curve (P) around an axis line (A) within an angular domain (D) to produce a Brep surface.

contexts.full_revolution: Connect a profile curve to P, a Line as axis to A, and a Domain of 0 to 2π (or 0 to 360°) to D; outputs closed Brep surface of revolution.
contexts.partial_revolution: Supply a restricted Domain (e.g., 0 to π) to D to create a partial surface; useful for half-shells or arcs of revolution.
contexts.lathe_style_modeling: Pair with a polyline or NURBS profile curve from Interpolate Curve; axis Line typically defined by Line component or two points on the profile's symmetry axis.

cdee962f-4202-456b-a1b4-f3ed9aa0dc29.errors: Null output if axis Line (A) is invalid or zero-length; degenerate Brep if profile curve passes through or crosses the axis; Domain (D) must be in radians — degree values produce unexpected partial surfaces.

3581f42a-9592-4549-bd6b-1c0fc39d067b.name: Construct Point
3581f42a-9592-4549-bd6b-1c0fc39d067b.quick: Construct Point | Inputs: X coordinate, Y coordinate, Z coordinate → Point

7f6a9d34-0470-4bb7-aadd-07496bcbe572.name: Point On Curve
7f6a9d34-0470-4bb7-aadd-07496bcbe572.quick: Point On Curve | Inputs: no inputs → output

fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.name: Evaluate Curve
fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.quick: Evaluates curve at parameter t → Point, Tangent vector, curvature Angle | t must be in curve domain (use Remap or Domain component)
fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.description: Evaluate a curve at the specified parameter.

contexts.point_sampling: Connect Curve to C, feed normalized or domain-mapped Number to t; outputs Point P for geometry placement. Use Range/Series for multiple sample points along curve.
contexts.tangent_extraction: Wire t from a slider or divide output; T gives tangent vector at that parameter — useful for orienting objects along curve with Plane from vector.
contexts.curvature_analysis: A output gives curvature angle; combine with Curve Frame neighbor for full frame. Useful for detecting bends or variable-radius paths.

fc6979e4-7e91-4508-8e05-37c680779751.errors: Wrong domain: t outside curve's actual parameter domain returns null P/T. Use Curve Domain + Remap to normalize. Closed curves wrap but open curves clamp — check domain first.

bc3e379e-7206-4e7b-b63a-ff61f4b38a3e.name: Construct Plane
bc3e379e-7206-4e7b-b63a-ff61f4b38a3e.quick: Construct Plane | Inputs: Origin, X-Axis, Y-Axis → Plane

e76040ec-3b91-41e1-8e00-c74c23b89391.name: Align Plane
e76040ec-3b91-41e1-8e00-c74c23b89391.quick: Align Plane | Inputs: Plane, Direction → Plane

2318aee8-01fe-4ea8-9524-6966023fc622.name: Align Planes
2318aee8-01fe-4ea8-9524-6966023fc622.quick: Aligns a list of planes to minimize serial rotation between consecutive planes | M sets reference/master plane
2318aee8-01fe-4ea8-9524-6966023fc622.description: Align planes by minimizing their serial rotation.

contexts.sweep_orientation: Feed a list of perpendicular frames along a curve into P; use World XY or first frame as M to keep orientations consistent and avoid twisting
contexts.serial_frame_alignment: Wire multiple construction planes into P; M acts as alignment guide — typically a stable reference plane like XY Plane output

2318aee8-01fe-4ea8-9524-6966023fc622.errors: <~30 tokens: Empty output if P list is null; single plane input loses benefit — needs list; M mismatch in plane normal may produce unexpected rotations>

79f9fbb3-8f1d-4d9a-88a9-f7961b1012cd.name: Unit X
79f9fbb3-8f1d-4d9a-88a9-f7961b1012cd.quick: Unit X | Inputs: Factor → Unit vector

d3d195ea-2d59-4ffa-90b1-8b7ff3369f69.name: Unit Y
d3d195ea-2d59-4ffa-90b1-8b7ff3369f69.quick: Unit Y | Inputs: Factor → Unit vector

9103c240-a6a9-4223-9b42-dbd19bf38e2b.name: Unit Z
9103c240-a6a9-4223-9b42-dbd19bf38e2b.quick: Unit Z | Inputs: Factor → Unit vector

934ede4a-924a-4973-bb05-0dc4b36fae75.name: Vector 2Pt
934ede4a-924a-4973-bb05-0dc4b36fae75.quick: Creates vector from point A to point B; U=True unitizes output | also outputs length L
934ede4a-924a-4973-bb05-0dc4b36fae75.description: Create a vector between two points.

contexts.direction_between_points: Wire two Point params to A and B; set U=True to get unit direction vector; L gives raw distance — useful before Cross Product or orient operations
contexts.distance_measurement: Leave U=False; read L output directly as point-to-point distance without needing separate Vector Length component
contexts.unitized_direction: U=True normalizes V to length 1.0, equivalent to piping through Unit Vector — saves a component when direction only is needed

934ede4a-924a-4973-bb05-0dc4b36fae75.errors: Null/invalid output if A or B are not valid Point types; L=0 and undefined direction if A equals B (zero-length vector); U must be Boolean, not integer

6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.name: Amplitude
6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.quick: Sets vector length to exact value A while preserving direction | zero-length vector input produces undefined direction
6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.description: Set the amplitude (length) of a vector.

contexts.normalize_to_length: Feed any vector into V, connect a Number slider to A; outputs vector of exact length A. Common after direction calculations before using as offset or move input.
contexts.scaling_direction_vectors: Use instead of Multiply when you need a precise absolute length rather than a relative scale factor. Neighbors Multiply/Divide offer relative scaling.

6ec39468-dae7-4ffa-a766-f2ab22a2c62e.errors: Zero-vector input (V = 0,0,0) has no direction, so amplitude cannot be set — output is likely invalid or zero. Negative A values may flip or zero the vector depending on implementation.

d2da1306-259a-4994-85a4-672d8a4c7805.name: Unit Vector
d2da1306-259a-4994-85a4-672d8a4c7805.quick: Normalizes a vector to length 1 | zero-length vector input will fail or return invalid result

contexts.direction_normalization: Feed output of Vector 2Pt or Vector XYZ into V; output is same direction, length 1. Use before Cross Product or any operation requiring unit vectors.
contexts.length_independent_direction: Pair with Vector Length to separate magnitude from direction: unitize for direction, length component for magnitude independently.

d2da1306-259a-4994-85a4-672d8a4c7805.errors: Zero-length vector (0,0,0) has no defined direction — unitizing it produces invalid/null output. Ensure input vector is non-zero before connecting.

2a5cfb31-028a-4b34-b4e1-9b20ae15312e.name: Cross Product
2a5cfb31-028a-4b34-b4e1-9b20ae15312e.quick: Computes A×B cross product vector; U=true unitizes result | outputs perpendicular vector V and length L

contexts.surface_normal: Wire two edge vectors from Vector 2Pt into A and B; set U=true to get unit normal; V is perpendicular to both input vectors
contexts.area_magnitude: Leave U=false; L output gives parallelogram area spanned by A and B — useful for area calculations
contexts.orientation_check: Combine with Dot Product on result to verify handedness; pair with Reverse if perpendicular direction needs flipping

2a5cfb31-028a-4b34-b4e1-9b20ae15312e.errors: Zero-length output V (and L=0) if A and B are parallel or anti-parallel; null/invalid if non-vector geometry is wired to A or B without conversion

43b9ea8f-f772-40f2-9880-011a9c3cbbb0.name: Dot Product
43b9ea8f-f772-40f2-9880-011a9c3cbbb0.quick: Computes dot product of two vectors → scalar Number; U input unitizes vectors before computation

contexts.angle_check: Wire two Vector 2Pt or Unit Vector outputs into A and B; set U=True to normalize first; D near 1 means parallel, near 0 means perpendicular
contexts.projection_magnitude: Feed raw vectors with U=False to get scalar projection magnitude; combine with Vector Length to compute projection ratios
contexts.alignment_test: Use D output with comparison components to check if vectors point in same direction (D>0) or opposite (D<0)

43b9ea8f-f772-40f2-9880-011a9c3cbbb0.errors: Null/invalid vectors on A or B cause null output; U expects Boolean (default likely False); non-vector geometry inputs will fail — ensure vectors not points are wired

d5788074-d75d-4021-b1a3-0bf992928584.name: Reverse
d5788074-d75d-4021-b1a3-0bf992928584.quick: Flips vector direction by multiplying by -1 | Input must be a Vector type, not a point or line

contexts.flip_normal: Feed surface normal vector into V; output reversed normal for offsetting inward instead of outward
contexts.negate_force: Chain after Vector 2Pt to reverse direction; use before Cross Product or Dot Product when sign matters
contexts.invert_motion: Reverse a Unit Vector output to get opposite direction for mirroring or reflection logic

d5788074-d75d-4021-b1a3-0bf992928584.errors: Fails if non-vector geometry (point, curve) is connected to V; no output if input is null or empty vector list

675e31bf-1775-48d7-bb8d-76b77786dd53.name: Vector Length
675e31bf-1775-48d7-bb8d-76b77786dd53.quick: Returns scalar magnitude of a vector | input must be Vector type, not a point or line
675e31bf-1775-48d7-bb8d-76b77786dd53.description: Compute the length (amplitude) of a vector.

contexts.normalize_workflow: Wire Vector 2Pt output into V; use L to check distance before feeding into Unit Vector for normalized direction
contexts.filtering_by_length: Connect cross product or any vector output to V; compare L output with threshold number to filter or cull vectors by magnitude
contexts.debugging_vectors: Plug any vector into V to verify it has non-zero length before using in downstream operations like Dot Product or Reverse

675e31bf-1775-48d7-bb8d-76b77786dd53.errors: <~30 tokens: Null or zero-length vector inputs return 0; passing a Point instead of Vector causes type mismatch — use Vector 2Pt first

d1a28e95-cf96-4936-bf34-8bf142d731bf.name: Construct Domain
d1a28e95-cf96-4936-bf34-8bf142d731bf.quick: Construct Domain | Inputs: Domain start, Domain end → Domain

825ea536-aebb-41e9-af32-8baeb2ecb590.name: Deconstruct Domain
825ea536-aebb-41e9-af32-8baeb2ecb590.quick: Extracts Start (S) and End (E) numbers from a 1D domain | Input must be a Domain type, not a number
825ea536-aebb-41e9-af32-8baeb2ecb590.description: Deconstruct a numeric domain into its component parts.

contexts.domain_inspection: Wire a Domain (e.g., from Divide Domain or Construct Domain) into I; outputs S and E as individual numbers for use in expressions, remapping, or conditionals
contexts.range_extraction: Use S and E outputs to feed into arithmetic or comparison components when you need the bounds of a domain separately rather than as a unit

825ea536-aebb-41e9-af32-8baeb2ecb590.errors: Fails if input is not a Domain type — passing a plain number or interval from a 2D domain (use Deconstruct Domain² instead) will cause type mismatch

2fcc2743-8339-4cdf-a046-a1f17439191d.name: Remap Numbers
2fcc2743-8339-4cdf-a046-a1f17439191d.quick: Remap Numbers | Inputs: Value, Source, Target → Mapped

75ef4190-91a2-42d9-a245-32a7162b0384.name: Divide Domain
75ef4190-91a2-42d9-a245-32a7162b0384.quick: Splits a 1D domain into C equal sub-domains | C must be integer ≥ 1; outputs list of C Domain segments
75ef4190-91a2-42d9-a245-32a7162b0384.description: Divide a domain into equal segments.

contexts.curve_subdivision: Feed a curve's domain into I, set C to desired segment count; outputs sub-domains for use with Evaluate Curve or similar to get evenly spaced points
contexts.range_generation: Use as alternative to Range when you need domain segments rather than values; wire sub-domains to Deconstruct Domain to extract start/end numbers
contexts.nested_domain_ops: Combine with Divide Domain² for 2D grids; use 1D divide first to establish row/column counts before constructing 2D domain

75ef4190-91a2-42d9-a245-32a7162b0384.errors: Fails or produces no output if C ≤ 0 or non-integer; null/invalid domain input I causes no output; C=1 returns single domain equal to input

59daf374-bc21-4a5e-8282-5504fb7ae9ae.name: List Item
59daf374-bc21-4a5e-8282-5504fb7ae9ae.quick: List Item | Inputs: List, Index, Wrap → Item

6ec97ea8-c559-47a2-8d0f-ce80c794d1f4.name: Reverse List
6ec97ea8-c559-47a2-8d0f-ce80c794d1f4.quick: Reverses item order in a list | Works on any Generic Data type
6ec97ea8-c559-47a2-8d0f-ce80c794d1f4.description: Reverse the order of a list.

contexts.reorder_before_sort: Wire sorted list output into Reverse List to get descending order; pairs naturally with Sort List for numeric sequences
contexts.flip_sequence: Use after Shift List or Split List to invert sub-list order; input L accepts any Generic Data, output L is same type reversed
contexts.index_alignment: Reverse before Longest List or Partition List when downstream logic expects last-to-first ordering

6ec97ea8-c559-47a2-8d0f-ce80c794d1f4.errors: Empty list input returns empty output without error. Single-item list returns unchanged. No type mismatch risk since input is Generic Data.

6f93d366-919f-4dda-a35e-ba03dd62799b.name: Sort List
6f93d366-919f-4dda-a35e-ba03dd62799b.quick: Sorts list A by numeric keys K; outputs reordered K and A in ascending order.
6f93d366-919f-4dda-a35e-ba03dd62799b.description: Sort a list of numeric keys.

contexts.sort_geometry_by_value: Wire a list of numbers (distances, areas, etc.) into K and corresponding geometry into A; outputs both sorted ascending. Pair with Shift List or Split List for further processing.
contexts.sort_data_parallel: K and A must be equal-length lists; A carries any data type (points, strings, etc.) reordered to match sorted K. Use List Item after to extract specific ranked elements.
contexts.sort_then_reverse: Connect Sort List output K/A into Reverse List to get descending order, since Sort List only sorts ascending.

6f93d366-919f-4dda-a35e-ba03dd62799b.errors: Mismatched K and A list lengths cause index errors or dropped items. Non-numeric K input fails — K must be Numbers. If K contains nulls, sort order is unpredictable.

4fdfe351-6c07-47ce-9fb9-be027fb62186.name: Shift List
4fdfe351-6c07-47ce-9fb9-be027fb62186.quick: Offsets list items by S steps; W (wrap) controls whether shifted items wrap around or are discarded.
4fdfe351-6c07-47ce-9fb9-be027fb62186.description: Offset all items in a list.

contexts.cyclic_rotation: Connect a list to L, integer offset to S, set W=True to wrap items cyclically. Common with geometry lists to rotate sequence without losing items.
contexts.trimming_shift: Set W=False to drop items that fall off the end, effectively trimming the list. Useful before pairing with Split List or Partition List.
contexts.negative_offset: Negative S values shift in reverse direction. Combine with Reverse List for reordering workflows.

4fdfe351-6c07-47ce-9fb9-be027fb62186.errors: Non-integer S causes type mismatch; S larger than list length with W=False returns empty or truncated list. W must be Boolean — unconnected defaults to True (wrap).

008e9a6f-478a-4813-8c8a-546273bc3a6b.name: Cull Pattern
008e9a6f-478a-4813-8c8a-546273bc3a6b.quick: Cull Pattern | Inputs: List, Cull Pattern → List

501aecbb-c191-4d13-83d6-7ee32445ac50.name: Cull Index
501aecbb-c191-4d13-83d6-7ee32445ac50.quick: Removes elements at specified indices from a list | W (Wrap) handles out-of-range indices
501aecbb-c191-4d13-83d6-7ee32445ac50.description: Cull (remove) indexed elements from a list.

contexts.filter_by_index: Wire list to L, integer indices to I; outputs list with those positions removed. Use Panel or Series to supply I indices.
contexts.wrap_mode: W (Boolean) wraps index values when they exceed list length, preventing errors on short lists.
contexts.random_culling: Pair with Random + integer conversion to stochastically remove elements by index from any list.

501aecbb-c191-4d13-83d6-7ee32445ac50.errors: Fails or skips silently if I indices are non-integer or out of range with W=False. Empty I input returns full list unchanged. Duplicate indices in I may cause unexpected behavior.

e2039b07-d3f3-40f8-af88-d74fed238727.name: Insert Items
e2039b07-d3f3-40f8-af88-d74fed238727.quick: Inserts items (I) into list (L) at index (i); W wraps index if out of range
e2039b07-d3f3-40f8-af88-d74fed238727.description: Insert a collection of items into a list.

contexts.single_insertion: Connect source list to L, item(s) to I, integer index to i; W=True prevents index errors by wrapping. Output L is the modified list with items inserted at position i.
contexts.bulk_insertion: I accepts multiple items (Generic Data); all inserted at index i. Pair with Sort List or Shift List afterward to reorder if needed.
contexts.index_control: i is an Integer; if i exceeds list length and W=False, may error or clamp. Set W=True to wrap safely around list bounds.

e2039b07-d3f3-40f8-af88-d74fed238727.errors: Out-of-range index with W=False likely causes null/error output. Mismatched data types in I vs L won't error but may cause downstream issues.

5a93246d-2595-4c28-bc2d-90657634f92a.name: Partition List
5a93246d-2595-4c28-bc2d-90657634f92a.quick: Splits list L into sub-lists of size S | S must be a positive integer chunk size

contexts.chunking_geometry: Feed a flat list of points/curves into L, set S to chunk size (e.g. 3); outputs C as a DataTree of sub-lists, one branch per chunk. Pair with Graft/Flatten as needed.
contexts.grouping_for_operations: Use after Shift List or Sort List to group reordered items into fixed-size batches before applying per-group operations like lofting or averaging.
contexts.uneven_lists: If list length is not divisible by S, last sub-list will be shorter than S. Combine with List Length to verify chunk count downstream.

5a93246d-2595-4c28-bc2d-90657634f92a.errors: Fails or produces unexpected results if S=0 or negative; outputs a DataTree so downstream components expecting flat lists need Flatten. Last partition may be incomplete if length % S ≠ 0.

9ab93e1a-ebdf-4090-9296-b000cff7b202.name: Split List
9ab93e1a-ebdf-4090-9296-b000cff7b202.quick: Split List | Inputs: List, Index → List A

84627490-0fb2-4498-8138-ad134ee4cb36.name: Curve | Curve
84627490-0fb2-4498-8138-ad134ee4cb36.quick: Finds intersection points between two curves; outputs point(s) and parameter values on each curve.
84627490-0fb2-4498-8138-ad134ee4cb36.description: Solve intersection events for two curves.

contexts.point_finding: Wire two Curve inputs (A, B); get intersection Point(s) P plus parameters tA/tB for locating position along each curve. Works for coplanar or 3D near-intersecting curves.
contexts.parameter_extraction: Use tA/tB outputs to evaluate positions on original curves via Evaluate Curve, enabling splitting, trimming, or measuring along each curve at intersection locations.
contexts.topology_analysis: Chain with Curve | Self or Brep | Curve to build intersection networks; P output feeds downstream geometry operations.

84627490-0fb2-4498-8138-ad134ee4cb36.errors: No output if curves don't intersect or are skew in 3D (not coplanar/near-touching). Non-Curve inputs cause type errors. Parallel overlapping curves may return no discrete points.

68546dd0-aa82-471c-87e9-81cb16ac50ed.name: Surface | Curve
68546dd0-aa82-471c-87e9-81cb16ac50ed.quick: Finds where a curve intersects a surface | outputs intersection points, UV coords, curve parameter, and normals
68546dd0-aa82-471c-87e9-81cb16ac50ed.description: Solve intersection events for a surface and a curve.

contexts.point_extraction: Wire a Surface (S) and Curve (C); output P gives 3D intersection points, uv gives surface UV parameters at each hit — useful for mapping or projection workflows
contexts.curve_trimming: Output t gives curve parameter at intersection — feed into curve split/shatter components to divide curve at surface hits
contexts.normal_analysis: Output N gives surface normal at intersection point; T gives curve tangent — useful for angle-of-incidence or orientation analysis

68546dd0-aa82-471c-87e9-81cb16ac50ed.errors: <~30 tokens: No outputs if curve misses surface entirely; ensure surface is untrimmed or curve actually crosses it; null results if inputs are disconnected or wrong types>

20ef81e8-df15-4a0c-acf1-993a7607cafb.name: Brep | Curve
20ef81e8-df15-4a0c-acf1-993a7607cafb.quick: Intersects a Brep with a curve; outputs trimmed curve segments (C) and intersection points (P)
20ef81e8-df15-4a0c-acf1-993a7607cafb.description: Solve intersection events for a Brep and a curve.

contexts.finding_intersection_points: Wire a closed or open Brep to B and any curve to C; P output gives 3D points where curve pierces Brep faces; useful for structural grid intersections or panel layouts
contexts.trimming_curves_by_brep: C output returns curve portions that lie on or inside the Brep; chain with List Item or Cull to isolate desired segments
contexts.surface_vs_brep_choice: Use this over Surface|Curve when geometry is a polysurface or solid Brep; for single untrimmed surfaces, Surface|Curve may be faster

20ef81e8-df15-4a0c-acf1-993a7607cafb.errors: Null output if curve misses Brep entirely; open Breps may produce unexpected C segments near naked edges; ensure Brep is valid (use Brep repair) to avoid empty results

904e4b56-484a-4814-b35f-aa4baf362117.name: Brep | Brep
904e4b56-484a-4814-b35f-aa4baf362117.quick: Finds intersection curves and points between two Breps | outputs C (curves) and P (points); both inputs must be valid closed or open Breps
904e4b56-484a-4814-b35f-aa4baf362117.description: Solve intersection events for two Breps.

contexts.boolean_prep: Wire two solid/surface Breps to A and B; output C gives intersection curves useful for trimming or splitting before boolean operations
contexts.collision_detection: Connect geometry Breps to A and B; check if C or P outputs are non-null to detect contact between objects
contexts.seam_finding: Use C output curves to locate where two surfaces meet; feed into Divide Curve or other curve ops for further analysis

904e4b56-484a-4814-b35f-aa4baf362117.errors: Returns null C and P if Breps don't actually intersect; fails or gives unexpected results if inputs are invalid/degenerate Breps or open surfaces with no geometric overlap

931e6030-ccb3-4a7b-a89a-99dcce8770cd.name: Multiple Curves
931e6030-ccb3-4a7b-a89a-99dcce8770cd.quick: Finds all intersection points among a set of curves at once | Input C accepts multiple curves as a list
931e6030-ccb3-4a7b-a89a-99dcce8770cd.description: Solve intersection events for multiple curves.

contexts.batch_curve_intersections: Wire a list of curves into C; outputs P (intersection points), iA/iB (curve indices), tA/tB (parameters on each curve). Use iA/iB to identify which curve pair intersected.
contexts.network_analysis: Feed planar or 3D curve networks; use iA/iB integer outputs to map intersections back to specific curve pairs for downstream logic or sorting.
contexts.replacing_pairwise_intersections: Use instead of multiple Curve|Curve components when intersecting many curves simultaneously; more efficient for large sets.

931e6030-ccb3-4a7b-a89a-99dcce8770cd.errors: <2 curves in list yields no intersections; non-planar or skew 3D curves may return no points if they don't physically intersect within tolerance; duplicate curves may produce coincident/overlapping events rather than point intersections

477c2e7b-c5e5-421e-b8b2-ba60cdf5398b.name: Region Intersection
477c2e7b-c5e5-421e-b8b2-ba60cdf5398b.quick: Returns overlapping area between two sets of planar closed curves | curves must be closed, coplanar, and on same plane P
477c2e7b-c5e5-421e-b8b2-ba60cdf5398b.description: Intersection between two sets of planar closed curves (regions)

contexts.boolean_overlap: Wire two closed planar curves into A and B; supply a shared Plane P (often XY or extracted from curve). Output R is the intersection region curve(s). Pair with Region Union/Difference for full boolean workflow.
contexts.multi_region: A and B accept curve lists; computes pairwise intersections across sets. Useful for finding overlaps in grid or tiling patterns. Flatten inputs if cross-referencing is unintended.
contexts.downstream_area: Feed R into Area component to measure intersection size, or into Boundary Surface to create a surface from the result.

477c2e7b-c5e5-421e-b8b2-ba60cdf5398b.errors: Fails or returns null if curves are not closed, not coplanar, or not on plane P. Non-planar or open curves produce no output. Mismatched planes between A and B cause empty results.

1222394f-0d33-4f31-9101-7281bde89fe5.name: Region Union
1222394f-0d33-4f31-9101-7281bde89fe5.quick: Merges overlapping planar closed curves into unified outline regions | All curves must be closed, planar, and coplanar to the input Plane
1222394f-0d33-4f31-9101-7281bde89fe5.description: Union of a set of planar closed curves (regions)

contexts.merging_floor_outlines: Feed multiple closed boundary curves into C; set P to the working plane (e.g., XY). Outputs merged outer boundary curves. Commonly paired with Region Intersection to combine boolean ops.
contexts.cleaning_overlapping_shapes: Use after geometry operations that produce overlapping closed curves. Wire all curves to C, provide a consistent plane P. Result R feeds downstream area or surface operations.
contexts.2d_boolean_workflow: Typically used alongside Region Intersection and Region Difference to perform full 2D boolean logic on planar curve sets. P must match the plane all curves lie on.

1222394f-0d33-4f31-9101-7281bde89fe5.errors: Fails if curves are not closed, not planar, or not coplanar with P. Non-intersecting curves may pass through unchanged. Open curves cause null output on R.

2696bd14-3fb5-4750-827f-86df6c31d664.name: Mesh Box
2696bd14-3fb5-4750-827f-86df6c31d664.quick: Creates a mesh box from a Box with X/Y/Z face subdivisions per axis | X, Y, Z are integer face counts, not dimensions

contexts.basic_box_mesh: Wire a Box (from Box component or similar) into B; set X, Y, Z integers (e.g. 1,1,1 for minimal faces) to control mesh density per axis. Outputs single Mesh M.
contexts.subdivision_control: Increase X/Y/Z integers to subdivide faces along each axis independently — useful before mesh deformation or smoothing operations downstream.
contexts.primitive_workflow: Pairs with Mesh Sphere, Mesh Plane for building mesh-based geometry without converting NURBS; avoids Brep-to-Mesh conversion artifacts.

2696bd14-3fb5-4750-827f-86df6c31d664.errors: Null output if B input is not a valid Box. X/Y/Z values ≤ 0 likely cause failure or degenerate mesh — use minimum value of 1.

8adbf481-7589-4a40-b490-006531ea001d.name: Mesh Plane
8adbf481-7589-4a40-b490-006531ea001d.quick: Creates a flat mesh plane from a Rectangle boundary with W×H quad subdivisions | B must be a Rectangle, not a curve or surface

contexts.basic_mesh_plane: Wire a Rectangle (from Rectangle or Boundary Surface) into B; set W and H integers for column/row count. Outputs mesh M and total area A as Number.
contexts.subdivision_control: W and H control quad density along rectangle width and height. Higher values = finer mesh. Both default likely to 1 if unset, producing a single quad face.
contexts.area_output: Output A gives the total mesh area as a Number, useful for area calculations without needing a separate Area component.

8adbf481-7589-4a40-b490-006531ea001d.errors: Fails if B is not a Rectangle type (curves or surfaces won't work). W or H ≤ 0 will likely produce null mesh. Non-planar rectangles may cause unexpected results.

58cf422f-19f7-42f7-9619-fc198c51c657.name: Mesh Surface
58cf422f-19f7-42f7-9619-fc198c51c657.quick: Creates a UV mesh from a surface with U/V count divisions; H=holes, Q=quads control topology

contexts.basic_meshing: Connect a NURBS or other surface to S, set U and V integers for grid density. Output M feeds Mesh Join or rendering. Higher U/V = finer mesh.
contexts.quad_mesh_generation: Set Q=True to force quad faces instead of triangles. Useful before Mesh Join or analysis workflows requiring uniform topology.
contexts.hole_handling: H (Boolean) likely controls whether surface holes/trims are respected in the mesh output. Toggle based on trimmed surface needs.

58cf422f-19f7-42f7-9619-fc198c51c657.errors: Null output if S is not a valid surface. U or V of 0 or negative will fail. Trimmed surfaces may produce unexpected topology near trim boundaries.

60e7defa-8b21-4ee1-99aa-a9223d6134ff.name: Mesh Brep
60e7defa-8b21-4ee1-99aa-a9223d6134ff.quick: Mesh Brep | Inputs: Brep, Settings → Mesh

2b9bf01d-5fe5-464c-b0b3-b469eb5f2efb.name: Mesh Edges
2b9bf01d-5fe5-464c-b0b3-b469eb5f2efb.quick: Mesh Edges | Inputs: Mesh → Naked Edges

e2c0f9db-a862-4bd9-810c-ef2610e7a56f.name: Construct Mesh
e2c0f9db-a862-4bd9-810c-ef2610e7a56f.quick: Construct Mesh | Inputs: Vertices, Faces, Colours → Mesh

cb4ca22c-3419-4962-a078-ad4ff7f1f929.name: Face Normals
cb4ca22c-3419-4962-a078-ad4ff7f1f929.quick: Extracts center point (C) and normal vector (N) per mesh face | outputs one item per face, not per vertex
cb4ca22c-3419-4962-a078-ad4ff7f1f929.description: Extract the normals and center points of all faces in a mesh

contexts.orient_geometry_to_faces: Connect mesh to M; use C (face centers) and N (face normals) to orient planes or geometry onto each face. Pair with Plane Normal or Align Plane.
contexts.visualize_normals: Feed N into Line SDL with C as start to draw normal lines per face. Useful for diagnosing mesh orientation or flipped faces.
contexts.filter_faces_by_direction: Dot product N with a reference vector to select faces pointing in a given direction. Combine with Cull Pattern to filter face subsets.

cb4ca22c-3419-4962-a078-ad4ff7f1f929.errors: Null output if M is not a valid mesh. Output count equals face count — mismatches occur if downstream components expect vertex-count data instead.

d8d68c35-f869-486d-adf3-69ee3cc2d501.name: Rail Revolution
d8d68c35-f869-486d-adf3-69ee3cc2d501.quick: Creates surface of revolution guided by a rail curve | axis line (A) is required to define rotation axis
d8d68c35-f869-486d-adf3-69ee3cc2d501.description: Create a surface of revolution using a sweep rail.

contexts.vase_or_bottle_shape: Connect profile curve to P, rail curve to R, axis Line to A; S boolean toggles closed/open revolution; outputs Brep surface
contexts.constrained_revolution: Unlike basic Revolution, rail curve R guides the sweep path, giving more control over how profile rotates around axis A
contexts.closed_surface: Set S=True to close the revolution into a full 360° surface; profile P and rail R should be compatible in domain

d8d68c35-f869-486d-adf3-69ee3cc2d501.errors: <~30 tokens: Null output if axis Line A is missing or not aligned with geometry; mismatched curve domains between P and R cause failed Brep

d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.name: Boundary Surfaces
d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.quick: Fills planar closed curves with flat surfaces | curves MUST be planar and closed
d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.description: Create planar surfaces from a collection of boundary edge curves.

contexts.cap_flat_regions: Wire closed planar curves (e.g., rectangles, polygons, projected outlines) into E; outputs capped flat Surface. Common after Curve Boolean or Project operations.
contexts.multiple_boundaries: Feed a list of closed planar curves; each gets its own surface. Useful for filling multiple floor plan outlines simultaneously.
contexts.pre_loft_or_extrude: Often used alongside Loft/Extrude to cap open-ended solids — provides the flat end faces before joining into a closed Brep.

d51e9b65-aa4e-4fd6-976c-cef35d421d05.errors: Fails silently (null surface) if input curve is not planar or not closed. Non-planar 3D curves produce no output — use Patch instead.

4b04a1e1-cddf-405d-a7db-335aaa940541.name: Surface From Points
4b04a1e1-cddf-405d-a7db-335aaa940541.quick: Builds NURBS surface from flat point grid | U count defines columns; total points must divide evenly by U
4b04a1e1-cddf-405d-a7db-335aaa940541.description: Create a nurbs surface from a grid of points.

contexts.grid_surface: Wire flattened point list to P, set U (integer = points per row). Points must form a rectangular grid. Output S is a NURBS surface ready for further ops.
contexts.parametric_paneling: Generate grid points via Surface > Divide or math expressions, flatten, feed into P with matching U count. Useful for morphing surfaces from point attractors.
contexts.interpolated_form: Toggle I (interpolate) to control whether surface passes through points or uses them as control points — affects surface smoothness and fit.

4b04a1e1-cddf-405d-a7db-335aaa940541.errors: Fails if point count is not divisible by U, or if points are null/non-grid. Non-rectangular or jagged grids produce degenerate surfaces.

7db14002-c09c-4d7b-9f80-e4e2b00dfa1d.name: Surface Split
7db14002-c09c-4d7b-9f80-e4e2b00dfa1d.quick: Splits a surface using one or more curves; curves must lie on the surface or fully intersect it to produce fragments.
7db14002-c09c-4d7b-9f80-e4e2b00dfa1d.description: Split a surface with a bunch of curves.

contexts.panel_subdivision: Wire a surface to S and a set of planar or projected curves to C; outputs multiple surface fragments. Curves must cross the surface boundary completely to split cleanly.
contexts.boolean_trimming: Use intersection curves (from Surface|Curve or Brep|Curve) fed into C to cut the surface; combine with List Item to isolate desired fragments.
contexts.multi-cut: Feed a Merge or list of curves into C to split with multiple cutters simultaneously; all cuts applied at once, producing all resulting pieces in F.

7db14002-c09c-4d7b-9f80-e4e2b00dfa1d.errors: Fails silently (returns unsplit surface) if curves don't fully cross the surface; curves not on the surface plane or not projected onto it won't split. Incomplete intersection = no split.

3092caf0-7cf9-4885-bcc0-e635d878832a.name: Trim with Region
3092caf0-7cf9-4885-bcc0-e635d878832a.quick: Splits curve C by closed region curve R on plane P; outputs inside (Ci) and outside (Co) segments.
3092caf0-7cf9-4885-bcc0-e635d878832a.description: Trim a curve with a region.

contexts.curve_clipping: Wire a curve to C, a closed boundary curve to R, and a reference plane to P. Outputs Ci (portions inside region) and Co (portions outside). Region R must be a closed planar curve.
contexts.2d_layout_trimming: Use with a rectangle or polygon as R and a construction plane as P to clip curves to a boundary. Pair with Join Curves to reconnect output segments.
contexts.region_selection: Use Ci to keep only curve portions inside a boundary, or Co to keep exterior portions. Useful before offsetting or paneling operations.

3092caf0-7cf9-4885-bcc0-e635d878832a.errors: Fails if R is not a closed curve or not planar to P. Missing or mismatched plane P causes incorrect trim results. Open curves as R produce no output.

8db16e9c-2816-4c95-939d-8fecdc30906f.name: Pull Curve
8db16e9c-2816-4c95-939d-8fecdc30906f.quick: Projects/pulls a curve onto a surface along surface normals | Surface must be valid; curve must be near the surface
8db16e9c-2816-4c95-939d-8fecdc30906f.description: Pull a curve onto a surface.

contexts.conforming_curve_to_surface: Wire a curve (C) and a target surface (S); output is the curve remapped onto the surface. Useful after constructing curves in 3D space that need to lie on a surface.
contexts.comparison_with_project_curve: Unlike Project Curve (which projects onto Breps along a direction), Pull Curve pulls along surface normals — better for curved or non-planar surfaces where directional projection would distort results.

8db16e9c-2816-4c95-939d-8fecdc30906f.errors: Fails or returns null if curve is too far from surface or surface is untrimmed/degenerate. Output curve may be fragmented if input curve crosses surface boundaries.

ef6b26f4-f820-48d6-b0c5-85898ef8888b.name: Split Brep
ef6b26f4-f820-48d6-b0c5-85898ef8888b.quick: Splits Brep B using cutter Brep C; outputs resulting Brep fragments | both inputs must be valid, closed or open Breps

contexts.cutting_solid: Feed a closed solid as B and a cutting surface or solid as C; R returns all resulting pieces. Often followed by Solid Union or Solid Difference to recombine selected fragments.
contexts.surface_splitting: Use an open surface as B and a cutting surface/brep as C to divide it into regions. Results may need List Item or filtering to isolate desired pieces.
contexts.multiple_cuts: For splitting B with many cutters, prefer Split Brep Multiple neighbor instead; chaining Split Brep sequentially can cause geometry failures.

ef6b26f4-f820-48d6-b0c5-85898ef8888b.errors: Fails silently (null R) if B and C don't intersect, or if geometry is invalid/degenerate. Open Breps used as cutters may not split closed solids reliably. Tolerance issues can cause missed splits.

f0b70e8e-7337-4ce4-a7bb-317fc971f918.name: Trim Solid
f0b70e8e-7337-4ce4-a7bb-317fc971f918.quick: Cuts holes into Brep S using solid Brep cutters T | Both S and T must be closed/solid Breps
f0b70e8e-7337-4ce4-a7bb-317fc971f918.description: Cut holes into a shape with a set of solid cutters.

contexts.boolean_subtraction_variant: Wire target closed Brep to S, one or more closed cutter Breps to T; outputs trimmed Brep R. Similar to Solid Difference but oriented for cutting voids/holes rather than full subtraction.
contexts.multiple_cutters: T accepts multiple Breps; connect a list of cutter solids to punch multiple holes into S simultaneously. Flatten or graft as needed to control pairing.
contexts.workflow_with_solid_ops: Often used alongside Solid Union and Solid Difference; Trim Solid is preferred when cutters should remove interior material (holes) from a base shape.

f0b70e8e-7337-4ce4-a7bb-317fc971f918.errors: Fails if S or T are open/non-manifold Breps; no result if cutters don't intersect S; degenerate geometry or self-intersecting Breps cause null output R.

ffe2dbed-9b5d-4f91-8fe3-10c8961ac2f8.name: Curve On Surface
ffe2dbed-9b5d-4f91-8fe3-10c8961ac2f8.quick: Interpolates a curve through UV points on a surface; uv input must be 2D points in surface parameter space | closed toggle via C
ffe2dbed-9b5d-4f91-8fe3-10c8961ac2f8.description: Create an interpolated curve through a set of points on a surface.

contexts.geodesic_path: Feed a surface (S) and a list of UV parameter points (uv) to trace a path along the surface; pair with Surface Closest Point to convert 3D points to UV coords first
contexts.closed_curve: Set boolean C=True to close the interpolated curve; useful for loops or boundary curves on surface patches
contexts.extracting_length_domain: Outputs L (arc length) and D (domain) alongside curve C; wire L to downstream length-dependent operations or D to Sub Curve for trimming

ffe2dbed-9b5d-4f91-8fe3-10c8961ac2f8.errors: Fails if uv points are outside surface domain (0–1 or actual UV range); passing 3D world points instead of UV parameter points produces wrong or null results; fewer than 2 UV points yields no curve

7663efbb-d9b8-4c6a-a0da-c3750a7bbe77.name: Sine
7663efbb-d9b8-4c6a-a0da-c3750a7bbe77.quick: Computes sin(x); input x is in radians, not degrees.
7663efbb-d9b8-4c6a-a0da-c3750a7bbe77.description: Compute the sine of a value

contexts.wave_motion: Feed a remap or expression output (radians) into x; y outputs -1 to 1 range. Pair with Cosine for circular motion patterns.
contexts.angle_to_component: Use after DegToRad conversion; wire y into vector or point construction for oscillating offsets.
contexts.periodic_surface: Drive surface U/V parameters through Sine to create wave-based geometry; combine with Cosine for Lissajous-type forms.

7663efbb-d9b8-4c6a-a0da-c3750a7bbe77.errors: Wrong range: passing degrees instead of radians gives unexpected small values. Output is Generic Data — may need explicit cast to Number for downstream math components.

d2d2a900-780c-4d58-9a35-1f9d8d35df6f.name: Cosine
d2d2a900-780c-4d58-9a35-1f9d8d35df6f.quick: Computes cos(x); input x is in radians, not degrees.
d2d2a900-780c-4d58-9a35-1f9d8d35df6f.description: Compute the cosine of a value

contexts.wave_motion: Feed a radian value (e.g., from Range or Expression) into x; outputs y in [-1,1]. Pair with Sine for circular motion or oscillation patterns.
contexts.angle_conversion: Convert degrees to radians first (multiply by Pi/180) before passing to x, otherwise results will be incorrect.
contexts.inverse_lookup: Use ArcCosine neighbor to reverse: get angle from a known cosine value.

d2d2a900-780c-4d58-9a35-1f9d8d35df6f.errors: Wrong output range if x is in degrees instead of radians. Generic Data type means non-numeric inputs will fail silently or error; ensure x is a number.

0f31784f-7177-4104-8500-1f4f4a306df4.name: Tangent
0f31784f-7177-4104-8500-1f4f4a306df4.quick: Computes tan(x); input in radians | undefined at x = π/2 + nπ (returns ±infinity)
0f31784f-7177-4104-8500-1f4f4a306df4.description: Compute the tangent of a value

contexts.angle_to_slope: Wire radian angle value into x; output y gives slope ratio (rise/run). Pair with ArcTangent to invert. Common in geometry and surface normal calculations.
contexts.trig_chain: Used alongside Sine and Cosine for parametric math. Feed Panel or Expression output as x; chain y into further math components for wave or angular transforms.

0f31784f-7177-4104-8500-1f4f4a306df4.errors: Undefined (infinity/NaN) at x = π/2 + nπ; ensure input is radians not degrees — use Radians component to convert first. Generic Data input means no type-checking; non-numeric input will fail silently.

cc15ba56-fae7-4f05-b599-cb7c43b60e11.name: ArcSine
cc15ba56-fae7-4f05-b599-cb7c43b60e11.quick: Returns angle (radians) whose sine equals input x | x must be in [-1, 1] or returns invalid
cc15ba56-fae7-4f05-b599-cb7c43b60e11.description: Compute the angle whose sine is the specified value.

contexts.inverse_trig: Feed normalized values (-1 to 1) into x; outputs angle in radians. Pair with Degrees component to convert. Commonly used after Sine to recover original angle.
contexts.angle_recovery: Use when you have a sine ratio (e.g., from geometry) and need the angle back. Wire output y into further trig or rotation operations.

cc15ba56-fae7-4f05-b599-cb7c43b60e11.errors: Input x outside [-1, 1] produces NaN/invalid — sine values are bounded, so any ratio beyond this range is mathematically undefined for ArcSine.

49584390-d541-41f7-b5f6-1f9515ac0f73.name: ArcCosine
49584390-d541-41f7-b5f6-1f9515ac0f73.quick: Returns angle (radians) whose cosine equals input x | x must be in [-1, 1] range
49584390-d541-41f7-b5f6-1f9515ac0f73.description: Compute the angle whose cosine is the specified value.

contexts.angle_from_dot_product: Feed normalized dot product result into x; output y gives angle in radians between 0 and π. Often paired with Cosine to invert cosine calculations in geometric workflows.
contexts.surface_normal_analysis: Connect ratio or normalized value (e.g., from vector dot products) to x; chain output y to Degrees component if angle in degrees needed downstream.

49584390-d541-41f7-b5f6-1f9515ac0f73.errors: Input outside [-1, 1] returns NaN or error — cosine values are bounded; non-numeric Generic Data input will fail silently or error. Output is in radians, not degrees.

b4647919-d041-419e-99f5-fa0dc0ddb8b6.name: ArcTangent
b4647919-d041-419e-99f5-fa0dc0ddb8b6.quick: Returns angle (radians) whose tangent equals input x | output is in radians, not degrees
b4647919-d041-419e-99f5-fa0dc0ddb8b6.description: Compute the angle whose tangent is the specified value.

contexts.angle_from_slope: Feed a slope ratio (rise/run) into x; outputs angle in radians. Use Degrees component to convert. Pairs with Tangent for round-trip verification.
contexts.vector_angle_calculation: Use with division of y/x components to recover angle from a 2D vector direction. Chain with Sine/Cosine for further trig operations.

b4647919-d041-419e-99f5-fa0dc0ddb8b6.errors: <~30 tokens: No domain restriction on x (all reals valid); output always in radians — forgetting conversion to degrees is the most common mistake.

ad476cb7-b6d1-41c8-986b-0df243a64146.name: Square Root
ad476cb7-b6d1-41c8-986b-0df243a64146.quick: Computes √x | Input must be ≥ 0; negative values produce NaN/error
ad476cb7-b6d1-41c8-986b-0df243a64146.description: Compute the square root of a value

contexts.geometry_scaling: Feed numeric values (lengths, areas) into x; output y gives square root for normalization or distance calculations. Often paired with Square or Power components.
contexts.math_chain: Used in chains with Square, Logarithm, or Power of E for algebraic expressions. Input x accepts numbers or number lists; output y is same structure.
contexts.distance_calculation: Commonly used after summing squared components (e.g., Pythagorean theorem). Wire sum of squares into x to get Euclidean distance.

ad476cb7-b6d1-41c8-986b-0df243a64146.errors: Negative input produces NaN or null output — ensure x ≥ 0 before wiring. Non-numeric generic data may fail silently or return null.

27d6f724-a701-4585-992f-3897488abf08.name: Logarithm
27d6f724-a701-4585-992f-3897488abf08.quick: Computes log base-10 of input value | Input must be positive (x > 0)
27d6f724-a701-4585-992f-3897488abf08.description: Compute the Base-10 logarithm of a value.

contexts.data_scaling: Wire numeric values to x; outputs log10(x). Pair with Power of 10 as inverse. Useful for compressing large numeric ranges into manageable scale.
contexts.inverse_of_power_of_10: Use alongside Power of 10 component: log10 and 10^N are inverses. Chain them to verify round-trip accuracy or normalize exponential data.
contexts.comparison_with_natural_log: Use Log base-10 for decade-based scaling; use Natural Logarithm for growth/decay models. Both accept generic numeric input.

27d6f724-a701-4585-992f-3897488abf08.errors: Fails or returns NaN/error for x ≤ 0 (log undefined for zero and negatives). Non-numeric generic data input will cause type mismatch.

c717f26f-e4a0-475c-8e1c-b8f77af1bc99.name: Power of E
c717f26f-e4a0-475c-8e1c-b8f77af1bc99.quick: Computes e^x (Euler's number raised to power x) | input x is numeric
c717f26f-e4a0-475c-8e1c-b8f77af1bc99.description: Raise E to the power of N.

contexts.exponential_growth: Feed numeric values into x to get e^x; commonly paired with Natural Logarithm (inverse operation) or used after arithmetic to compute exponential curves
contexts.inverse_of_ln: Use after Natural Logarithm output to recover original value: e^(ln(x)) = x; wire Natural Log output directly into x input

c717f26f-e4a0-475c-8e1c-b8f77af1bc99.errors: Non-numeric input to x will fail; very large x values may produce overflow; no output if x is null or unconnected

0d2ccfb3-9d41-4759-9452-da6a522c3eaa.name: Pi
0d2ccfb3-9d41-4759-9452-da6a522c3eaa.quick: Returns N × π | N=1 gives π, N=2 gives 2π, N=0.5 gives π/2

contexts.angle_conversion: Feed integer or decimal into N to get multiples of Pi; useful for defining full/half rotations in radians before passing to trig functions like Sin or Cos.
contexts.geometry_scaling: Use N=2 for full circle circumference factors or N=0.5 for quarter-turn angles; wire output directly into Rotate or Arc components expecting radian values.

0d2ccfb3-9d41-4759-9452-da6a522c3eaa.errors: No type errors expected; non-numeric N input will fail. N=0 returns 0, not an error but a common logical mistake.

0d1e2027-f153-460d-84c0-f9af431b08cb.name: Maximum
0d1e2027-f153-460d-84c0-f9af431b08cb.quick: Returns the greater of two values (A vs B) | Works on generic data; numeric comparison most reliable
