0d1e2027-f153-460d-84c0-f9af431b08cb.description: Return the greater of two items.

contexts.clamping_upper_bound: Pair with Minimum to clamp values; wire raw number to A, upper limit to B; R outputs whichever is larger, effectively enforcing a floor
contexts.numeric_comparison: Wire two Number params to A and B; R returns the larger value; commonly used before Clamp or Truncate to bound ranges
contexts.list_operations: With matching list lengths, compares element-wise; mismatched lists trigger longest-list or cross-reference depending on graft settings

0d1e2027-f153-460d-84c0-f9af431b08cb.errors: Non-comparable generic types (e.g., text vs number) will fail or return null; mismatched list lengths may produce unexpected cross-referenced results; ensure both inputs share the same data type

57308b30-772d-4919-ac67-e86c18f3a996.name: Minimum
57308b30-772d-4919-ac67-e86c18f3a996.quick: Returns lesser of A and B | Works on numbers; generic type means non-comparable inputs may fail
57308b30-772d-4919-ac67-e86c18f3a996.description: Return the lesser of two items.

contexts.clamping_lower_bound: Pair with Maximum to clamp values: Maximum(min_val, Minimum(max_val, x)); feeds into Clamp-like patterns without using Clamp directly
contexts.numeric_comparison: Wire two Number or Integer streams to A and B; outputs element-wise minimum per list item via standard Grasshopper data matching
contexts.bounding_ranges: Use alongside Truncate or Clamp to restrict numerical extremes; Minimum sets upper cap on lower bound logic

57308b30-772d-4919-ac67-e86c18f3a996.errors: Non-numeric or incomparable generic types (e.g., text, geometry) will likely return null or error; mismatched list lengths trigger shortest-list or cross-reference behavior depending on data matching mode

338666eb-14c5-4d9b-82e2-2b5be60655df.name: Weighted Average
338666eb-14c5-4d9b-82e2-2b5be60655df.quick: Computes weighted average of items I using weights W | W count must match I count
338666eb-14c5-4d9b-82e2-2b5be60655df.description: Solve the arithmetic weighted average for a set of items

contexts.blending_values: Feed numeric list to I and corresponding weight list to W; outputs single weighted mean. Useful for interpolating between multiple values with custom influence per item.
contexts.geometry_weighting: I accepts Generic Data so can handle points or vectors; W drives relative contribution. Pair with Average neighbor for comparison of weighted vs. unweighted results.
contexts.parameter_control: Use Clamp or Truncate on W inputs before feeding to ensure weights stay in valid range; negative or zero weights may produce unexpected results.

338666eb-14c5-4d9b-82e2-2b5be60655df.errors: Mismatched list lengths between I and W will cause errors or incorrect output; non-numeric W values will fail. Empty I list returns no output.

9df5e896-552d-4c8c-b9ca-4fc147ffa022.name: Expression
9df5e896-552d-4c8c-b9ca-4fc147ffa022.quick: Expression | Inputs: x, y, z → Result

cc2b626f-6eff-4d08-9829-2877560693f4.name: Evaluate
cc2b626f-6eff-4d08-9829-2877560693f4.quick: Evaluate | Inputs: E, x, y → R
cc2b626f-6eff-4d08-9829-2877560693f4.description: Evaluate an expression with a flexible number of variables.

bc984576-7aa6-491f-a91d-e444c33675a7.name: Graph Mapper
bc984576-7aa6-491f-a91d-e444c33675a7.quick: Graph Mapper | Inputs: no inputs → output

cb2c7d3c-41b4-4c6d-a6bd-9235bd2851bb.name: Gate Not
cb2c7d3c-41b4-4c6d-a6bd-9235bd2851bb.quick: Inverts a boolean: True→False, False→True | Input must be Boolean type

contexts.toggle_inversion: Wire a Toggle or boolean output into A; R outputs the opposite value. Useful for switching between two states in conditional logic.
contexts.logic_chain: Combine with Gate And/Or/Xor to build complex boolean expressions. E.g., NOT(A) fed into Gate And to exclude a condition.
contexts.filter_negation: Use R to filter geometry or data where a condition is false — pass R into Dispatch or Cull Pattern to select non-matching items.

cb2c7d3c-41b4-4c6d-a6bd-9235bd2851bb.errors: Non-boolean input causes type conversion issues; null/empty input returns null. No list handling warnings — operates item by item on lists.

de4a0d86-2709-4564-935a-88bf4d40af89.name: Gate Xor
de4a0d86-2709-4564-935a-88bf4d40af89.quick: Gate Xor | Inputs: A, B → R

d8332545-21b2-4716-96e3-8559a9876e17.name: Dispatch
d8332545-21b2-4716-96e3-8559a9876e17.quick: Dispatch | Inputs: List, Dispatch pattern → List A

eeafc956-268e-461d-8e73-ee05c6f72c01.name: Stream Filter
eeafc956-268e-461d-8e73-ee05c6f72c01.quick: Selects one of multiple input streams (0,1,...) based on integer gate G | G index must match an available stream input
eeafc956-268e-461d-8e73-ee05c6f72c01.description: Filters a collection of input streams

contexts.conditional_stream_selection: Wire multiple data streams to inputs 0,1,2...; connect an integer (often from a Value List or logic) to G; selected stream passes to S. Pairs with Stream Gate for bidirectional routing.
contexts.branching_logic: Use with boolean-to-integer conversion (e.g., 0/1 from comparison) to switch between two geometry or data sources dynamically without rebuilding tree structure.

eeafc956-268e-461d-8e73-ee05c6f72c01.errors: If G is out of range of available stream inputs, output S is null. Non-integer G causes type mismatch. Mismatched data structures between streams don't error but may produce unexpected tree shapes downstream.

71fcc052-6add-4d70-8d97-cfb37ea9d169.name: Stream Gate
71fcc052-6add-4d70-8d97-cfb37ea9d169.quick: Routes stream S to output 0 or 1 based on integer G (0 or 1) | G determines which output receives data
71fcc052-6add-4d70-8d97-cfb37ea9d169.description: Redirects a stream into specific outputs.

contexts.conditional_routing: Connect data to S, drive G with an integer (0 or 1) to switch which output branch receives the stream; useful for toggling between two processing paths
contexts.boolean_switching: Pair with a Boolean-to-integer conversion (True=1, False=0) on G to dynamically redirect data based on logic conditions
contexts.branching_workflows: Use alongside Stream Filter for multi-stream routing; Stream Gate handles binary switching while Stream Filter handles collection-based filtering

71fcc052-6add-4d70-8d97-cfb37ea9d169.errors: G values outside 0 or 1 likely send nothing to either output; non-integer G input may cause type mismatch; no data flows if G is null

23afc7aa-2d2f-4ae7-b876-bf366246b826.name: Natural logarithm
23afc7aa-2d2f-4ae7-b876-bf366246b826.quick: Computes ln(x) | Input must be positive number; ln(0) or negative values return undefined/error
23afc7aa-2d2f-4ae7-b876-bf366246b826.description: Compute the natural logarithm of a value.

contexts.inverse_of_power_of_e: Pair with Power of E component: ln(e^n) = n. Wire numeric values directly; useful for normalizing exponential growth data.
contexts.math_expressions: Used in polynomial/math chains alongside Logarithm (base-10) and Square Root. Wire Number or expression output into x; y outputs ln result as number.
contexts.domain_scaling: Apply to positive domain values to compress large ranges. Ensure upstream values are strictly positive; use Absolute Value or clamp before input if needed.

23afc7aa-2d2f-4ae7-b876-bf366246b826.errors: Fails or returns NaN for x ≤ 0; Generic Data input means type mismatches (text, null) will cause runtime errors. No list-handling issues beyond standard per-item processing.

bd96f893-d57b-4f04-90d0-dca0d72ff2f9.name: Truncate
bd96f893-d57b-4f04-90d0-dca0d72ff2f9.quick: Truncates numerical extremes from data I using threshold t | t controls the truncation limit

contexts.clamping_alternative: Feed numeric list into I, set t as threshold; unlike Clamp (which has min/max), Truncate cuts values beyond a single extreme — wire alongside Minimum/Maximum for range control
contexts.data_cleaning: Use before Weighted Average to remove outliers; I accepts Generic Data so numbers or lists work; t sets the cutoff value for truncation

bd96f893-d57b-4f04-90d0-dca0d72ff2f9.errors: Passing non-numeric data into I may cause type errors; t must be a Number — leaving t unset or null likely causes no truncation or component failure

3cadddef-1e2b-4c09-9390-0e8f78f7609f.name: Merge
3cadddef-1e2b-4c09-9390-0e8f78f7609f.quick: Merge | Inputs: Data 1, Data 2, Data 3 → Result

1303da7b-e339-4e65-a051-82c4dce8224d.name: Simplify Tree
1303da7b-e339-4e65-a051-82c4dce8224d.quick: Removes common leading path indices shared by all branches, flattening redundant nesting | Boolean F toggles simplification on/off
1303da7b-e339-4e65-a051-82c4dce8224d.description: Simplify a data tree by removing the overlap shared amongst all branches.

contexts.cleaning_tree_paths: Wire any data tree into T; outputs same data with shared path prefix stripped. E.g., {0;0;0} and {0;0;1} become {0} and {1}. Use before Tree Branch to make paths more readable.
contexts.conditional_simplify: Set F (Boolean) to false to bypass simplification and pass tree through unchanged — useful for toggling in debugging workflows alongside Tree Statistics.
contexts.pre_entwine_cleanup: Place before Entwine or Stream Filter to normalize path depths across branches, preventing unexpected nesting mismatches when combining streams.

1303da7b-e339-4e65-a051-82c4dce8224d.errors: No simplification occurs if branches already have minimal paths or only one branch exists — output equals input. F=false disables component entirely. Does not flatten data; only trims shared leading indices.

41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.name: Flip Matrix
41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.quick: Swaps rows and columns of a matrix-like data tree | Tree must have uniform branch lengths (rectangular matrix) or results are unpredictable
41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.description: Flip a matrix-like data tree by swapping rows and columns.

contexts.transposing_grid_data: Wire a rectangular data tree (e.g., {0;0}, {0;1}... {n;m}) into D; output reindexes so {row;col} becomes {col;row}. Commonly used after Surface or Grid components that produce row-major trees.
contexts.reordering_for_downstream: Use before Entwine or Relative Items when data is organized by one axis but downstream components expect the other axis as the primary branch path.
contexts.stream_routing: Pair with Stream Filter or Stream Gate when you need to redistribute transposed branches into separate outputs per column.

41aa4112-9c9b-42f4-847e-503b9d90e4c7.errors: Fails silently or produces ragged output if input tree branches have unequal lengths (non-rectangular matrix). Empty branches in input produce empty branches in unexpected positions in output.

f9b89a46-bc5d-4f7a-9a6f-134f93ac3af9.name: Path Mapper
f9b89a46-bc5d-4f7a-9a6f-134f93ac3af9.quick: Remaps data tree branch paths using lexical pattern matching (e.g., {A;B} → {B;A}) | Mapping syntax must be exact; mismatched patterns silently pass data unchanged
f9b89a46-bc5d-4f7a-9a6f-134f93ac3af9.description: Perform lexical operations on data trees.

contexts.reordering_path_indices: Wire any data tree; set source pattern like {A;B;C} and target like {C;A;B} to reorder path indices. Often used after Entwine to reorganize combined stream paths.
contexts.flattening_specific_levels: Use wildcard patterns (e.g., {A;B;*} → {A}) to collapse specific path levels while preserving others. Pair with Path Compare to verify paths before mapping.
contexts.renumbering_branches: Map {A;B} → {0;A} style patterns to inject fixed indices or normalize branch numbering before passing to Stream Gate or Stream Filter.

f9b89a46-bc5d-4f7a-9a6f-134f93ac3af9.errors: Wrong pattern syntax causes no remapping (data passes through unmodified). Mismatched index count between source and target patterns causes failure. Patterns are case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive.

3a710c1e-1809-4e19-8c15-82adce31cd62.name: Tree Branch
3a710c1e-1809-4e19-8c15-82adce31cd62.quick: Retrieves a single branch from a data tree by path | P must be a valid path (e.g., {0;1}) matching the tree structure
3a710c1e-1809-4e19-8c15-82adce31cd62.description: Retrieve a specific branch from a data tree.

contexts.extracting_specific_branch: Wire a data tree to T and a Path input to P; use Tree Statistics or Param Viewer first to identify valid paths; outputs the list of items at that branch
contexts.isolating_data_subset: Use after Explode Tree or alongside Tree Statistics to target a known path; P can be constructed with Path component; B outputs flat list from that branch only

3a710c1e-1809-4e19-8c15-82adce31cd62.errors: B is empty if P doesn't match any existing branch path; wrong path format or out-of-range indices silently return no data; ensure path exists using Tree Statistics first

99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.name: Tree Statistics
99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.quick: Returns all branch paths (P), item counts per branch (L), and total item count (C) for any data tree.
99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.description: Get some statistics regarding a data tree.

contexts.debugging_tree_structure: Wire any tree into T; outputs P (list of all paths), L (item count per branch), C (total items). Use before Tree Branch or Explode Tree to understand tree shape.
contexts.validating_data: Check C output to confirm expected total item count, or compare L values across branches to detect uneven data distributions before further tree operations.
contexts.inspecting_after_simplify_trim: After Simplify Tree or Trim Tree, feed result into Tree Statistics to confirm path structure changed as expected.

99bee19d-588c-41a0-b9b9-1d00fb03ea1a.errors: No errors likely; accepts Generic Data. Empty or null-heavy trees (before Clean Tree) may show unexpected L/C counts.

537b0419-bbc2-4ff4-bf08-afe526367b2c.name: Custom Preview
537b0419-bbc2-4ff4-bf08-afe526367b2c.quick: Custom Preview | Inputs: Geometry, Material → output

9c53bac0-ba66-40bd-8154-ce9829b9db1a.name: Colour Swatch
9c53bac0-ba66-40bd-8154-ce9829b9db1a.quick: Interactive color picker/swatch that outputs a single Color value | no inputs, color set via UI

contexts.custom_preview_coloring: Connect output Color to Custom Preview's 'Shader' input to apply a specific color to geometry previews; set color by double-clicking swatch in canvas
contexts.gradient_definition: Feed into Gradient component as color stops or use alongside Gradient to define fixed reference colors for blending workflows
contexts.color_parameter_input: Use as a named, visible color constant in canvas instead of hardcoding; Panel can label it for documentation clarity

9c53bac0-ba66-40bd-8154-ce9829b9db1a.errors: No inputs means no type mismatch errors; downstream failures occur if connected component expects System.Drawing.Color but receives mismatched type from incorrect wiring

3b220754-4114-4170-b6c3-b286b86ed524.name: Text Tag
3b220754-4114-4170-b6c3-b286b86ed524.quick: Displays 2D text tags at 3D points in Rhino viewport | Tags are flat/screen-facing, no geometry output
3b220754-4114-4170-b6c3-b286b86ed524.description: Represents a list of text tags in a Rhino viewport

contexts.labeling_points: Wire Point list to L, matching text strings to T; use Panel or concatenated strings. Tags appear screen-aligned at each point location.
contexts.colored_labels: Connect Split AHSL or Color Swatch to C input to color-code tags per item; list lengths of L, T, C must match.
contexts.debugging_lists: Pair with Point Order to verify point sequence; feed same point list to L and index/value strings to T for quick inspection.

3b220754-4114-4170-b6c3-b286b86ed524.errors: Null or mismatched list lengths between L and T cause missing or misaligned tags. Non-Point geometry at L will fail. No output — display only.

0ad9f1ab-2204-45bb-b282-474469e2fa7b.name: Point Order
0ad9f1ab-2204-45bb-b282-474469e2fa7b.quick: Visualizes index order of a point list in the viewport | display-only, no outputs
0ad9f1ab-2204-45bb-b282-474469e2fa7b.description: Displays the order of a list of points

contexts.debugging_point_lists: Wire a list of points to P; numbered labels appear in viewport showing sequence order. Useful alongside Point List or Text Tag to verify sorting/reordering operations.
contexts.verifying_curve_sampling: Connect sampled points from Divide Curve or similar to confirm point ordering matches expected direction before feeding into lofts or polylines.

0ad9f1ab-2204-45bb-b282-474469e2fa7b.errors: No outputs — cannot pass data downstream. Only accepts Point type; non-point geometry will fail. Empty or null list produces no display.

e87db220-a0a0-4d67-a405-f97fd14b2d7a.name: Linear Array
e87db220-a0a0-4d67-a405-f97fd14b2d7a.quick: Duplicates geometry N times along vector D | N includes original (count=1 gives no copies)
e87db220-a0a0-4d67-a405-f97fd14b2d7a.description: Create a linear array of geometry.

contexts.row_duplication: Connect geometry to G, unit or scaled vector to D, integer count to N; outputs arrayed geometry and transform list for downstream use
contexts.transform_reuse: X output provides per-copy transforms; pipe into Transform component to apply same spacing to other geometry without re-running array
contexts.spacing_control: Scale vector D before input to control spacing between copies; D defines both direction and step distance per copy

e87db220-a0a0-4d67-a405-f97fd14b2d7a.errors: N=0 or N=1 may produce empty or single-item output with no visible array; non-vector input to D causes type mismatch; null geometry in G propagates nulls through all copies

e521f7c8-92f4-481c-888b-eea109e3d6e9.name: Rectangular Array
e521f7c8-92f4-481c-888b-eea109e3d6e9.quick: Arrays geometry in a 2D rectangular grid defined by a Rectangle boundary, X and Y counts | Rectangle input sets grid extents
e521f7c8-92f4-481c-888b-eea109e3d6e9.description: Create a rectangular array of geometry.

contexts.grid_duplication: Wire geometry to G, a Rectangle to C defining the grid boundary, integers to X and Y for column/row counts; outputs arrayed geometry and transform list for downstream use
contexts.transform_reuse: Output X (Transform list) can drive other geometry through Transform component, reusing the same grid pattern without re-running the array
contexts.combining_arrays: Often paired with Linear Array or Box Array when 2D grid is needed vs. linear or volumetric distribution

e521f7c8-92f4-481c-888b-eea109e3d6e9.errors: <~30 tokens: Null output if C is not a valid Rectangle; X or Y count of 0 or 1 produces single row/column only; geometry type mismatches may cause silent failures>

fca5ad7e-ecac-401d-a357-edda0a251cbc.name: Polar Array
fca5ad7e-ecac-401d-a357-edda0a251cbc.quick: Rotates geometry N times around plane P's origin over angle A (degrees) | N includes original; A is total arc span
fca5ad7e-ecac-401d-a357-edda0a251cbc.description: Create a polar array of geometry.

contexts.radial_distribution: Connect geometry to G, define center plane P (origin = rotation center, Z = rotation axis), set N for count and A for total angle (e.g., 360 for full circle). Outputs arrayed geometry and transforms.
contexts.partial_arc_array: Set A less than 360 to distribute copies over a partial arc. N copies spaced evenly across A degrees. Use X output to apply same transforms to other geometry.
contexts.transform_reuse: X output provides Transform list; feed into Transform component to apply same polar pattern to secondary geometry without re-running array.

fca5ad7e-ecac-401d-a357-edda0a251cbc.errors: Wrong rotation axis: ensure plane P's Z-axis aligns with intended rotation axis. N=0 or N=1 produces no copies or just original. A=0 collapses all copies to same position.

9f6f954c-ba7b-4428-bf1e-1768cdff666c.name: Box Array
9f6f954c-ba7b-4428-bf1e-1768cdff666c.quick: Arrays geometry in 3D grid within a Box; X/Y/Z integers set count per axis | Box (C) defines the overall volume/orientation
9f6f954c-ba7b-4428-bf1e-1768cdff666c.description: Create a box array of geometry.

contexts.3d_grid_distribution: Connect geometry to G, a Box to C, and integers to X/Y/Z for count per axis. Output G gives all arrayed geometry; X gives transforms for reuse with other geometry.
contexts.transform_reuse: Output X (Transform list) can be applied to other geometry via Transform component, avoiding re-running the array for different objects.
contexts.oriented_arrays: Pair with Bounding Box to derive a fitting Box (C) from existing geometry, ensuring array aligns to geometry's local axes.

9f6f954c-ba7b-4428-bf1e-1768cdff666c.errors: Null output if C is not a valid Box or G is empty. X/Y/Z counts of 0 or negative likely produce no output. Non-integer inputs to X/Y/Z may cause type mismatch errors.

c6f23658-617f-4ac8-916d-d0d9e7241b25.name: Curve Array
c6f23658-617f-4ac8-916d-d0d9e7241b25.quick: Arrays geometry N times along a curve; N controls count of instances distributed along curve length
c6f23658-617f-4ac8-916d-d0d9e7241b25.description: Create an array of geometry along a curve.

contexts.distributing_objects_along_path: Connect source geometry to G, a curve to C, and integer count to N; outputs arrayed geometry and transform data for each instance position along curve
contexts.extracting_transforms: X output provides transform per instance; useful for orienting additional geometry or driving downstream operations without re-running array
contexts.combining_with_divide_curve: Divide Curve neighbor suggests N may align with division count; pairing both can synchronize spacing logic along same curve

c6f23658-617f-4ac8-916d-d0d9e7241b25.errors: Wrong N type (non-integer) causes failure; null or open/closed curve mismatch may produce unexpected spacing; N=0 or N=1 yields empty or single result; geometry must be valid non-null

378d0690-9da0-4dd1-ab16-1d15246e7c22.name: Orient
378d0690-9da0-4dd1-ab16-1d15246e7c22.quick: Remaps geometry from source plane A to target plane B (ChangeBasis transform) | both planes must be valid
378d0690-9da0-4dd1-ab16-1d15246e7c22.description: Orient an object. Orientation is sometimes called a 'ChangeBasis tranformation'. It allows for remapping of geometry from one axis-system to another.

contexts.place_geometry_on_surface: Connect geometry to G, define source plane A (often World XY or construction plane), connect target plane B from surface frame or Plane component; outputs reoriented geometry
contexts.reuse_transform: Output X (Transform matrix) can be fed into Transform component to apply same orient operation to other geometry without recomputing
contexts.align_to_normal: Use with Evaluate Surface to get normal-based plane as B; orient objects to follow surface curvature or direction

378d0690-9da0-4dd1-ab16-1d15246e7c22.errors: <~30 tokens: Null/invalid plane A or B causes failed transform; geometry not matching expected coordinate space if planes are misaligned or coincident

06d7bc4a-ba3e-4445-8ab5-079613b52f28.name: Project Along
06d7bc4a-ba3e-4445-8ab5-079613b52f28.quick: Projects geometry onto a plane along a specified direction vector | Direction D must not be parallel to plane P or projection fails
06d7bc4a-ba3e-4445-8ab5-079613b52f28.description: Project an object onto a plane along a direction.

contexts.oblique_shadow_projection: Wire geometry to G, define target plane P (e.g., ground plane), set D to sun/light direction vector; outputs projected geometry and transform X for reuse
contexts.directional_flattening: Use instead of standard Project when perpendicular projection is insufficient; D controls the projection angle, P defines the target surface plane
contexts.reusing_transform: Output X (Transform) can be fed into other transform components to apply the same oblique projection to additional geometry without recomputing

06d7bc4a-ba3e-4445-8ab5-079613b52f28.errors: Fails or produces degenerate results if D is parallel or near-parallel to plane P (no valid intersection); G must be projectable geometry (points, curves, surfaces); null D or P causes no output

5889b68f-fd88-4032-860f-869fb69654dd.name: Surface Morph
5889b68f-fd88-4032-860f-869fb69654dd.quick: Surface Morph | Inputs: G, R, S, U → G
5889b68f-fd88-4032-860f-869fb69654dd.description: Morph geometry into surface UVW coordinates

d8940ff0-dd4a-4e74-9361-54df537b50db.name: Box Morph
d8940ff0-dd4a-4e74-9361-54df537b50db.quick: Morphs geometry from a reference Box (R) into a Twisted Box (T) space | R must tightly match geometry's bounding region
d8940ff0-dd4a-4e74-9361-54df537b50db.description: Morph an object into a twisted box.

contexts.surface_paneling: Wire panel geometry to G, a bounding Box to R, and a Twisted Box (from Surface Box or Blend Box) to T; repeats geometry conforming to surface curvature
contexts.twisted_box_population: Chain with Twisted Box component: generate twisted boxes from corner points, feed to T; use original bounding box of source geometry as R
contexts.blend_morphing: Use Blend Box output as T to morph geometry smoothly between two surfaces; R should be axis-aligned box enclosing source geometry

d8940ff0-dd4a-4e74-9361-54df537b50db.errors: Geometry falls outside R box → distorted or clipped output; R not matching geometry extents causes incorrect morphing; T twisted box degenerate (zero volume) causes failure

539f5564-4fc0-4fc1-a7d3-b802fa2ef072.name: Bend Deform
539f5564-4fc0-4fc1-a7d3-b802fa2ef072.quick: Bends geometry along an Arc; Arc (B) defines the bend curve and extent | Arc input, not line or curve
539f5564-4fc0-4fc1-a7d3-b802fa2ef072.description: Deform a shape by bending it

contexts.bending_geometry_along_arc: Connect mesh/brep/solid to G, supply an Arc to B defining the bend path; geometry deforms to follow the arc's curvature. Pair with Arc component or arc from 3-point input.
contexts.morphing_pipeline: Used alongside Twist, Point Deform, or Spatial Deform for compound deformations; apply Bend Deform first, then layer additional morphing operations on the output G.

539f5564-4fc0-4fc1-a7d3-b802fa2ef072.errors: Fails or produces no deformation if B is not an Arc type (curves/lines rejected); geometry far from arc origin may deform unexpectedly or produce invalid geometry.

9509cb30-d24f-4f55-a5ac-bf0b12a06cfa.name: Twist
9509cb30-d24f-4f55-a5ac-bf0b12a06cfa.quick: Twists geometry around a Line axis by angle A | axis line direction and length matter for twist distribution
9509cb30-d24f-4f55-a5ac-bf0b12a06cfa.description: Deforms objects by twisting them around an axis.

contexts.twisting_column_or_tower: Feed brep/mesh as G, draw vertical Line X as axis, set angle A in degrees/radians; geometry wraps around axis proportionally along its length
contexts.parametric_twist_variation: Drive A with a Number Slider to animate twist amount; toggle I (Infinite) to extend axis influence beyond line endpoints; R likely controls angle units (radians vs degrees)
contexts.combining_with_other_morphs: Chain output G into Bend Deform or Taper for compound deformations; ensure geometry is cleanly meshed or joined before input to avoid seam artifacts

9509cb30-d24f-4f55-a5ac-bf0b12a06cfa.errors: Wrong angle units (radians vs degrees) causes unexpected over-twist; axis Line too short relative to geometry may clamp twist effect; null or open geometry in G can fail silently

ad0ee51e-c86f-4668-8de5-b55b850f6001.name: Taper
ad0ee51e-c86f-4668-8de5-b55b850f6001.quick: Deforms geometry toward/away from an axis line using start/end radii | R0 and R1 control taper scale at axis ends
ad0ee51e-c86f-4668-8de5-b55b850f6001.description: Deforms objects toward or away from an axis

contexts.basic_taper: Connect geometry to G, define axis with Line (X), set R0 (start radius/scale) and R1 (end radius/scale) as Numbers; geometry scales radially along axis
contexts.flat_taper: Toggle F (Flat) Boolean to constrain taper to a flat/planar deformation rather than radial; useful for wedge-like forms
contexts.infinite_axis: Toggle I (Infinite) Boolean to extend axis influence beyond line endpoints, affecting geometry outside the defined axis range
contexts.relative_scaling: Toggle R (Relative) Boolean to switch between absolute and relative radius interpretation; affects how R0/R1 values scale the geometry

ad0ee51e-c86f-4668-8de5-b55b850f6001.errors: Null output if X (Line) is invalid or zero-length; unexpected deformation if R0/R1 are zero or equal; geometry must overlap axis region when I is false

a4cd2751-414d-42ec-8916-476ebf62d7fe.name: Radians
a4cd2751-414d-42ec-8916-476ebf62d7fe.quick: Converts degrees to radians (D × π/180) | Use before trig functions that expect radians input
a4cd2751-414d-42ec-8916-476ebf62d7fe.description: Convert an angle specified in degrees to radians

contexts.trig_input_prep: Wire degree values (e.g., from sliders in 0–360 range) into D; output R feeds Sin, Cos, Tan or rotation components expecting radians
contexts.angle_conversion: Paired with Degrees component for round-trip conversion; D accepts any Number, including negative angles and values beyond 360

a4cd2751-414d-42ec-8916-476ebf62d7fe.errors: No type errors expected since input/output are both Numbers; logical errors occur if degrees are already in radians (double-converting), producing values ~57x too large

bb59bffc-f54c-4682-9778-f6c3fe74fce3.name: Arc
bb59bffc-f54c-4682-9778-f6c3fe74fce3.quick: Creates arc from plane, radius, and angle domain | angle domain in radians (e.g., 0 to Pi)
bb59bffc-f54c-4682-9778-f6c3fe74fce3.description: Create an arc defined by base plane, radius and angle domain.

contexts.basic_arc_construction: Connect a Plane (origin = center, X-axis = start direction), a Number for radius, and a Domain (e.g., 0 to 1.57) for angle span. Outputs Arc geometry and arc length L.
contexts.parametric_angle_control: Use Domain component or construct domain with two numbers to control arc sweep. Full semicircle = 0 to Pi; quarter = 0 to Pi/2. Angle domain drives arc extent.
contexts.oriented_arcs: Feed custom planes (e.g., from Plane Normal or rotated planes) to orient arcs in 3D space. Plane origin sets center point, plane orientation sets arc plane.

bb59bffc-f54c-4682-9778-f6c3fe74fce3.errors: Wrong angle units (degrees instead of radians) produces unexpected arc size. Zero or negative radius fails. Null plane defaults to world XY. Domain with equal start/end produces zero-length arc.

6e5de495-ba76-42d0-9985-a5c265e9aeca.name: Ruled Surface
6e5de495-ba76-42d0-9985-a5c265e9aeca.quick: Creates a ruled surface by linearly interpolating between two curves A and B | Both curves should have compatible parameterization
6e5de495-ba76-42d0-9985-a5c265e9aeca.description: Create a surface between two curves.

contexts.basic_lofting: Wire two curves into A and B; outputs a simple ruled (linear) surface. Unlike Loft, no options for tangency—strictly linear interpolation between the two curves.
contexts.architectural_panels: Use with lines or polylines as A and B to generate flat-ruled geometry. Useful when a developable or near-developable surface is needed between two rail curves.
contexts.comparison_with_edge_surface: Edge Surface accepts 2–4 curves and can blend smoothly; Ruled Surface is strictly linear between exactly two curves A and B, giving a simpler, more predictable result.

6e5de495-ba76-42d0-9985-a5c265e9aeca.errors: Fails or produces twisted surface if A and B have mismatched start/end directions or very different parameterizations; ensure curve domains and orientations are aligned.

2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.name: Interpolate
2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.quick: Creates interpolated NURBS curve through points | needs ≥2 points; degree D and knot style K affect shape
2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.description: Create an interpolated curve through a set of points.

contexts.basic_curve_through_points: Wire a list of Points into V; set D=3 for cubic curve; P=False for open, P=True for periodic/closed; outputs Curve C, length L, domain D
contexts.closed_periodic_curve: Set P=True to create a smooth closed loop through all input points; useful for organic closed shapes without manually matching endpoints
contexts.degree_and_knot_control: D controls curve degree (1=polyline, 3=smooth cubic); K sets knot style (0=uniform, 1=chord, 2=sqrt chord) affecting parameterization and point spacing influence

2b2a4145-3dff-41d4-a8de-1ea9d29eef33.errors: Fails with fewer than 2 points in V; degree D must be less than point count or curve won't solve; periodic mode P=True requires enough points to support chosen degree

d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.name: Circle CNR
d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.quick: Creates circle from center point, normal vector, and radius | Normal vector defines circle's plane orientation
d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.description: Create a circle defined by center, normal and radius.

contexts.oriented_circle: Wire a Point to C, a Vector (e.g., from Unit Z or surface normal) to N, and a Number to R; outputs a Circle lying in the plane defined by that normal at the center point
contexts.vs_base_plane_circle: Use Circle CNR when you have a point+vector pair rather than a full plane; avoids constructing a Plane component explicitly — normal vector alone sets orientation
contexts.downstream_use: Output Circle feeds into Extrude, Pipe, Loft, or Curve components; compatible anywhere a Circle/Curve is accepted

d114323a-e6ee-4164-946b-e4ca0ce15efa.errors: <~30 tokens: Zero-length normal vector causes invalid plane and failed circle; R≤0 produces degenerate output; mismatched data trees between C, N, R cause null items

d93100b6-d50b-40b2-831a-814659dc38e3.name: Rectangle
d93100b6-d50b-40b2-831a-814659dc38e3.quick: Rectangle | Inputs: Plane, X Size, Y Size → Rectangle

9fa1b081-b1c7-4a12-a163-0aa8da9ff6c4.name: Arc 3Pt
9fa1b081-b1c7-4a12-a163-0aa8da9ff6c4.quick: Creates arc through 3 points (A=start, B=mid, C=end); outputs geometry, plane, and radius | points must not be collinear
9fa1b081-b1c7-4a12-a163-0aa8da9ff6c4.description: Create an arc through three points.

contexts.basic_arc_construction: Wire three Point params to A, B, C; arc passes through all three in order. Output A gives the arc curve for further use in curves/surfaces.
contexts.extracting_arc_properties: Use P output (plane) to get arc orientation/center, R output (number) for radius — useful for driving other geometry like Circle or Arc components.
contexts.replacing_circle_3pt: Similar to Circle 3Pt but produces an arc segment rather than full circle; use when only a partial curve through 3 points is needed.

9fa1b081-b1c7-4a12-a163-0aa8da9ff6c4.errors: Fails or returns null if three points are collinear (no unique arc exists). Duplicate points also cause failure. Ensure points are distinct and non-collinear.

dde71aef-d6ed-40a6-af98-6b0673983c82.name: Nurbs Curve
dde71aef-d6ed-40a6-af98-6b0673983c82.quick: Builds NURBS curve from control points (V), degree (D), periodic toggle (P) | degree must be < point count
dde71aef-d6ed-40a6-af98-6b0673983c82.description: Construct a nurbs curve from control points.

contexts.basic_curve_construction: Feed Point list into V, set D (typically 3 for cubic), P=False for open curve; outputs Curve, Length, Domain. Minimum points = degree+1.
contexts.periodic_closed_curve: Set P=True to create smooth closed periodic curve without sharp seam; control points wrap continuously. Useful for closed profiles.
contexts.downstream_operations: Output C feeds Sub Curve for domain trimming, Tween Curve for morphing between shapes, or Iso Curve workflows on surfaces.

dde71aef-d6ed-40a6-af98-6b0673983c82.errors: <degree+1 points causes failure; D=1 gives polyline-like result; mismatched data trees produce per-branch curves or nulls>

30ce59ce-22a1-49ee-9e21-e6d16b3684a8.name: Bezier Span
30ce59ce-22a1-49ee-9e21-e6d16b3684a8.quick: Builds a cubic Bezier curve from two endpoints (A, B) and their tangent vectors (At, Bt) | tangent magnitude affects curve shape
30ce59ce-22a1-49ee-9e21-e6d16b3684a8.description: Construct a bezier span from endpoints and tangents.

contexts.smooth_curve_between_points: Wire two Points to A/B and Vectors to At/Bt; outputs Curve C ready for further operations. Tangent direction and length control bulge/curvature.
contexts.chaining_spans: Connect B/Bt of one span to A/At of next to build G1-continuous polyBezier. Ensure tangents are collinear at joints for smooth continuity.
contexts.length_and_domain: L gives arc length as Number; D gives parameter domain — useful for reparameterization or dividing the span downstream.

30ce59ce-22a1-49ee-9e21-e6d16b3684a8.errors: <~30 tokens: Null curve if A equals B (zero-length span); zero-length tangent vectors produce degenerate or straight segment with no curvature.

429cbba9-55ee-4e84-98ea-876c44db879a.name: Sub Curve
429cbba9-55ee-4e84-98ea-876c44db879a.quick: Extracts a portion of a curve using a domain (t-value range) | Domain must be within curve's natural domain
429cbba9-55ee-4e84-98ea-876c44db879a.description: Construct a curve from the sub-domain of a base curve.

contexts.trimming_curve_segment: Wire a base Curve into C and a Domain (e.g., from Construct Domain or Curve Domain component) into D; outputs the sub-curve spanning that parameter range. Useful for isolating segments.
contexts.reparameterized_curves: If curve is reparameterized (0-1 domain), supply a sub-domain like {0.25, 0.75} to extract the middle half. Pair with Reparameterize or Curve Domain to get valid bounds.
contexts.animation_or_partial_curves: Drive D with a number slider or expression to animate which portion of the curve is extracted; useful for progressive reveal or partial lofting workflows.

429cbba9-55ee-4e84-98ea-876c44db879a.errors: Fails or returns null if Domain D falls outside the curve's actual parameter domain; empty output if D is zero-length or inverted (start > end).

d1d57181-d594-41e8-8efb-041e29f8a5ca.name: Iso Curve
d1d57181-d594-41e8-8efb-041e29f8a5ca.quick: Iso Curve | Inputs: Surface, UV point → U Isocurve

d0a1b843-873d-4d1d-965c-b5423b35f327.name: Connect Curves
d0a1b843-873d-4d1d-965c-b5423b35f327.quick: Connects a sequence of curves into one | G controls continuity type, L toggles loop closure, B sets blend radius

contexts.chaining_open_curves: Wire list of open curves to C; set G (0=position, 1=tangent, 2=curvature) for join continuity; outputs single connected curve
contexts.closing_loop: Set L=True to connect last curve back to first, forming closed loop; useful after Polygon or Arc sequences
contexts.blended_connections: Use B (number) to control blend/fillet radius at connection points; larger B creates smoother transitions between curve segments

d0a1b843-873d-4d1d-965c-b5423b35f327.errors: Fails or produces gaps if input curves are not ordered sequentially; mismatched curve directions can cause unexpected geometry; B=0 may produce sharp kinks regardless of G setting

439a55a5-2f9e-4f66-9de2-32f24fec2ef5.name: Plane Surface
439a55a5-2f9e-4f66-9de2-32f24fec2ef5.quick: Plane Surface | Inputs: Plane, X Size, Y Size → Plane

3e6bb383-d3dc-4bd2-b44d-d47b5a5d3e45.name: Pipe Variable
3e6bb383-d3dc-4bd2-b44d-d47b5a5d3e45.quick: Creates pipe surface with variable radii along a rail curve | t params and R radii must match in count
3e6bb383-d3dc-4bd2-b44d-d47b5a5d3e45.description: Create a pipe surface with variable radii around a rail curve.

contexts.variable_radius_pipe: Wire C (rail curve), paired t (parameter 0-1 along curve) and R (radius values) lists — count must match. E controls end cap type (0=none,1=flat,2=round). Fr toggles fitting. Outputs closed Brep.
contexts.tapering_tube: Use Graph Mapper or manual number lists to define t positions and corresponding R values for tapered or organic tube shapes along any curve path.
contexts.capping_control: Set E integer to control end caps: connect Integer component or panel. Combine with Brep tools for boolean operations on resulting pipe geometry.

3e6bb383-d3dc-4bd2-b44d-d47b5a5d3e45.errors: Mismatch between t and R list lengths causes failure. Invalid curve (null/open when closed expected) or zero/negative radii will produce no output.

57b2184c-8931-4e70-9220-612ec5b3809a.name: Patch
57b2184c-8931-4e70-9220-612ec5b3809a.quick: Fits a surface through curves and/or points | S (spans) controls resolution; more spans = better fit but heavier

contexts.closing_open_boundary: Wire one or more closed or open curves into C; optionally add guide Points P; S sets span count (default ~10); F is flexibility/stiffness number controlling how tightly surface fits
contexts.point_cloud_surfacing: Feed scattered points into P with no curves; Patch interpolates a surface through them; increase S for denser fit
contexts.trimmed_surface_fill: Use boundary curves from naked edges of a Brep as C input to fill holes; T (trim) boolean controls whether output is trimmed to boundary

57b2184c-8931-4e70-9220-612ec5b3809a.errors: Too few spans (S) causes poor fit to complex curves; non-planar or self-intersecting curves in C may produce twisted patches; very high S values slow computation; mismatched curve/point data types cause null surface output

36132830-e2ef-4476-8ea1-6a43922344f0.name: Edge Surface
36132830-e2ef-4476-8ea1-6a43922344f0.quick: Creates a surface from 2–4 edge curves (A–D); curves must form a closed boundary | order matters for surface shape
36132830-e2ef-4476-8ea1-6a43922344f0.description: Create a surface from two, three or four edge curves.

contexts.two_curves: Wire two curves into A and B; similar to Ruled Surface but uses edge-fitting logic. Good for simple lofted panels.
contexts.three_curves: Provide A, B, C for a triangular-boundary surface. Useful for irregular panels where one edge degenerates to a point.
contexts.four_curves: Wire four boundary curves into A, B, C, D forming a closed loop. Common for quad panels; curves should meet at endpoints for clean Brep output.
contexts.comparison_with_neighbors: Prefer Edge Surface over Ruled Surface when edges don't share the same parameterization; use Network Surface when interior curves are also needed.

36132830-e2ef-4476-8ea1-6a43922344f0.errors: Fails or produces bad geometry if curves don't meet at endpoints, leaving gaps. With only one curve wired, no surface is created. Curve order/orientation mismatch causes twisted surfaces.

38a5638b-6d01-4417-bf11-976d925f8a71.name: Extrude Along
38a5638b-6d01-4417-bf11-976d925f8a71.quick: Extrudes curves/surfaces along a guide curve path → Brep | Guide curve shape drives the extrusion direction and profile.
38a5638b-6d01-4417-bf11-976d925f8a71.description: Extrude curves and surfaces along a curve.

contexts.profile_along_path: Connect a profile curve or surface to B and a rail/path curve to C; outputs swept Brep. Similar to Sweep1 but treats B as cross-section extruded along C.
contexts.surface_extrusion: Feed a planar surface into B with a curved path in C to generate a thick swept solid Brep; useful for ribbon or band geometry.
contexts.comparing_to_sweep: Unlike Sweep1, Extrude Along maintains the cross-section orientation relative to the path without rail alignment options; simpler but less controllable.

38a5638b-6d01-4417-bf11-976d925f8a71.errors: Fails if B is not a valid curve or surface geometry; open/non-planar inputs may produce invalid Brep. Null or degenerate C curve causes no output.

71506fa8-9bf0-432d-b897-b2e0c5ac316c.name: Network Surface
71506fa8-9bf0-432d-b897-b2e0c5ac316c.quick: Creates a NURBS surface from U and V curve networks; C controls continuity/fitting tolerance
71506fa8-9bf0-432d-b897-b2e0c5ac316c.description: Create a surface from curve networks

contexts.curve_network_surfacing: Wire multiple U-direction curves to U and multiple V-direction curves to V; curves must intersect properly. C integer sets continuity (0=position, 1=tangent, 2=curvature). Output S is a single NURBS surface fitted through the network.
contexts.complex_freeform_surfaces: Use when Edge Surface (2-4 curves) is insufficient; Network Surface handles many crossing curves. Pair with Divide Curve or interpolated curves to build the U/V network from point data.

71506fa8-9bf0-432d-b897-b2e0c5ac316c.errors: Fails if U and V curves don't intersect or are non-planar in incompatible ways; mismatched curve directions cause twisted output; C value out of valid range may error or produce poor fit

c77a8b3b-c569-4d81-9b59-1c27299a1c45.name: 4Point Surface
c77a8b3b-c569-4d81-9b59-1c27299a1c45.quick: Creates a surface from 3 or 4 corner points; D is optional for triangular surface
c77a8b3b-c569-4d81-9b59-1c27299a1c45.description: Create a surface connecting three or four corner points.

contexts.quad_surface: Wire 4 Point params to A, B, C, D corners — order matters, points should form a logical quad (not self-intersecting) to get a clean bilinear surface
contexts.triangular_surface: Leave D disconnected; A, B, C define a planar or non-planar triangular surface patch
contexts.base_for_further_ops: Output S feeds into Surface ops like Divide Surface, Evaluate Surface, or Edge Surface for further modeling

c77a8b3b-c569-4d81-9b59-1c27299a1c45.errors: Self-intersecting or non-sequential point order produces twisted/degenerate surface; coincident points collapse surface; all 4 points coplanar gives flat result which may cause issues in downstream curvature ops

8efd5eb9-a896-486e-9f98-d8d1a07a49f3.name: Extrude Linear
8efd5eb9-a896-486e-9f98-d8d1a07a49f3.quick: Extrudes curves/surfaces along a straight line path → Brep | requires Line input (A) for direction/distance
8efd5eb9-a896-486e-9f98-d8d1a07a49f3.description: Extrude curves and surfaces along a straight path.

contexts.curve_extrusion: Connect a curve to P, provide a Line to A for direction and length; Po and Ao are optional orientation planes. Outputs closed or open Brep wall.
contexts.surface_thickening: Feed a surface into P with a Line A perpendicular to it to extrude into a solid Brep; useful before Boolean ops.
contexts.directional_control: Use Po/Ao plane inputs to orient the extrusion relative to a local coordinate system rather than world axes.

8efd5eb9-a896-486e-9f98-d8d1a07a49f3.errors: Null output if P is not a curve or surface (e.g., raw point/mesh). Line A must be valid and non-zero length. Missing A input causes no extrusion. Unlike Extrude Along, path must be straight.

0a391eac-5048-443c-9c1b-f592299b6dd6.name: Mesh Sphere
0a391eac-5048-443c-9c1b-f592299b6dd6.quick: Creates a mesh sphere from a base plane, radius, and U/V subdivisions | U/V control polygon density

contexts.basic_sphere: Connect a Plane (or use default World XY), a Number for radius R, and Integers for U and V subdivision counts → outputs a triangulated/quad Mesh sphere ready for analysis or rendering
contexts.subdivision_control: U sets longitude divisions, V sets latitude divisions; low values (e.g. U=6, V=6) give coarse mesh, higher values give smoother approximation; feed Integer sliders for interactive control
contexts.comparison_with_ex: Use Mesh Sphere Ex (neighbor) for square-patch topology; use this component for standard UV-sphere topology with triangular poles

0a391eac-5048-443c-9c1b-f592299b6dd6.errors: Null output if R ≤ 0 or U/V < 3; degenerate mesh if U or V too low (minimum ~3–4 recommended); non-integer U/V inputs may be auto-cast but unexpected values can cause errors

5723c845-cafc-442d-a667-8c76532845e6.name: Solid Intersection
5723c845-cafc-442d-a667-8c76532845e6.quick: Returns only the overlapping volume between two Brep sets | both inputs must be closed (solid) Breps
5723c845-cafc-442d-a667-8c76532845e6.description: Perform a solid intersection on two Brep sets.

contexts.boolean_intersection: Wire two closed Breps into A and B; outputs the shared solid volume. Pair with Solid Union/Difference for full boolean workflow. Both Breps must be valid, closed solids.
contexts.clipping_to_boundary: Use a bounding solid as B to clip geometry in A to a defined region. Output R is the portion of A inside B.

5723c845-cafc-442d-a667-8c76532845e6.errors: <~30 tokens: Open or invalid Breps return null/empty R. Non-manifold geometry or self-intersecting surfaces commonly cause failures.

4fe828e8-fa95-4cc5-9a8c-c33856ecc783.name: Brep | Plane
4fe828e8-fa95-4cc5-9a8c-c33856ecc783.quick: Intersects a Brep with a plane (section cut); outputs intersection curves C and points P | no output if plane misses Brep
4fe828e8-fa95-4cc5-9a8c-c33856ecc783.description: Solve intersection events for a Brep and a plane (otherwise known as section).

contexts.section_cut: Wire a Brep solid/surface to B, a constructed XY/custom Plane to P; C returns cross-section curves usable for further analysis or drawing
contexts.contour_slicing: Drive P with a series of offset planes (e.g., from Series + Plane components) to generate multiple section curves across a Brep for contour mapping
contexts.point_extraction: P output captures isolated intersection points where plane meets Brep edges/vertices; useful for locating specific geometry intersections

4fe828e8-fa95-4cc5-9a8c-c33856ecc783.errors: Returns null/empty if plane does not intersect Brep geometry; open Breps may yield partial or unclosed curves; ensure Brep is valid (use IsValid check) to avoid failed intersections

3b112fb6-3eba-42d2-ba75-0f903c18faab.name: Contour
3b112fb6-3eba-42d2-ba75-0f903c18faab.quick: Contour | Inputs: Shape, Point, Direction → Contours

3ac8e589-37f5-477d-aa61-6699702c5728.name: Rotate Axis
3ac8e589-37f5-477d-aa61-6699702c5728.quick: Rotates geometry around a Line axis by angle (radians) | axis is a Line, not a vector+point
3ac8e589-37f5-477d-aa61-6699702c5728.description: Rotate an object around an axis.

contexts.spin_around_line: Wire geometry to G, a Line to X (defines axis origin+direction), angle in radians to A; outputs transformed geometry and reusable Transform
contexts.reuse_transform: Output X (Transform) can be fed to other transform components to apply same rotation to multiple objects without recomputing
contexts.vs_rotate3d: Use Rotate Axis when axis is already a Line; use Rotate 3D when you have a center point + separate axis vector

3ac8e589-37f5-477d-aa61-6699702c5728.errors: <~30 tokens: Angle must be in radians (not degrees); null/invalid Line on X causes no rotation or error; geometry must be valid

9c007a04-d0d9-48e4-9da3-9ba142bc4d46.name: Subtraction
9c007a04-d0d9-48e4-9da3-9ba142bc4d46.quick: Subtracts B from A (A - B) | Generic inputs accept numbers, vectors, or compatible types

contexts.numeric_arithmetic: Wire Number or Integer params to A and B; outputs R = A - B. Chain with Multiplication or Power for compound expressions.
contexts.vector_offset: Connect Point/Vector to A and a numeric or vector to B to shift geometry values. Works alongside Addition for bidirectional offsets.
contexts.boolean_logic_adjacent: Used near Gate Not/Xor for mixed numeric-boolean workflows; ensure inputs are numeric, not boolean, to avoid type mismatch.

9c007a04-d0d9-48e4-9da3-9ba142bc4d46.errors: Type mismatch if A and B are incompatible (e.g., text vs number). List length mismatch triggers item-matching warnings. Null inputs produce null output R.

78fed580-851b-46fe-af2f-6519a9d378e0.name: Power
78fed580-851b-46fe-af2f-6519a9d378e0.quick: Computes A^B (A raised to power B) | both inputs accept numbers; negative base with fractional exponent returns NaN
78fed580-851b-46fe-af2f-6519a9d378e0.description: Raise a value to a power.

contexts.scaling_geometry: Feed a numeric value into A and exponent into B; wire output R into multiplication or other math ops for non-linear scaling curves
contexts.curve_parameterization: Use Power to apply polynomial relationships; chain with Subtraction or Multiplication for custom easing or falloff functions
contexts.boolean_context: Avoid: inputs A/B are Generic Data but expect numeric types; boolean or non-numeric data from Gate components will cause null/error output

78fed580-851b-46fe-af2f-6519a9d378e0.errors: Null output if A or B are non-numeric (e.g., boolean from Gate components). Negative A with non-integer B produces NaN. Zero base with negative exponent causes division-by-zero.

431bc610-8ae1-4090-b217-1a9d9c519fe2.name: Modulus
431bc610-8ae1-4090-b217-1a9d9c519fe2.quick: Returns remainder of A divided by B (A mod B) | B=0 causes division error
431bc610-8ae1-4090-b217-1a9d9c519fe2.description: Divides two numbers and returns only the remainder.

contexts.pattern_cycling: Feed integer index as A, cycle length as B to wrap values; wire integer outputs from Series or Range into A, constant integer into B
contexts.even_odd_check: Connect integer input to A, B=2; R=0 means even, R=1 means odd; combine with Equality or conditional logic
contexts.grid_tiling: Use with integer coordinates to tile or repeat patterns; chain with Multiplication and Subtraction to reconstruct quotient

431bc610-8ae1-4090-b217-1a9d9c519fe2.errors: B=0 causes divide-by-zero, returning null/error; non-numeric Generic Data inputs will fail — ensure upstream values resolve to numbers; floating-point inputs return fractional remainders which may surprise if integers are expected

28124995-cf99-4298-b6f4-c75a8e379f18.name: Absolute
28124995-cf99-4298-b6f4-c75a8e379f18.quick: Returns absolute value of input | works on numbers; non-numeric input will fail
28124995-cf99-4298-b6f4-c75a8e379f18.description: Compute the absolute of a value.

contexts.distance_or_magnitude: Wire numeric output (e.g., from Subtraction) into x to ensure non-negative result; useful before Power or Multiplication to avoid sign issues
contexts.error_checking: Use after subtraction to get unsigned difference between two values; chain with other math_operators for further processing

28124995-cf99-4298-b6f4-c75a8e379f18.errors: Non-numeric Generic Data (e.g., text, geometry) passed to x will cause null/error output; boolean inputs from Gate components likely unsupported

30d58600-1aab-42db-80a3-f1ea6c4269a0.name: Larger Than
30d58600-1aab-42db-80a3-f1ea6c4269a0.quick: Larger Than | Inputs: First Number, Second Number → Larger than

ae840986-cade-4e5a-96b0-570f007d4fc0.name: Smaller Than
ae840986-cade-4e5a-96b0-570f007d4fc0.quick: Smaller Than | Inputs: First Number, Second Number → Smaller than

5db0fb89-4f22-4f09-a777-fa5e55aed7ec.name: Equality
5db0fb89-4f22-4f09-a777-fa5e55aed7ec.quick: Tests if two numbers are equal | outputs both = (true if equal) and ≠ (true if not equal) simultaneously

contexts.filtering_equal_values: Wire two Number params to A and B; = output drives filtering logic. Often paired with Gate Not or Gate Xor for conditional branching.
contexts.inequality_check: ≠ output directly gives inverse result without needing Gate Not; use when checking if values differ, e.g., filtering duplicate coordinates.
contexts.arithmetic_comparison: Combine with Subtraction: subtract A-B and check if result equals zero as alternative approach; Equality is more direct for exact match checks.

5db0fb89-4f22-4f09-a777-fa5e55aed7ec.errors: Floating-point precision issues: two nearly-equal numbers may return false due to decimal rounding; use Subtraction + threshold comparison instead of direct equality for computed values.

5b850221-b527-4bd6-8c62-e94168cd6efa.name: Mass Addition
5b850221-b527-4bd6-8c62-e94168cd6efa.quick: Sums all items in a list; outputs total (R) and running partial sums (Pr)
5b850221-b527-4bd6-8c62-e94168cd6efa.description: Perform mass addition of a list of items

contexts.summing_a_list: Connect a list of numbers to I; R returns the total sum, Pr returns cumulative partial sums at each step — useful for running totals or prefix sums
contexts.aggregating_geometry_or_values: Accepts Generic Data, so can handle numbers, vectors, or other addable types; wire output of Series or other list-generating components directly into I

5b850221-b527-4bd6-8c62-e94168cd6efa.errors: Fails if input items are non-addable types (e.g., text, surfaces). Empty list input yields null output. Mixed types in list likely cause type mismatch errors.

040f195d-0b4e-4fe0-901f-fedb2fd3db15.name: Gate And
040f195d-0b4e-4fe0-901f-fedb2fd3db15.quick: Boolean AND gate: outputs True only when both A and B are True | both inputs must be Boolean

contexts.filtering_logic: Wire two condition outputs (e.g., from comparison components) into A and B; R drives culling or branching — all conditions must pass simultaneously
contexts.combining_gates: Chain with Gate Not, Gate Or, Gate Xor to build compound logic expressions; R feeds next gate's input as Boolean

040f195d-0b4e-4fe0-901f-fedb2fd3db15.errors: Non-Boolean inputs cause type conversion issues; null or missing input defaults to False, making R always False unexpectedly

cfb6b17f-ca82-4f5d-b604-d4f69f569de3.name: Plane Normal
cfb6b17f-ca82-4f5d-b604-d4f69f569de3.quick: Creates a plane perpendicular to a vector Z at origin O; X/Y axes are auto-computed from Z direction.
cfb6b17f-ca82-4f5d-b604-d4f69f569de3.description: Create a plane perpendicular to a vector.

contexts.orient_geometry: Wire a Point (O) and Vector (Z) to define a plane whose normal aligns with Z; useful for orienting objects along custom directions like surface normals.
contexts.custom_plane_from_direction: Pair with Vector components or surface normal outputs to build planes at specific locations; X/Y axes are arbitrary but consistent, unlike Construct Plane which requires explicit axes.

cfb6b17f-ca82-4f5d-b604-d4f69f569de3.errors: Fails if Z is a zero-length vector. Ambiguous X/Y axes when Z is near world Z-axis — use Construct Plane for explicit axis control.

c98a6015-7a2f-423c-bc66-bdc505249b45.name: Plane 3Pt
c98a6015-7a2f-423c-bc66-bdc505249b45.quick: Creates a plane through 3 points (A=origin, B defines X-axis, C defines Y direction) | Points must not be collinear
c98a6015-7a2f-423c-bc66-bdc505249b45.description: Create a plane through three points.

contexts.custom_orientation: Wire 3 non-collinear points: A as origin, B along desired X direction, C in XY plane region; outputs Plane for transforms, Orient, or surface operations
contexts.surface_normal_plane: Extract points from a surface or mesh face, feed into A/B/C to define a local coordinate plane aligned to geometry
contexts.deconstruct_verify: Pipe output Pl into Deconstruct Plane to inspect origin and axes, confirming orientation before using in downstream transforms

c98a6015-7a2f-423c-bc66-bdc505249b45.errors: Fails or returns invalid plane if A, B, C are collinear (no unique plane defined); coincident points (A=B or A=C) also cause failure

56b92eab-d121-43f7-94d3-6cd8f0ddead8.name: Vector XYZ
56b92eab-d121-43f7-94d3-6cd8f0ddead8.quick: Vector XYZ | Inputs: X component, Y component, Z component → Vector

a50fcd4a-cf42-4c3f-8616-022761e6cc93.name: Deconstruct Vector
a50fcd4a-cf42-4c3f-8616-022761e6cc93.quick: Splits a vector into X, Y, Z number components | Input must be a Vector type, not a point
a50fcd4a-cf42-4c3f-8616-022761e6cc93.description: Deconstruct a vector into its component parts.

contexts.extracting_components: Wire any Vector (from Vector 2Pt, Unit Vector, or Vector XYZ) into V; outputs X, Y, Z as Numbers for math or filtering operations
contexts.roundtrip_with_vectorxyz: Deconstruct → modify individual X/Y/Z values → feed back into Vector XYZ to rebuild a transformed vector
contexts.length_check: Pair with Vector Length to verify magnitude while also accessing individual axis values separately

a50fcd4a-cf42-4c3f-8616-022761e6cc93.errors: Fails if a Point is wired instead of a Vector — use Deconstruct Point for points. Null vector input yields null X/Y/Z outputs.

7a218bfb-b93d-4c1f-83d3-5a0b909dd60b.name: Replace Items
7a218bfb-b93d-4c1f-83d3-5a0b909dd60b.quick: Replaces items in list L at indices i with new items I; W (wrap) controls index wrapping behavior.
7a218bfb-b93d-4c1f-83d3-5a0b909dd60b.description: Replace certain items in a list.

contexts.targeted_substitution: Wire source list to L, replacement values to I, integer indices to i. W=True wraps out-of-range indices. Outputs modified list with specified positions replaced.
contexts.conditional_update: Use with Boolean/filter logic upstream to compute which indices i need replacement. Pair with List Item to extract originals before replacing.
contexts.multi_item_replace: I and i accept multiple values; matching counts replace corresponding indexed positions in L simultaneously.

7a218bfb-b93d-4c1f-83d3-5a0b909dd60b.errors: Index out of range if i exceeds list length and W=False. Mismatched counts between I and i may cause partial replacement or null items. Wrong data type at I may cause downstream type errors.

36947590-f0cb-4807-a8f9-9c90c9b20621.name: Cross Reference
36947590-f0cb-4807-a8f9-9c90c9b20621.quick: Cross Reference | Inputs: List (A), List (B) → List (A)

8440fd1b-b6e0-4bdb-aa93-4ec295c213e9.name: Longest List
8440fd1b-b6e0-4bdb-aa93-4ec295c213e9.quick: Pads shorter lists to match longest list length by repeating last item | both outputs same length
8440fd1b-b6e0-4bdb-aa93-4ec295c213e9.description: Grow a collection of lists to the longest length amongst them

contexts.parallel_data_matching: Wire two lists of different lengths into A and B; outputs repeat last item of shorter list until lengths match, enabling parallel operations like point-curve pairing
contexts.pre_processing_before_operations: Use before math or geometry operations requiring matched list lengths; connect outputs directly to downstream components expecting equal-length inputs

8440fd1b-b6e0-4bdb-aa93-4ec295c213e9.errors: If one input is empty, output may be empty or single-item repeated; no true null-padding — last item repeats, which can cause unintended data duplication if lists differ greatly in length

5a13ec19-e4e9-43da-bf65-f93025fa87ca.name: Shortest List
5a13ec19-e4e9-43da-bf65-f93025fa87ca.quick: Trims all input lists to match the shortest one's length | both A and B outputs are truncated equally
5a13ec19-e4e9-43da-bf65-f93025fa87ca.description: Shrink a collection of lists to the shortest length amongst them

contexts.syncing_parallel_lists: Wire two lists of different lengths into A and B; outputs both trimmed to shorter length. Useful before pairing points with curves or values with geometry to avoid null mismatches.
contexts.preprocessing_before_operations: Place before Sort List, Shift List, or Partition List when input lists may have unequal counts. Ensures downstream components receive matched-length data without index errors.
contexts.multi_list_alignment: Accepts generic data, so works with any type — numbers, curves, surfaces. Pair with Longest List (similar component) when padding is preferred over trimming.

5a13ec19-e4e9-43da-bf65-f93025fa87ca.errors: If one list is empty, all outputs become empty. No warning is raised — silent data loss. Excess items in the longer list are permanently discarded with no remainder output.

dd8134c0-109b-4012-92be-51d843edfff7.name: Duplicate Data
dd8134c0-109b-4012-92be-51d843edfff7.quick: Duplicates entire data input N times; O likely controls order/flattening of output list
dd8134c0-109b-4012-92be-51d843edfff7.description: Duplicate data a predefined number of times.

contexts.repeat_list: Connect any data to D, integer count to N; outputs N copies of D concatenated — useful before Cull Pattern or masking operations
contexts.sequence_building: Pair with Char Sequence or Random to repeat base sequences N times before further filtering with Cull Index
contexts.stack_vs_duplicate: Unlike Stack Data (duplicates individual items in-place), Duplicate Data repeats the whole dataset N times as a block

dd8134c0-109b-4012-92be-51d843edfff7.errors: N=0 or negative returns empty output; O boolean likely toggles between appended vs interleaved order — wrong O setting causes unexpected list structure

2ab17f9a-d852-4405-80e1-938c5e57e78d.name: Random
2ab17f9a-d852-4405-80e1-938c5e57e78d.quick: Random | Inputs: Range, Number, Seed → Random

74cad441-2264-45fe-a57d-85034751208a.name: Explode Tree
74cad441-2264-45fe-a57d-85034751208a.quick: Extracts all branches from a data tree as separate outputs; output count matches branch count dynamically.
74cad441-2264-45fe-a57d-85034751208a.description: Extract all the branches from a tree

contexts.accessing_all_branches: Connect any data tree to D; each branch becomes a separate named output (-). Useful when downstream components need individual branch lists rather than a tree structure.
contexts.debugging_trees: Pair with Tree Statistics to know branch count first, then use Explode Tree to inspect each branch individually. Works alongside Simplify Tree to reduce path complexity before exploding.
contexts.flattening_workflow: Use before operations that require flat lists per branch. Unlike Flatten, preserves branch separation — each output is one branch's items.

74cad441-2264-45fe-a57d-85034751208a.errors: Output count is dynamic and matches branch count; if tree has many branches, panel becomes unwieldy. Connecting a flat list (single branch) yields only one output. Null/invalid items in branches pass through — use Clean Tree first if needed.

86866576-6cc0-485a-9cd2-6f7d493f57f7.name: Merge
86866576-6cc0-485a-9cd2-6f7d493f57f7.quick: Combines two data streams (A+B) into one output S; preserves tree structure of both inputs.

contexts.combining_lists: Wire two lists or trees into A and B; output S contains both as merged branches. Use when consolidating geometry or values from two sources before further processing.
contexts.tree_management: Pair with Stream Filter or Stream Gate to selectively merge/split streams. Merged output maintains original branch paths from A and B.
contexts.scaling_up: For more than two streams, use Merge 03, Merge 10, or Merge Multiple instead — this component only accepts exactly two inputs.

86866576-6cc0-485a-9cd2-6f7d493f57f7.errors: Mismatched tree structures may cause unexpected branch indexing in S. If more than two streams needed, wrong component — use Merge Multiple. Empty inputs produce empty or partial output.

353b206e-bde5-4f02-a913-b3b8a977d4b9.name: Evaluate Surface
353b206e-bde5-4f02-a913-b3b8a977d4b9.quick: Evaluate Surface | Inputs: Surface, Point → Point

2dc44b22-b1dd-460a-a704-6462d6e91096.name: Curve Closest Point
2dc44b22-b1dd-460a-a704-6462d6e91096.quick: Curve Closest Point | Inputs: Point, Curve → Point

4a9e9a8e-0943-4438-b360-129c30f2bb0f.name: Surface Closest Point
4a9e9a8e-0943-4438-b360-129c30f2bb0f.quick: Surface Closest Point | Inputs: Point, Surface → Point

571ca323-6e55-425a-bf9e-ee103c7ba4b9.name: Closest Point
571ca323-6e55-425a-bf9e-ee103c7ba4b9.quick: Finds single closest point in collection C to query point P | returns matched point, its index, and distance
571ca323-6e55-425a-bf9e-ee103c7ba4b9.description: Find closest point in a point collection.

contexts.nearest_neighbor_lookup: Wire query point to P, point list/cloud to C; outputs closest point geometry, its index i for list item retrieval, and distance D as number
contexts.distance_filtering: Use output D (Number) to threshold or sort; pair with List Item using index i to retrieve associated data from parallel lists
contexts.vs_closest_points: Use this for single closest result; use 'Closest Points' neighbor when multiple nearest neighbors are needed

571ca323-6e55-425a-bf9e-ee103c7ba4b9.errors: <~30 tokens: Null output if C is empty list; mismatched data trees between P and C cause unintended cross-matching; D is Euclidean 3D distance

4beead95-8aa2-4613-8bb9-24758a0f5c4c.name: Brep Closest Point
4beead95-8aa2-4613-8bb9-24758a0f5c4c.quick: Finds closest point on a Brep surface | outputs point, normal vector, and distance
4beead95-8aa2-4613-8bb9-24758a0f5c4c.description: Find the closest point on a brep

contexts.proximity_analysis: Wire a Point (P) and Brep (B); outputs closest surface point, face normal (N), and distance (D). Useful for projecting points onto complex geometry or measuring clearance.
contexts.surface_normal_extraction: Use N output to get the surface normal at the closest location — helpful for orienting objects or evaluating surface direction at arbitrary points.
contexts.distance_filtering: Connect D output to a threshold comparison to filter or cull points based on proximity to a Brep, e.g., selecting points within a certain range of a solid.

4beead95-8aa2-4613-8bb9-24758a0f5c4c.errors: Null output if Brep (B) is invalid or unset. Open Breps return closest point on nearest face/edge; closed Brep required for inside/outside tests (use Point In Breps instead). Multiple points require list matching with Brep input.

6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.name: Evaluate Length
6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.quick: Evaluates curve at a length distance; N toggles normalized (0-1) vs. actual curve units | outputs point, tangent vector, and curve parameter t
6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.description: Evaluate a curve at a certain factor along its length. Length factors can be supplied both in curve units and normalized units. Change the [N] parameter to toggle between the two modes.

contexts.point_along_curve: Wire Curve to C, supply a distance number to L. Set N=True for normalized 0-1 fractions, N=False for actual length units. Outputs point P and tangent T at that location.
contexts.divide_by_length: Combine with Division component to compute fractional positions (e.g., L/4 for quarter-points). Use N=False with explicit length values derived from Curve Length component.
contexts.feed_downstream_frames: Output parameter t feeds directly into Perp Frame or Evaluate Curve for consistent frame/tangent calculations at the same curve location.

6b021f56-b194-4210-b9a1-6cef3b7d0848.errors: Fails if L exceeds curve length when N=False (out-of-domain). N=True expects 0–1 range; values outside cause null output. Null curve input returns no geometry.

86b28a7e-94d9-4791-8306-e13e10d5f8d5.name: Area
86b28a7e-94d9-4791-8306-e13e10d5f8d5.quick: Returns area (A) and centroid point (C) for breps, meshes, or planar closed curves | open or non-planar curves will fail
86b28a7e-94d9-4791-8306-e13e10d5f8d5.description: Solve area properties for breps, meshes and planar closed curves.

contexts.surface_area: Wire a Brep or Surface into G; outputs numeric area A and centroid Point C. Commonly used before Evaluate Surface or Brep Closest Point to validate geometry size.
contexts.curve_area: Wire a planar closed curve into G to get enclosed area and centroid. Curve must be closed and planar — open or 3D curves return null.
contexts.mesh_area: Wire a mesh into G; works on mesh faces collectively. Useful for comparing mesh vs. brep area to check mesh fidelity.
contexts.centroid_extraction: Use C output as a reference point for centering operations, labeling, or driving downstream transforms without needing a separate centroid component.

86b28a7e-94d9-4791-8306-e13e10d5f8d5.errors: Fails or returns null if geometry is open, non-planar curve, or invalid brep. Null G input causes solution error. Very small or degenerate geometry may return near-zero area.

7c0523e8-79c9-45a2-8777-cf0d46bc5432.name: Volume
7c0523e8-79c9-45a2-8777-cf0d46bc5432.quick: Computes volume and centroid of closed breps/meshes | geometry must be closed/watertight or returns null
7c0523e8-79c9-45a2-8777-cf0d46bc5432.description: Solve volume properties for closed breps and meshes.

contexts.volume_check: Wire closed Brep or mesh to G; V outputs numeric volume, C outputs centroid point. Use for mass calculations or sorting by size.
contexts.centroid_extraction: C output gives volumetric center of mass point — useful for placing objects, orienting, or driving transforms relative to solid geometry.
contexts.open_geometry_debug: If V returns null/zero, geometry is not closed. Use Brep Edges or Cap Holes upstream to diagnose and fix open edges before feeding to Volume.

7c0523e8-79c9-45a2-8777-cf0d46bc5432.errors: Fails (null output) if geometry is open/not watertight. Surfaces, open polysurfaces, or open meshes return no valid volume. Ensure brep is solid before use.

1addcc85-b04e-46e6-bd4a-6f6c93bf7efd.name: Brep Join
1addcc85-b04e-46e6-bd4a-6f6c93bf7efd.quick: Joins multiple Breps into one; outputs joined Brep and Boolean indicating if join was closed/successful
1addcc85-b04e-46e6-bd4a-6f6c93bf7efd.description: Join a number of Breps together

contexts.merging_surfaces: Feed list of Breps into B input; component attempts to merge adjacent faces into unified Brep. C output returns True if result is closed solid. Often followed by Cap Holes to close remaining openings.
contexts.solid_creation: Use after constructing individual surface patches to combine into single closed Brep. Check C (closed) boolean to verify watertight result before passing to downstream solid operations.
contexts.pre_fillet: Join surfaces before applying Fillet Edge — fillet requires a unified Brep with shared edges, not separate surfaces.

1addcc85-b04e-46e6-bd4a-6f6c93bf7efd.errors: Join fails silently (C=False) if surfaces have gaps or mismatched edges; non-manifold geometry or duplicate faces cause incomplete joins. Input must be Brep type — raw surfaces may need conversion first.

79aa7f47-397c-4d3f-9761-aaf421bb7f5f.name: Domain Box
79aa7f47-397c-4d3f-9761-aaf421bb7f5f.quick: Domain Box | Inputs: Base, X, Y → Box

575660b1-8c79-4b8d-9222-7ab4a6ddb359.name: Rectangle 2Pt
575660b1-8c79-4b8d-9222-7ab4a6ddb359.quick: Creates rectangle from base plane + two corner points; R input rounds corners, L output gives side lengths
575660b1-8c79-4b8d-9222-7ab4a6ddb359.description: Create a rectangle from a base plane and two points

contexts.basic_rectangle: Wire a Plane to P, two Points to A and B defining opposite corners; output R is the rectangle curve, L gives lengths of sides
contexts.rounded_corners: Connect a Number to R input to fillet rectangle corners by that radius; keep radius smaller than shortest half-side to avoid failure
contexts.extracting_dimensions: Use L output to retrieve side lengths for downstream area calculations or parametric constraints without extra measurement components

575660b1-8c79-4b8d-9222-7ab4a6ddb359.errors: Corner rounding R too large relative to rectangle size causes invalid geometry; mismatched plane orientation vs. points may produce unexpected rectangle alignment

71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.name: PolyLine
71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.quick: Connects ordered points into a polyline curve | C (Boolean) closes the polyline back to start
71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.description: Create a polyline connecting a number of points.

contexts.open_polyline: Feed a list of Point3d into V, set C=False; outputs open Curve usable in downstream curve ops or extrusion
contexts.closed_polyline: Set C=True to close the polyline; last point connects back to first, producing a closed Curve suitable for boundary or loft operations
contexts.chaining_with_connect_curves: Output Pl can feed into Connect Curves to join with other curve segments into a continuous path

71b5b089-500a-4ea6-81c5-2f960441a0e8.errors: Fewer than 2 points in V produces no valid curve; unordered points create self-intersecting polyline; non-Point input to V causes type mismatch

9c85271f-89fa-4e9f-9f4a-d75802120ccc.name: Division
9c85271f-89fa-4e9f-9f4a-d75802120ccc.quick: Divides A by B (A÷B) | Division by zero returns null/error

contexts.scalar_division: Connect number outputs to A and B; R returns quotient. Commonly chained with Multiplication for ratio calculations.
contexts.list_operations: A and B can be lists; Grasshopper matches items per standard data matching (longest list/cross-reference). Useful for normalizing values.
contexts.curve_workflow: Often used alongside Divide Curve or Evaluate Length to compute fractional parameters or segment counts before passing to curve components.

9c85271f-89fa-4e9f-9f4a-d75802120ccc.errors: Division by zero (B=0) causes null or error output. Non-numeric Generic Data inputs will fail; ensure upstream data resolves to numbers.

4139f3a3-cf93-4fc0-b5e0-18a3acd0b003.name: Surface Curvature
4139f3a3-cf93-4fc0-b5e0-18a3acd0b003.quick: Evaluates Gaussian (G) and Mean (M) curvature at a UV point on a surface; outputs frame plane F | UV must be in surface domain
4139f3a3-cf93-4fc0-b5e0-18a3acd0b003.description: Evaluate the surface curvature at a {uv} coordinate.

contexts.curvature_analysis: Wire surface to S, UV coordinate (Point) to uv — often sourced from Evaluate Surface or Surface Closest Point. Outputs Gaussian curvature G and Mean curvature M as numbers, plus local frame plane F for visualization or further analysis.
contexts.comparison_with_principal_curvature: Use alongside Principal Curvature component for full curvature characterization. Surface Curvature gives scalar G and M values; Principal Curvature gives directional min/max curvature values at same UV location.
contexts.inflection_detection: G=0 indicates parabolic regions; G<0 indicates saddle/anticlastic regions. Combine with Surface Inflection to locate zero-curvature curves across the surface.

4139f3a3-cf93-4fc0-b5e0-18a3acd0b003.errors: Fails if UV point is outside surface domain — remap or use Surface Closest Point first. Untrimmed surface required for reliable results near boundaries.

0e94542a-2e46-4793-9f98-2200b06b28f4.name: Curve Frames
0e94542a-2e46-4793-9f98-2200b06b28f4.quick: Generates N equally spaced frames (planes) along a curve | N controls count, not spacing distance
0e94542a-2e46-4793-9f98-2200b06b28f4.description: Generate a number of equally spaced curve frames.

contexts.array_along_curve: Wire a curve to C and integer count to N; outputs F (planes) and t (parameters). Use F to orient geometry instances along the curve path.
contexts.comparing_frame_types: Unlike Perp Frames (perpendicular to tangent) or Horizontal Frames (world-aligned), Curve Frames uses default GH frame orientation — check which frame type suits your geometry before choosing.
contexts.extracting_parameters: Output t gives normalized or curve parameters at each frame location; feed into other curve evaluation components like Evaluate Curve for further processing.

0e94542a-2e46-4793-9f98-2200b06b28f4.errors: N=0 or negative produces no output. Very short curves with large N may produce near-duplicate frames. Closed curves divide evenly but first/last frame may overlap.

62cc9684-6a39-422e-aefa-ed44643557b9.name: Extend Curve
62cc9684-6a39-422e-aefa-ed44643557b9.quick: Extends a curve by distance at start/end | T integer controls extension type (line, arc, smooth)
62cc9684-6a39-422e-aefa-ed44643557b9.description: Extend a curve by a specified distance.

contexts.extend_both_ends: Wire curve to C, set T for extension type (0=line,1=arc,2=smooth), L0 for start extension distance, L1 for end extension distance; outputs extended curve
contexts.extend_one_end: Set L0=0 to extend only end, or L1=0 to extend only start; useful for trimming/joining workflows with Offset or Project Curve neighbors
contexts.joining_gaps: Use after Flip Curve to ensure correct curve direction before extending; chain with Simplify Curve to clean result

62cc9684-6a39-422e-aefa-ed44643557b9.errors: Null output if C is not a valid curve; T out of valid integer range may cause no extension; L0/L1 negative values likely cause errors or no change

5cad70f9-5a53-4c5c-a782-54a479b4abe3.name: Gate Or
5cad70f9-5a53-4c5c-a782-54a479b4abe3.quick: Boolean OR gate: outputs True if A or B (or both) are True | both inputs must be Boolean

contexts.conditional_filtering: Wire two Boolean conditions (e.g., from comparison components) into A and B; R feeds Dispatch or Cull to filter geometry when either condition is met
contexts.logic_combination: Chain with Gate And/Gate Not to build compound logic; e.g., NOT(A OR B) = NOR, achievable by connecting R to Gate Not

5cad70f9-5a53-4c5c-a782-54a479b4abe3.errors: Non-Boolean inputs cause type errors; null/empty inputs return null. If inputs are lists, ensure matching lengths or single-item broadcasting to avoid mismatched results.
