contexts.form_finding: Use with other Kangaroo goals to constrain specific particles to a mesh boundary or guide surface while rest of network deforms freely

6c1c3018-487b-4573-afc5-3af263ae5808.errors: P output is Generic Data — must connect to Kangaroo solver Goals, not geometry components directly. Mesh must be valid/closed or point projection may fail. Strength=0 disables constraint.

6d36a97d-811f-423a-a4a1-35a7a7637697.name: Direction
6d36a97d-811f-423a-a4a1-35a7a7637697.quick: Kangaroo2 goal: aligns a line segment to a given vector direction; omit Direction to snap to nearest World XYZ axis | output D feeds Kangaroo solver
6d36a97d-811f-423a-a4a1-35a7a7637697.description: Align a line segment with a given vector, or if none supplied, the closest of the World XYZ vectors

contexts.axis_alignment: Connect Line from geometry, leave Direction unconnected to auto-snap to nearest X/Y/Z axis; Strength controls stiffness. Output D goes to Kangaroo solver Goals list.
contexts.custom_direction: Wire a specific Vector into Direction input to align line toward arbitrary direction. Combine with EqualLength or LengthSnap goals for constrained structural members.
contexts.physics_simulation: Used alongside DynamicWeight1d for load-bearing line elements that must maintain orientation. Strength value balances against competing goals in solver.

6d36a97d-811f-423a-a4a1-35a7a7637697.errors: No Direction vector and ambiguous line orientation may produce unexpected axis snapping. Strength of 0 disables goal effect. Output D must connect to Kangaroo solver, not standard GH components.

6e9f7437-714b-4140-99e8-0842de58f59c.name: CoCircular
6e9f7437-714b-4140-99e8-0842de58f59c.quick: Kangaroo2 goal: pulls a set of points to lie on a common circle | output C feeds KangarooSolver

contexts.circular_constraint: Wire a list of Point params into Points, set Strength (number) to control stiffness; output C connects to KangarooSolver Goals input alongside other co-goals like CoPlanar or CoLinear
contexts.combined_goals: Combine with CoPlanar to constrain points to a circle in a specific plane; all co-family goals output Generic Data consumed by the solver

6e9f7437-714b-4140-99e8-0842de58f59c.errors: Fewer than 3 points yields degenerate circle; non-Point input to Points causes type error; Strength of 0 disables constraint silently

70de1114-9a0d-49a1-a101-f2d26374e161.name: Unroll Brep
70de1114-9a0d-49a1-a101-f2d26374e161.quick: Unrolls a Brep/surface to flat 2D geometry; Join boolean controls whether faces merge into single output

contexts.fabrication_flattening: Connect a ruled or developable Brep to Brep input; set Join=True to get single unrolled piece. Works best with single-curvature surfaces; doubly-curved surfaces may fail or distort.
contexts.multi_face_unroll: Feed multi-face Brep; Join=False returns individual unrolled faces separately, useful for labeling or nesting each panel independently.
contexts.post_processing: Output is Generic Data — likely a Brep or curve; cast explicitly or connect to Brep param. Pair with Sort Duplicate Breps or curve tools for cleanup.

70de1114-9a0d-49a1-a101-f2d26374e161.errors: Doubly-curved (non-developable) Breps will fail or produce distorted results. Generic Data output may need explicit casting. Null output if Brep input is invalid.

72dadfdd-3be9-44e3-a352-9343f3d5d3b1.name: TangentialSmooth
72dadfdd-3be9-44e3-a352-9343f3d5d3b1.quick: Smooths mesh tangentially (in local tangent planes only) | Must be used with SoapFilm goal in Kangaroo solver
72dadfdd-3be9-44e3-a352-9343f3d5d3b1.description: Smooth a mesh only in the local tangent planes. Used in conjunction with SoapFilm

contexts.soap_film_smoothing: Wire mesh (M) and Strength number into TangentialSmooth, combine output P with SoapFilm goal outputs into Kangaroo solver. Prevents mesh bunching while maintaining surface shape.
contexts.mesh_relaxation: Pair with Smooth component for combined tangential + normal smoothing. TangentialSmooth preserves surface curvature direction; Strength controls influence per iteration.

72dadfdd-3be9-44e3-a352-9343f3d5d3b1.errors: Fails if M is not a valid mesh. Without SoapFilm in same solver, smoothing may produce unexpected drift. Strength=0 has no effect; very high Strength can cause instability.

74953dd1-9af7-4736-983c-f258302de692.name: SplitAtCorners
74953dd1-9af7-4736-983c-f258302de692.quick: Splits a polyline into segments at corners exceeding angle threshold A (radians/degrees) | outputs corner Points C and split Curves S
74953dd1-9af7-4736-983c-f258302de692.description: Break a polyline into multiple parts based on angle

contexts.mesh_prep: Feed polyline boundary curves into P, set angle threshold A to detect sharp corners; output S gives individual straight or near-straight segments for Kangaroo simulation edges
contexts.corner_detection: Use output C (corner points) to identify vertices where angle exceeds A; wire into removeDuplicatePts to clean coincident corner points before further processing
contexts.polyline_segmentation: Chain with interconnectPoints or other Kangaroo2 utility components; S outputs multiple curve segments suitable for goal assignment in physics simulations

74953dd1-9af7-4736-983c-f258302de692.errors: Fails or returns no splits if P is not a polyline (smooth NURBS curves have no corners); A threshold units unclear — wrong value yields no splits (too large) or over-splits (too small); null output if curve is invalid

75245842-a7ba-497b-83df-2fc9aa2e8c54.name: Mesh Extrude
75245842-a7ba-497b-83df-2fc9aa2e8c54.quick: Extrudes mesh along a vector; toggle Solid? for closed extrusion, Both Sides? for bidirectional | Dir must be a Vector not a line
75245842-a7ba-497b-83df-2fc9aa2e8c54.description: Extrudes a mesh object along a specified vector.

contexts.solid_extrusion: Connect Mesh + Vector (e.g., Unit Z scaled by distance); set Solid?=True to cap ends, producing a closed mesh volume. Both Sides?=False for one-directional.
contexts.open_shell_extrusion: Set Solid?=False to produce only side faces without caps — useful for thin wall geometry or further mesh operations with Mesh Edges or Mesh Offset.
contexts.bidirectional_extrusion: Set Both Sides?=True to extrude symmetrically in both directions along Dir vector; halve the vector magnitude to control total extent.

75245842-a7ba-497b-83df-2fc9aa2e8c54.errors: Wrong input type: Dir expects Vector, not Curve or Point — causes null output. Zero-length vector produces no extrusion. Non-manifold input mesh may produce invalid solid output.

7539614d-dee1-44b4-a781-95accee71c8c.name: Reverse Surface Direction
7539614d-dee1-44b4-a781-95accee71c8c.quick: Flips UV directions of a surface | R integer controls which direction(s) to reverse (U, V, or both)
7539614d-dee1-44b4-a781-95accee71c8c.description: Reverse the UV directions of a surface.

contexts.fixing_surface_normals: Connect a surface to Srf; set R integer (0=none,1=U,2=V,3=both) to flip UV orientation before paneling or unrolling workflows
contexts.pre_unroll_prep: Feed into Unroll Brep after reversing UV to ensure consistent seam/direction alignment on developable surfaces

7539614d-dee1-44b4-a781-95accee71c8c.errors: Wrong R value (out of expected 0-3 range) may produce unexpected orientation; non-surface geometry input to Srf will fail; output is Generic Data, so explicit casting may be needed downstream

761c4e3d-141b-9770-6525-2303925136c3.name: Weaverbird's Mesh Thicken
761c4e3d-141b-9770-6525-2303925136c3.quick: Thickens an open mesh into a closed solid by offsetting; mesh must be orientable and offsettable | D controls thickness, T sets offset type
761c4e3d-141b-9770-6525-2303925136c3.description:
Computes a new mesh that is a closed solid, provided that the original mesh is offsettable and oriented.

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.shell_to_solid: Feed a single-surface mesh (M) from Weaverbird subdivision or mesh ops, set D (number) for wall thickness, choose T (OffsetTypeEnum: e.g., vertex normals or face normals) to get a closed solid output mesh
contexts.post_subdivision: Typically placed after Weaverbird subdivision components; thickens the refined mesh before export or rendering to give physical wall thickness
contexts.fabrication_prep: Used before mesh export for 3D printing — converts open mesh shells into printable closed solids; pair with mesh repair tools if mesh has holes or non-manifold edges

761c4e3d-141b-9770-6525-2303925136c3.errors: Fails if mesh is not orientable (non-manifold, flipped normals, or open/holey mesh); zero or negative D produces degenerate geometry; wrong OffsetTypeEnum may cause self-intersecting output on curved surfaces

763c5b56-3dc6-4fe0-be7b-6b60cd27f744.name: SolidPointCollide
763c5b56-3dc6-4fe0-be7b-6b60cd27f744.quick: Keep points outside or inside a closed mesh solid | Mesh must be closed; 'In' boolean toggles containment direction
763c5b56-3dc6-4fe0-be7b-6b60cd27f744.description: Keep a set of points outside or inside a given Mesh

contexts.collision_exclusion: Wire particle points to Points, closed mesh to Solid, In=False to push points outside. Output S feeds Kangaroo solver as goal object alongside other goals.
contexts.containment: Set In=True to keep points inside the mesh volume. Useful for constraining particles within a container mesh. Strength controls goal weight in solver.
contexts.unidirectional_mode: Uni=True makes constraint one-directional (only pushes, doesn't pull), useful when points start outside and should stay outside without attraction.

763c5b56-3dc6-4fe0-be7b-6b60cd27f744.errors: Fails or misbehaves if Mesh is open/non-manifold — solid collision requires watertight mesh. Null points or mismatched list lengths may cause silent goal failures in solver.

76469b0a-11f0-4b8e-ad65-31a555d4cddd.name: PlasticAnchor
76469b0a-11f0-4b8e-ad65-31a555d4cddd.quick: Plastic anchor goal for Kangaroo2: point P anchored with plastic (permanent deformation) behavior; L=rest length, Strength=stiffness, R=reset

contexts.plastic_deformation_simulation: Wire P to a mesh/point, set L (threshold length) and Strength (stiffness number). R (Boolean) resets plastic state. Output A feeds Kangaroo solver goals list.
contexts.comparison_with_anchor: Unlike rigid Anchor, PlasticAnchor allows permanent deformation once force threshold exceeded — useful for simulating material yielding or irreversible shape change.

76469b0a-11f0-4b8e-ad65-31a555d4cddd.errors: R must toggle (not hold True) to reset properly. L=0 may cause no plastic behavior. Output A must connect to Kangaroo solver goals; wrong type input on P (non-point) will fail.

76ab889c-8593-4892-861d-a80b5311a981.name: SoapFilm
76ab889c-8593-4892-861d-a80b5311a981.quick: Creates zero mean curvature (minimal surface) mesh goal for Kangaroo2 solver | output S feeds solver, not a mesh directly
76ab889c-8593-4892-861d-a80b5311a981.description: For generating zero mean curvature meshes

contexts.minimal_surface: Connect a starting mesh to M, set Strength (e.g. 1.0), wire S into Kangaroo2 solver Goals list alongside boundary anchor goals to hold edges fixed while interior relaxes to soap-film shape
contexts.combined_with_smooth: Pair with Smooth goal on same mesh for additional fairness; both feed solver Goals — SoapFilm drives area minimization, Smooth reduces local roughness

76ab889c-8593-4892-861d-a80b5311a981.errors: No mesh output until solver runs — S is a goal object, not geometry. Mesh with no fixed boundary anchors will collapse. Non-manifold or open meshes may produce unstable results.

76b38cca-507d-409e-a773-044b2577d0b4.name: RigidBody
76b38cca-507d-409e-a773-044b2577d0b4.quick: Creates a rigid body goal for Kangaroo2 6DOF simulation from a Brep part, reference plane, anchor points, and strength.

contexts.6dof_physics_simulation: Connect a Brep to Part, a reference Plane defining body orientation, Points for constraint anchors, and Strength as a number. Output RB feeds into Kangaroo2 solver alongside collision goals like SolidPlaneCollide.
contexts.rigid_assembly: Used with RigidPointSet when multiple bodies must maintain relative positions. Wire RB output into solver's Goals list with other constraints for multi-body rigid simulation.

76b38cca-507d-409e-a773-044b2577d0b4.errors: Null output if Part (Brep) is invalid or Plane is unset. Strength of 0 disables goal effect. Points must be on or near the body geometry for meaningful constraints.

77e9376b-a397-4010-9b2c-dd0326107a91.name: Diagonalize
77e9376b-a397-4010-9b2c-dd0326107a91.quick: Replaces each mesh edge with a new triangular/quad face, increasing mesh density | Input must be a valid mesh
77e9376b-a397-4010-9b2c-dd0326107a91.description: Replace each edge with a new face

contexts.mesh_subdivision: Feed a base mesh into M; outputs a denser mesh where each edge becomes a face. Often used before Kangaroo2 simulation to create diagonal bracing topology. Pair with Combine&Clean to remove duplicate vertices.
contexts.structural_pattern: Use after MeshDirection to ensure consistent face normals before diagonalizing. Result mesh has more faces than input — useful for creating diagonal structural patterns from simple quad meshes.

77e9376b-a397-4010-9b2c-dd0326107a91.errors: <~30 tokens: Null or invalid mesh input returns no output. Non-manifold or open meshes may produce unexpected topology.

780a08f2-c42d-4b8e-b8c9-8b3e09c318d0.name: FloorFriction
780a08f2-c42d-4b8e-b8c9-8b3e09c318d0.quick: FloorFriction | Inputs: P, L, S → F

78ab7d1a-51c8-43a8-b17a-fe42d699f938.name: Create DataTable
78ab7d1a-51c8-43a8-b17a-fe42d699f938.quick: Assembles a named DataTable from header and value text inputs | Headers and Values must align in count/structure

contexts.building_dataset: Wire Name (text), Headers (text list for column names), Values (text data rows) → DataTable output feeds into Create DataSet or Write XML File for structured data export
contexts.csv_or_grid_export: DataTable output connects to Create Data Grid for visual inspection or Create CSV for flat-file export; ensure Values match header column count per row
contexts.xml_json_pipeline: DataTable → Create DataSet → Write XML File → Convert XML to JSON for full data transformation pipeline within LunchBox data family

78ab7d1a-51c8-43a8-b17a-fe42d699f938.errors: Mismatched Headers vs. Values column count likely causes malformed or null DataTable; all inputs expect Text type — passing non-text geometry or numbers without conversion may fail

797e3a90-16e6-4cfc-9a0b-d0d494d9d598.name: Staggered Quad Panels
797e3a90-16e6-4cfc-9a0b-d0d494d9d598.quick: Divides surface into staggered (offset-row) quad panels | U/V control column/row count
797e3a90-16e6-4cfc-9a0b-d0d494d9d598.description: Creates staggered quad panels on a surface.

contexts.facade_panelization: Connect NURBS surface to Srf, integer sliders to U and V for column/row counts; outputs panel surfaces/polylines for fabrication or further geometry ops
contexts.pattern_variation: Use alongside Diamond Panels or Triangle Panels to compare panel layouts on same surface; swap Srf input to test different base surfaces

797e3a90-16e6-4cfc-9a0b-d0d494d9d598.errors: <~30 tokens: Non-surface input to Srf fails; U/V of 0 or negative produces no panels; very high U/V values may cause performance issues

7cf46619-66b8-4313-a493-edd54e7133b9.name: Diamond Grid
7cf46619-66b8-4313-a493-edd54e7133b9.quick: Generates diamond-shaped corner point grid on a surface | U/V integers control grid density
7cf46619-66b8-4313-a493-edd54e7133b9.description: Creates a diamond corner point grid on a surface.

contexts.panel_layout: Connect a NURBS surface to Srf, set U/V integer counts for grid density; outputs C1-C4 are corner points per diamond cell, MPt is midpoint, N is normal — wire corners to surface paneling or custom geometry construction
contexts.facade_paneling: Used alongside Diamond Panels, Hexagon Cells, Staggered Quad Panels for comparative panel layouts; C1-C4 corner points feed directly into panel geometry or structural framing components
contexts.point_extraction: MPt (midpoint) and N (normal) outputs useful for placing mullions, labels, or orienting geometry at each diamond cell center

7cf46619-66b8-4313-a493-edd54e7133b9.errors: Null output if Srf is unset or invalid; non-positive U/V integers cause grid failure; untrimmed surfaces recommended — trimmed surfaces may produce incomplete edge cells

7db2c4c9-15b5-4378-8495-a8f9a8db5723.name: DynamicWeight1d
7db2c4c9-15b5-4378-8495-a8f9a8db5723.quick: Applies a -Z load scaled by line length (dynamic weight) | W is weight per unit length; Line must be a line/curve segment
7db2c4c9-15b5-4378-8495-a8f9a8db5723.description: A load in the negative Z direction, which updates its magnitude according to the length of the line

contexts.hanging_structures: Feed structural members as Line inputs with W as mass-per-length; DW output connects to Kangaroo2 solver goals list for gravity simulation on cables or beams
contexts.form_finding: Use alongside EqualLength or LengthSnap goals; DW plugs into solver's Goals input to simulate self-weight that updates as geometry deforms during solving

7db2c4c9-15b5-4378-8495-a8f9a8db5723.errors: Null output if Line input is not a valid curve/line; W=0 produces zero load (no effect); non-line curves may cause unexpected length calculations

7e077f48-9ae8-4ef5-bb4b-77ab75106a2d.name: Text Reader
7e077f48-9ae8-4ef5-bb4b-77ab75106a2d.quick: Reads text file from disk into Grasshopper | Boolean toggle triggers read; Path must be valid file path string
7e077f48-9ae8-4ef5-bb4b-77ab75106a2d.description: Read a text stream to a file.

contexts.reading_text_file: Connect a file path string to Path, set Read to True with a Boolean Toggle; outputs text content as Generic Data, typically fed into panel or string processing components
contexts.paired_with_text_writer: Used alongside Text Writer to round-trip data: Text Writer saves, Text Reader reloads; Read toggle controls when file is read to avoid constant polling
contexts.data_pipeline: Useful for importing external data (CSV, config files) into Grasshopper; output Generic Data may need casting to string for downstream processing

7e077f48-9ae8-4ef5-bb4b-77ab75106a2d.errors: Read=False outputs nothing; invalid or nonexistent Path causes null/empty output; no automatic refresh — must toggle Read to re-read updated files

8083a51c-2e58-4f1b-af42-a5c6d22eb6a5.name: Brep Join Progression
8083a51c-2e58-4f1b-af42-a5c6d22eb6a5.quick: Progressively joins Brep faces in input order using tolerance; outputs intermediate join states at each step.
8083a51c-2e58-4f1b-af42-a5c6d22eb6a5.description: Progressively join Brep faces with a tolerance value. Faces are progressively joined together in the order they are supplied.

contexts.step_by_step_join: Feed ordered list of Brep faces; set tol to match document tolerance; compact=True collapses redundant intermediate results. Outputs Generic Data list showing cumulative join at each addition.
contexts.debugging_join_failures: Supply faces one by one to identify which face breaks the join sequence; compare intermediate Brep outputs to isolate problematic geometry.
contexts.incremental_assembly: Use alongside Sort Duplicate Breps to pre-sort faces before progressive joining, ensuring consistent join order and avoiding topology conflicts.

8083a51c-2e58-4f1b-af42-a5c6d22eb6a5.errors: Fails or produces open Breps if tolerance is too tight or faces have gaps exceeding tol; wrong input order causes incomplete joins; non-manifold or duplicate faces (check Sort Duplicate Breps) cause join failures.

81cc6201-6cda-4954-8503-66be5363aac8.name: SolidPlaneCollide
81cc6201-6cda-4954-8503-66be5363aac8.quick: Collision goal between a mesh solid and a plane in Kangaroo2 6DOF simulation | outputs goal object (SP) for solver
81cc6201-6cda-4954-8503-66be5363aac8.description: Collision between a plane and a solid

contexts.rigid_body_floor_collision: Wire mesh as Solid, attach SolidPlane (local plane of rigid body), set CollisionPlane as world ground/wall plane, connect Strength; feed SP into Kangaroo solver alongside RigidBody goals
contexts.6dof_physics_simulation: Used with RigidBody and Support goals to prevent solid objects from passing through boundary planes; SolidPlane must match the rigid body's reference plane

81cc6201-6cda-4954-8503-66be5363aac8.errors: Null output if Solid is not a closed mesh or planes are unset; mismatched SolidPlane (not aligned to rigid body frame) causes incorrect collision response; Strength=0 disables constraint

856bd786-9f29-4052-b721-0d64b7b3f3ea.name: Developablize
856bd786-9f29-4052-b721-0d64b7b3f3ea.quick: Converts triangular mesh into developable patches with creases (Kangaroo2 goal) | Strength controls optimization intensity
856bd786-9f29-4052-b721-0d64b7b3f3ea.description: Turn a triangular mesh into developable patches with creases. Based on the paper 'Developability of Triangle Meshes' by Stein, Grinspun & Crane

contexts.fabrication_flattening: Wire M (triangulated mesh) and Strength (number ~1-100) into Kangaroo2 solver as goal output D; use when preparing meshes for flat-sheet fabrication like metal or paper
contexts.kangaroo_solver_setup: Output D feeds directly into Kangaroo2 solver Goals input alongside other mesh goals; combine with boundary anchors to preserve shape while developablizing

856bd786-9f29-4052-b721-0d64b7b3f3ea.errors: Fails or produces poor results if mesh is not triangulated (quad/ngon meshes unsupported); very low Strength may not converge; highly curved input meshes may produce many sharp creases

8582bf30-b78b-4d21-b4cf-f744a84af497.name: Diamond Panels
8582bf30-b78b-4d21-b4cf-f744a84af497.quick: Creates diamond + triangle panels on a surface | U/V integers control panel count in each direction
8582bf30-b78b-4d21-b4cf-f744a84af497.description: Creates diamond panels on a surface.

contexts.facade_paneling: Connect NURBS surface to Srf, set U/V integer counts for panel density; outputs Diamonds and Triangles as separate panel geometry lists for independent material/fabrication workflows
contexts.parametric_pattern: Pair with Diamond Grid neighbor to align corner points; Diamonds output gives main panels, Triangles fills edge gaps — both outputs needed for complete surface coverage
contexts.panel_count_tuning: U and V are integers; increasing either multiplies panel count in that direction. Non-uniform U/V ratios produce elongated diamonds matching surface domain proportions

8582bf30-b78b-4d21-b4cf-f744a84af497.errors: <~30 tokens: Surface must be valid NURBS; U/V must be positive integers ≥1 or component produces no output; untrimmed surfaces work best — trimmed surfaces may yield incomplete edge panels

86cee9bc-ba05-49ff-ad55-895ae66cc978.name: SoftBodyCollide
86cee9bc-ba05-49ff-ad55-895ae66cc978.quick: Collision goal between deformable meshes in Kangaroo2 | Meshes must be a collection; outputs goal object for solver
86cee9bc-ba05-49ff-ad55-895ae66cc978.description: Collisions between a collection of deformable meshes

contexts.soft_body_simulation: Feed a list of meshes into Meshes input; set Strength (number) to control collision stiffness; wire SB output into Kangaroo solver Goals list alongside other goals
contexts.multi_mesh_interaction: Use when multiple deformable mesh bodies need to avoid interpenetration; combine with other soft body goals (e.g., spring, anchor) for full simulation setup

86cee9bc-ba05-49ff-ad55-895ae66cc978.errors: Fails if Meshes input is not a valid mesh collection or is null; very low Strength may allow interpenetration; SB output must connect to a Kangaroo solver — it is not geometry directly

87c0cc0e-d792-481e-b219-cc16b3e7b7b9.name: SimpleRemesh
87c0cc0e-d792-481e-b219-cc16b3e7b7b9.quick: Isotropically remesh a Brep or Mesh to uniform edge Length | Length controls target edge size; Steps controls iteration count
87c0cc0e-d792-481e-b219-cc16b3e7b7b9.description: Isotropically remesh a Brep or Mesh

contexts.basic_remesh: Connect a Brep or Mesh to Geometry, set Length (target edge length as number), set Steps (integer iterations, e.g. 10-50). Outputs uniform triangle mesh M.
contexts.feature_preservation: Use Creases (curves) to preserve sharp edges and Corners (points) to lock vertices during remeshing. Wire feature curves from BRep edges to Creases input.
contexts.simulation_prep: Feed output M into Kangaroo2 solver or physics simulation. Uniform mesh improves simulation stability compared to raw BRep tessellation.

87c0cc0e-d792-481e-b219-cc16b3e7b7b9.errors: Null output if Geometry is invalid or Length is too large/small relative to geometry size. No output if Steps=0. Creases must lie on geometry surface or they are ignored.

888d89c6-8580-4f8e-96ea-41225c33e883.name: Convert XML to JSON
888d89c6-8580-4f8e-96ea-41225c33e883.quick: Converts XML string to JSON output | Input must be valid XML text string
888d89c6-8580-4f8e-96ea-41225c33e883.description: Converts a XML string to JSON

contexts.xml_to_json_pipeline: Wire XML text (from file read or Write XML File output) into XML input; outputs Generic Data JSON string, usable with Create JSON or downstream JSON parsers
contexts.data_format_bridging: Use when workflow receives XML data but downstream components (Create DataTable, Create Data Grid) expect JSON format; acts as format bridge in lunchbox_data pipelines

888d89c6-8580-4f8e-96ea-41225c33e883.errors: Fails if XML input is malformed, empty, or not a valid XML string; Generic Data output may need casting before use in typed inputs

894ce9f3-45c4-41b4-9301-501bef0a84fa.name: Create CSV
894ce9f3-45c4-41b4-9301-501bef0a84fa.quick: Assembles a CSV string from headers and values; Delimit sets separator, Quotes wraps fields in quotes

contexts.export_tabular_data: Wire header row as Text list to Headers, data rows as Text to Values; set Delimit to ',' or ';'; enable Quotes (True) when fields may contain the delimiter character
contexts.feed_to_file_writer: Output CSV string connects to file-write components or Create Data Grid for saving; pairs naturally with Read CSV for round-trip workflows
contexts.custom_delimiter: Set Delimit to tab or semicolon for TSV or regional CSV formats; Headers and Values must be flat or properly structured Text lists

894ce9f3-45c4-41b4-9301-501bef0a84fa.errors: Mismatched header count vs. value columns produces malformed rows; null/empty Values input yields headers-only output; wrong Delimit type (non-Text) causes input rejection

8aa5774d-422a-433b-9a3f-667946bde157.name: RigidPointSet
8aa5774d-422a-433b-9a3f-667946bde157.quick: Locks a set of points into a rigid body maintaining relative positions | Plane defines local reference frame; Strength controls rigidity
8aa5774d-422a-433b-9a3f-667946bde157.description: A set of points which maintain their relative positions

contexts.rigid_body_simulation: Feed a list of Points and a reference Plane; output RB connects to Kangaroo solver as a 6DOF rigid body goal. Higher Strength enforces shape more strictly.
contexts.multi_body_assembly: Use alongside RigidBody goals; P output gives updated plane each solver iteration, useful for tracking orientation of the rigid set during simulation.

8aa5774d-422a-433b-9a3f-667946bde157.errors: Empty or single-point list produces degenerate rigid body. Mismatched Plane orientation relative to point cloud causes unexpected rotation. Strength=0 disables constraint entirely.

8abedb3c-ff82-46ea-8f77-fcb236b55d89.name: G2
8abedb3c-ff82-46ea-8f77-fcb236b55d89.quick: Maintains G2 curvature continuity between 2 NURBS curves | requires ordered Points input and Strength number
8abedb3c-ff82-46ea-8f77-fcb236b55d89.description: Maintain curvature continuity between 2 nurbs curves

contexts.smooth_curve_joining: Feed control points from two NURBS curves into Points (ordered at junction), set Strength; output G2 goal feeds into Kangaroo solver alongside other goals like Rod for structural continuity
contexts.kangaroo_simulation: G2 goal output connects to Kangaroo2 solver Goals input; combine with position/anchor goals to enforce curvature continuity while allowing dynamic relaxation

8abedb3c-ff82-46ea-8f77-fcb236b55d89.errors: Wrong point ordering at curve junction breaks continuity intent; too-low Strength causes goal to be overridden by competing goals; non-NURBS curve control points may produce unexpected curvature behavior

8b4dbe32-0c6c-4304-972e-3f60ed613114.name: OnCurve
8b4dbe32-0c6c-4304-972e-3f60ed613114.quick: Kangaroo2 goal: constrains point(s) to stay on a curve during simulation | Strength controls constraint stiffness
8b4dbe32-0c6c-4304-972e-3f60ed613114.description: Keep a point on a given Curve

contexts.curve_constraint_simulation: Wire particle Points, target Curve, and Strength (e.g. 1000 for rigid) into OnCurve; feed output P into Kangaroo solver goals list alongside other goals
contexts.soft_attraction: Use lower Strength values to softly attract points toward curve rather than hard-constrain; combine with other goals for flexible behavior

8b4dbe32-0c6c-4304-972e-3f60ed613114.errors: Output P is Generic Data — must feed into Kangaroo solver, not geometry components directly. Mismatched point/curve data trees may cause goal misalignment. Zero or null Strength disables constraint.

8bdb8e9f-f1dd-491d-ab9a-f80f1e170708.name: Shortest Walk
8bdb8e9f-f1dd-491d-ab9a-f80f1e170708.quick: Finds shortest path through a curve network | Crvs must form a connected network; Lengths input overrides default curve lengths as edge weights
8bdb8e9f-f1dd-491d-ab9a-f80f1e170708.description: Find the 'Shortest Walk' within a curve network. This node uses updated code originally authored by Giulio Piacentino of McNeel and Associates. https://www.food4rhino.com/en/app/shortest-walk-gh

contexts.path_finding: Connect a list of curves as Crvs, optionally provide Number weights via Lengths to bias routing; supply start/end as Lines in Paths; outputs Walk curves representing the shortest route
contexts.weighted_routing: Feed custom Number values to Lengths to weight edges differently from geometric length, enabling cost-based routing through the curve network

8bdb8e9f-f1dd-491d-ab9a-f80f1e170708.errors: Fails if curve network is disconnected (no valid path between endpoints); Paths lines must snap to curve endpoints or no walk is found; mismatched Lengths list length vs curve count causes incorrect weighting

8c27c7ea-f4ac-9c11-4478-164ea6cd1e0a.name: Weaverbird's Discover Covering and Retrim
8c27c7ea-f4ac-9c11-4478-164ea6cd1e0a.quick: Compares two curve groupings to find covered edges, then merges them | curves must be in same order
8c27c7ea-f4ac-9c11-4478-164ea6cd1e0a.description:
Compares two groupings of faces, and tells which edges became covered. Then, merges the covered edges.
Curves must be in the same order.

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.edge_covering_detection: Feed original edge curves (O) with tolerances (tO), replacement curves (R) with tolerances (tR), and trim curves (T); outputs merged/retrimed curves. Used after mesh edge extraction to detect which edges became covered by new faces.
contexts.mesh_subdivision_workflow: Typically used alongside Weaverbird's Mesh Edges to extract wireframe curves before and after subdivision, comparing original vs. new edge groupings to identify and merge covered edges.

8c27c7ea-f4ac-9c11-4478-164ea6cd1e0a.errors: Fails if O and R curve lists are not in matching order; tolerance inputs (tO, tR) must be valid numbers; mismatched list lengths likely cause null outputs.

8cb1880b-464e-470e-87af-ea27ae95132d.name: Bipartite
8cb1880b-464e-470e-87af-ea27ae95132d.quick: Tests if mesh is bipartite; assigns 0/1 integer per vertex so no adjacent vertices share same value | fails on odd-cycle (non-bipartite) meshes
8cb1880b-464e-470e-87af-ea27ae95132d.description: Attempt to assign a boolean to each vertex of a mesh such that no connected vertices share the same value

contexts.mesh_coloring: Feed a Mesh into M; output A gives integer (0 or 1) per vertex indicating partition group. Use with vertex color or weighting in Kangaroo simulations.
contexts.topology_check: Connect mesh from Kangaroo or Rhino; if mesh contains odd-length edge loops, bipartite assignment is impossible and result may be incomplete or invalid.

8cb1880b-464e-470e-87af-ea27ae95132d.errors: Non-bipartite meshes (containing triangles or odd-cycle polygons) cannot be two-colored; output A may be inconsistent or fail. Input must be a valid mesh with connectivity data.

8f083dbb-357b-4172-80d0-b584b21b6d75.name: NoFoldThrough
8f083dbb-357b-4172-80d0-b584b21b6d75.quick: Prevents hinge faces from folding through each other | requires 4 points defining hinge edge + both face tips
8f083dbb-357b-4172-80d0-b584b21b6d75.description: To stop the sides of a hinge passing through each other

contexts.mesh_folding_simulation: Wire FoldStart/FoldEnd as the shared hinge edge endpoints; Tip1/Tip2 are opposite vertices of the two adjacent mesh faces. Output H feeds into Kangaroo solver goals list. Strength controls collision resistance.
contexts.origami_or_crease_patterns: Use alongside other Kangaroo mesh goals to constrain fold angles; prevents self-intersection at fold lines during physics simulation.

8f083dbb-357b-4172-80d0-b584b21b6d75.errors: Fails if FoldStart/FoldEnd are coincident (degenerate hinge). Wrong Tip assignment (same side) makes constraint ineffective. Strength=0 disables goal.

8f78572b-7fd0-4795-b444-3de3ca5933ae.name: CoPlanar
8f78572b-7fd0-4795-b444-3de3ca5933ae.quick: Kangaroo2 goal: pulls a set of points toward a common plane | Strength controls force weight

contexts.form_finding: Connect a list of Points (e.g., mesh vertices or free points) and a Strength number to output goal C; feed C into Kangaroo2 Solver alongside other goals to enforce planarity during simulation
contexts.planar_panel_optimization: Use with CoLinear or CoCircular goals to enforce geometric rationalization constraints; higher Strength values dominate other competing goals in the solver

8f78572b-7fd0-4795-b444-3de3ca5933ae.errors: Fails silently if Points list is empty or contains fewer than 3 points (plane undefined); non-Point types cause type mismatch; Strength of 0 produces no effect

8f9f19c0-207a-419d-90f6-2fcadaa845f9.name: Solver
8f9f19c0-207a-419d-90f6-2fcadaa845f9.quick: Solver | Inputs: GoalObjects, Reset, Threshold, Tolerance → I, V, O
8f9f19c0-207a-419d-90f6-2fcadaa845f9.description: The main component where Goals are combined and applied

9103348d-9ec2-4937-a04f-79c509f8093c.name: Isothermic
9103348d-9ec2-4937-a04f-79c509f8093c.quick: Creates a Kangaroo2 goal to make a quad mesh S-Isothermic | outputs Generic goal object for Kangaroo solver
9103348d-9ec2-4937-a04f-79c509f8093c.description: Make a quad mesh S-Isothermic, as described in the paper 'Quasiisothermic Mesh Layout' by Sechelmann, Rörig & Bobenko

contexts.architectural_paneling: Feed a quad mesh (M) and Strength number into Isothermic goal; combine output G with other goals in Kangaroo solver to optimize mesh toward S-Isothermic property for planar/conical panel layouts
contexts.form_finding: Use alongside Wind or structural goals in Kangaroo2 solver; Strength controls how strongly the isothermic constraint is enforced relative to other goals

9103348d-9ec2-4937-a04f-79c509f8093c.errors: Fails or produces no effect if mesh is not quad-dominant; non-quad faces ignored or cause solver instability. Strength=0 disables goal. Output G must feed Kangaroo solver, not used directly.

919a9141-c43e-417c-3838-c1ad637291b9.name: Weaverbird's Naked boundary
919a9141-c43e-417c-3838-c1ad637291b9.quick: Extracts naked boundary polycurve from a mesh by joining singly-covered naked edges | Input must be mesh geometry
919a9141-c43e-417c-3838-c1ad637291b9.description:
Finds the naked, or singly covered, polycurve as the connection of multiple naked edges

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.boundary_extraction: Connect mesh (M) from subdivision or smoothing ops (e.g., Weaverbird Laplacian Smoothing); outputs closed or open polycurve (C) representing the mesh boundary/hole edges
contexts.open_mesh_analysis: Use after mesh operations that produce open meshes; C output can feed into curve-based operations like lofting or surface trimming to cap or analyze holes

919a9141-c43e-417c-3838-c1ad637291b9.errors: Fails or returns null if mesh has no naked edges (fully closed mesh); may return multiple curves if mesh has multiple boundary loops — component joins edges into polycurves but disconnected boundaries may not merge into one

928b2951-2a01-4b6b-8ccb-6fbeb3e490ad.name: Wind
928b2951-2a01-4b6b-8ccb-6fbeb3e490ad.quick: Applies wind force to a mesh in Kangaroo2 simulation | output is a goal object, must feed into solver

contexts.cloth_simulation: Connect mesh geometry to M, define wind direction/strength as Vector to W; output goal feeds into Kangaroo2 solver alongside other goals like gravity and anchors
contexts.aerodynamic_loading: Use Vector component scaled by wind speed for W input; combine with mesh from Mesh or surface-derived mesh; solver accumulates forces per face

928b2951-2a01-4b6b-8ccb-6fbeb3e490ad.errors: Output is Generic goal data — plugging directly into geometry components fails; mesh must be valid (non-null); zero-length wind vector produces no effect

93705de7-bc3e-414f-a201-824b40e828b8.name: Sort Duplicate Breps
93705de7-bc3e-414f-a201-824b40e828b8.quick: Filters duplicate Breps from a list, returning unique Breps and their original indices | outputs Generic Data, not typed Brep
93705de7-bc3e-414f-a201-824b40e828b8.description: Sort a list of Breps based on duplicates.

contexts.deduplication_before_processing: Feed a Brep list into Breps input; Unique output gives deduplicated Breps, Indices output gives their positions in original list. Useful before Brep Join Progression or Unroll Brep to avoid redundant operations.
contexts.geometry_cleanup: Use after collecting Breps from multiple sources to remove exact duplicates. Likely uses document tolerance similar to Sort Duplicate Curves neighbor. Cast Generic Data outputs to Brep as needed downstream.

93705de7-bc3e-414f-a201-824b40e828b8.errors: Outputs are Generic Data not Brep — downstream components expecting Brep type may need explicit cast. Non-Brep geometry input will fail. Duplicate detection likely tolerance-based; near-identical but non-exact Breps may not be caught.

93da261b-5255-4276-182c-c51385f197da.name: Weaverbird's Blur Mesh
93da261b-5255-4276-182c-c51385f197da.quick: Blurs mesh vertex positions and colors over L iterations with T strength; does not subdivide or add faces.
93da261b-5255-4276-182c-c51385f197da.description:
Calculates a smoothened representation of an original mesh, but only in respect to colors and vertex coordinated. Does not increase the face count.

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.vertex_position_smoothing: Connect a mesh to M, integer iteration count to L, and a 0–1 number to T for blend strength. Outputs smoothed mesh with same topology. Similar to Laplacian Smoothing but also affects vertex colors.
contexts.color_blending: When mesh has per-vertex colors, Blur Mesh averages colors across neighbors over L iterations. Wire colored mesh to M; T controls blend amount per pass.
contexts.lightweight_smoothing: Use instead of subdivision-based smoothers when face count must stay fixed. Pair with Weaverbird's Laplacian or LaplacianHC for comparison of smoothing styles.

93da261b-5255-4276-182c-c51385f197da.errors: Non-mesh geometry on M will fail. L must be a positive integer; zero or negative may produce no effect. T outside 0–1 range may cause over-smoothing or instability.

94bf912d-4d0c-4764-a100-5813a98a8b73.name: Collider
94bf912d-4d0c-4764-a100-5813a98a8b73.quick: Collision goal for Kangaroo2: keeps thickened line segments and spheres from overlapping | Objects must be lines or points; Radii sets thickness
94bf912d-4d0c-4764-a100-5813a98a8b73.description: Collisions between thickened line segments and spheres

contexts.rod_packing: Feed lines as Objects with per-element Radii to simulate thick rod collisions; wire into Kangaroo solver's Goals input alongside other goals
contexts.sphere_collision: Pass point/sphere objects with uniform Radius; IgnoreA/IgnoreB accept integer group indices to skip self-collision within groups
contexts.selective_collision: Use IgnoreA and IgnoreB integer lists to prevent collision between specific object pairs or groups, e.g. connected members in a network

94bf912d-4d0c-4764-a100-5813a98a8b73.errors: Fails if Objects are not line segments or sphere-compatible geometry; mismatched Radii list length causes unintended uniform radius; IgnoreA/IgnoreB must be integers — wrong type causes solver errors

97253642-cb05-43e6-bc79-4bd0306441e5.name: PlanarityAnalysis
97253642-cb05-43e6-bc79-4bd0306441e5.quick: Visualizes mesh face planarity as colored mesh | X sets tolerance/scale threshold for color mapping
97253642-cb05-43e6-bc79-4bd0306441e5.description: Display face planarity as a coloured mesh

contexts.planarity_check: Connect quad mesh to M; X controls color range threshold (number). Output M is colored mesh for display; P returns per-face planarity deviation values for further analysis or filtering.
contexts.optimization_feedback: Use P (planarity numbers) to drive Kangaroo goals or identify non-planar faces. Wire P to analysis components to find worst offenders before panelization.

97253642-cb05-43e6-bc79-4bd0306441e5.errors: Fails or gives no output if M is not a valid mesh or is null. Triangular meshes always return 0 planarity (trivially planar); meaningful results require quad or ngon faces. X=0 may cause division issues or flat color output.

9a4d18a1-87f0-428d-8c01-da8530f5fb7a.name: Platonic Octahedron
9a4d18a1-87f0-428d-8c01-da8530f5fb7a.quick: Generates a parametric octahedron mesh/geometry | Trunc controls truncation (0=pure octahedron, higher=truncated)
9a4d18a1-87f0-428d-8c01-da8530f5fb7a.description: Create a parametric octrahedron with a truncation parameter.

contexts.basic_octahedron: Connect a Plane (origin+orientation), a Number for Rad (size), and Trunc=0 for standard octahedron; output Plato is Generic Data, likely a mesh or brep requiring casting
contexts.truncated_octahedron: Vary Trunc (Number Slider) between 0 and some max to progressively truncate vertices; pair with Platonic Tetrahedron for comparative platonic solid studies
contexts.positioning: Feed a constructed Plane (e.g., from XY Plane + Move) to Pln to control location and orientation of the solid in 3D space

9a4d18a1-87f0-428d-8c01-da8530f5fb7a.errors: Output is Generic Data — may need explicit casting to Mesh or Brep for downstream ops. Invalid Trunc values (negative or out of range) may produce degenerate geometry. Null Plane input likely causes no output.

9b67d915-6dd7-4742-b85f-7826ab7f234e.name: Text Writer
9b67d915-6dd7-4742-b85f-7826ab7f234e.quick: Writes text to a file at given path | Write input must be True to trigger; nothing written if False
9b67d915-6dd7-4742-b85f-7826ab7f234e.description: Write a text stream to a file.

contexts.export_data: Connect a file path string to Path, list or single string to Text, and a Boolean toggle (True) to Write; fires on True to save text file to disk
contexts.conditional_write: Wire a button or logic-driven Boolean to Write so file is only written when explicitly triggered, preventing accidental overwrites on every recompute
contexts.pipeline_output: Pair with Text Reader neighbor to round-trip text data; use after processing/decrypting text to persist results

9b67d915-6dd7-4742-b85f-7826ab7f234e.errors: File not written if Write is False or null; invalid/non-existent directory in Path causes failure; Text input must resolve to string — geometry or non-text types will error

9c2695de-127b-4b46-a17b-f3a676891c0d.name: MeshDirection
9c2695de-127b-4b46-a17b-f3a676891c0d.quick: Sorts/unifies face normal directions of a mesh | ensures consistent winding order across all faces
9c2695de-127b-4b46-a17b-f3a676891c0d.description: Sort the face directions of a mesh

contexts.pre_simulation: Feed raw or combined mesh into M before Kangaroo2 physics; consistent normals prevent solver artifacts. Often follows Combine&Clean to fix merged mesh orientation.
contexts.normal_consistency: Use after boolean or imported meshes with mixed face winding. Input single mesh M, output is same mesh with sorted face directions for reliable normal computation.

9c2695de-127b-4b46-a17b-f3a676891c0d.errors: Fails or produces no change if input mesh is null or has no faces. Non-manifold meshes from Combine&Clean may still have ambiguous directions after sorting.

9c98e97a-819a-41bd-9af8-866353e28cb0.name: Weaverbird's Bevel Vertices
9c98e97a-819a-41bd-9af8-866353e28cb0.quick: Replaces each mesh vertex with a new face; requires mesh input M, offset distance D, and inset type T.
9c98e97a-819a-41bd-9af8-866353e28cb0.description:
Replaces each original mesh vertex with a new face, connecting all edges.

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.vertex_chamfering: Wire a Weaverbird-compatible mesh to M, a Number slider to D (controls bevel size), and InsetTypeEnum to T. Output O is the beveled mesh geometry, ready for further subdivision or thickening.
contexts.subdivision_prep: Use before Weaverbird's Mesh Thicken or subdivision components to add vertex faces, increasing mesh complexity and rounding sharp corners prior to solidifying.

9c98e97a-819a-41bd-9af8-866353e28cb0.errors: Fails if M receives non-mesh geometry. D values too large may cause self-intersecting faces. T must be valid InsetTypeEnum; wrong type causes null output.

9e8f42f8-8688-4718-a498-522d2263bf37.name: Read CSV
9e8f42f8-8688-4718-a498-522d2263bf37.quick: Parses CSV text string into Headers and Values; requires delimiter input (default comma)
9e8f42f8-8688-4718-a498-522d2263bf37.description: Read a CSV string. (Comma Separated Value)

contexts.data_import: Wire a file-read text output into CSV input; set Delimit to ',' or ';'. Outputs Headers (first row) and Values (remaining rows) as generic data lists.
contexts.paired_with_create_csv: Use alongside Create CSV for round-trip CSV workflows — Create CSV builds the string, Read CSV parses it back into structured headers and values.
contexts.custom_delimiter: For tab-separated or semicolon-separated files, change Delimit input accordingly; mismatched delimiter causes all data to appear in single columns.

9e8f42f8-8688-4718-a498-522d2263bf37.errors: Wrong delimiter causes unsplit rows. Non-text input to CSV param fails. Empty string input likely returns null Headers and Values.

9f055808-c262-4462-b429-7e20d4ca3a5e.name: remesher
9f055808-c262-4462-b429-7e20d4ca3a5e.quick: Iterative remeshing via Kangaroo2 | L sets target edge length; Reset restarts process

contexts.isotropic_remeshing: Feed Brep/Mesh into Geom, number into L for target edge length, integer into Iter for iteration count; toggle Reset Boolean to restart. Outputs remeshed mesh M.
contexts.constrained_remeshing: Use FixC (curves) and FixV (points) to lock boundary edges or feature vertices during remeshing. Pull controls attraction strength to original surface.
contexts.flip_control: Flip integer controls edge-flip behavior during remeshing iterations; adjust to improve triangle quality.

9f055808-c262-4462-b429-7e20d4ca3a5e.errors: Null output if Geom is not a valid mesh or Brep; L=0 or negative causes degenerate edges; high Iter without Reset may accumulate drift; FixC curves not on surface may be ignored or cause instability.

a16a3c53-7ae9-4bb0-a0c2-fcc67e0c432c.name: Hyperbolic Paraboloid
a16a3c53-7ae9-4bb0-a0c2-fcc67e0c432c.quick: Generates a hyperbolic paraboloid surface | U/V control subdivisions; a, b, S shape parameters; D1/D2 define UV domains

contexts.basic_surface_generation: Connect integer sliders to U and V for mesh resolution, number sliders to a, b (shape coefficients) and S (scale), wire Domain components to D1/D2 for UV range; outputs Generic Data surface usable with Lunchbox panels or standard GH surface ops
contexts.architectural_form: Typical saddle-roof or shell form; adjust a and b independently to control curvature asymmetry; D1/D2 domains shift or scale the parametric extent of the surface

a16a3c53-7ae9-4bb0-a0c2-fcc67e0c432c.errors: Output is Generic Data, not native Surface — may need casting for standard GH surface components. Zero or negative a/b values may produce degenerate geometry. U/V must be positive integers; zero causes no surface output.

a1b5310f-eb7d-4534-9ca1-c0acad970a28.name: Triangular Panels A
a1b5310f-eb7d-4534-9ca1-c0acad970a28.quick: Divides surface into triangular panels via U/V count; outputs panel geometry as Generic Data.
a1b5310f-eb7d-4534-9ca1-c0acad970a28.description: Creates triangular panels on a surface.

contexts.facade_panelization: Connect a NURBS surface to Srf, set U and V integers for grid density; outputs triangle panel geometry for fabrication or visualization. Pair with Brep components to process individual panels.
contexts.parametric_pattern: Use alongside Triangle Panels B or Diamond Panels to compare triangulation strategies on the same surface. U/V control panel count in each direction independently.

a1b5310f-eb7d-4534-9ca1-c0acad970a28.errors: Fails or produces no output if Srf is not a valid surface. Very high U/V values may cause performance issues. Generic Data output requires type casting to access panel geometry downstream.

a3586a96-8767-48df-87ff-bc336b24ae1b.name: Decrypt Text
a3586a96-8767-48df-87ff-bc336b24ae1b.quick: Decrypts encrypted text using a passphrase | both Text and Pass must match the original encryption

contexts.decrypt_encrypted_file: Wire Text Reader output into Text, provide matching passphrase to Pass; output feeds Deserialize Geometry or panel to recover original data
contexts.paired_with_encrypt: Used as counterpart to Encrypt Text (similar component); same passphrase required — mismatch yields garbled or null output

a3586a96-8767-48df-87ff-bc336b24ae1b.errors: Wrong or missing passphrase returns null/garbage output; non-encrypted text input likely fails silently or errors; output is Generic Data, may need casting

a3c33654-0db2-4aeb-8551-d7a48b763128.name: Mesh Reduce
a3c33654-0db2-4aeb-8551-d7a48b763128.quick: Reduces mesh polygon count to simplify geometry | Size (integer) controls target face count

contexts.mesh_simplification: Connect a mesh to Mesh input, set Size as integer target polygon count, toggle Dist (distribution method) and Normalize booleans; RedMsh outputs simplified mesh for downstream ops like Mesh Extrude
contexts.accuracy_control: Accuracy (number) controls how closely reduced mesh approximates original shape; lower values = faster but less faithful reduction

a3c33654-0db2-4aeb-8551-d7a48b763128.errors: RedMsh outputs Generic Data, not typed Mesh — may need casting downstream. Size=0 or negative likely causes failure. Dist/Normalize booleans may default to false if unconnected.

a412ddf4-4899-4456-8325-f3f9a8134a25.name: interconnectPoints
a412ddf4-4899-4456-8325-f3f9a8134a25.quick: Generates all pairwise lines between N points; output count = N*(N-1)/2 lines
a412ddf4-4899-4456-8325-f3f9a8134a25.description: Draws one line between every pair of points in a list

contexts.connectivity_mesh: Feed a list of points (P); outputs all pair-wise line connections as Curves. Useful for visualizing full connectivity graphs or spring networks before Kangaroo simulation.
contexts.preprocessing: Often paired with removeDuplicateLines to clean redundant edges, or removeDuplicatePts to ensure unique input points before generating connections.

a412ddf4-4899-4456-8325-f3f9a8134a25.errors: Large point lists cause combinatorial explosion (100 pts = 4950 lines). Non-point input to P will fail. Duplicate points produce overlapping zero-length lines.

a4c75331-c017-e23b-a212-27212c433356.name: Weaverbird's LaplacianHC Smoothing
a4c75331-c017-e23b-a212-27212c433356.quick: LaplacianHC smoothing on mesh; preserves volume better than basic Laplacian | requires mesh input M, iterations L
a4c75331-c017-e23b-a212-27212c433356.description:
Calculates a smoothened representation of an original mesh. Does not increase the face count. Allows volume enhancing specifications.

Provided by Weaverbird 0.9.0.1.

contexts.volume_preserving_smoothing: Connect mesh to M, integer iterations to L, NakedEdgeEnum to S for boundary handling; tune P (alpha), O (beta), A, T parameters to balance smoothness vs. volume preservation
contexts.comparison_with_laplacian: Use instead of Weaverbird's Laplacian Smoothing when volume shrinkage is a concern; HC variant uses back-projection to recover lost volume via P and O parameters
contexts.mesh_refinement_pipeline: Typically placed after subdivision (e.g., Catmull-Clark) and before Mesh Edges or Vertices extraction; does not increase face count

a4c75331-c017-e23b-a212-27212c433356.errors: Null output if M is not a valid mesh; wrong type on L (must be integer) causes failure; S expects NakedEdgeEnum — passing wrong boundary type may cause naked edge distortion

a5287477-4326-442f-8ab3-904779ec720d.name: RTree Closest Point
a5287477-4326-442f-8ab3-904779ec720d.quick: Queries an RTree structure to find closest point(s) and their indices | RTree input must come from an RTree-building component, not raw points
a5287477-4326-442f-8ab3-904779ec720d.description: Find the closest point in an RTree from search points

contexts.spatial_lookup: Wire search points (SPoints) from Point or Construct Point, wire RTree from a dedicated RTree-builder component; returns closest matching point (CPoint) and its list index (Index) for each search point
contexts.index_driven_workflow: Use output Index to retrieve associated data from original point list via List Item; enables fast nearest-neighbor lookups without brute-force distance comparison

global_gotchas.text: Create by name may return obsolete components. Always use GUID.
Many components share names (Sphere, Box, Integer). Check category or use GUID.
Sliders have no Params property. They act as simple output sources.
Three data types: single (1 path, 1 item), list (1 path, N items), tree (N paths). Use gh_inspect_output to check.
Graft adds branch level (list→tree). Flatten removes ALL branches (tree→list). Not perfect inverses.
